#2115. Chelsea make early move for Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Chelsea have reportedly made contact with Palmeiras as they attempt to gain an early advantage in the race to sign Brazilian teenager Eduardo Conceicao.

The 16-year-old forward has attracted attention from several leading European clubs, but Chelsea are understood to be among the first to establish direct contact with Palmeiras over a potential future transfer.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, the London club have held a series of discussions as they seek to position themselves ahead of their rivals.

Palmeiras are reportedly preparing for substantial offers, with some figures at the Brazilian club discussing a valuation as high as €100m (£85m).

That figure has not been established as a firm asking price, however, and Brus reports that industry sources expect the eventual cost to be lower. Chelsea’s previous investment of approximately £51m in Estevao is regarded as a possible benchmark.

Manchester City’s ownership group have also made contact regarding Conceicao, while Arsenal, Manchester United, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs reported to have watched him.

Chelsea’s existing relationship with Palmeiras could help their efforts, although the level of competition means there is no guarantee that their early interest will lead to a deal.

The player’s age is another consideration. Conceicao cannot complete an international transfer to England until he turns 18, leaving interested clubs facing a potentially lengthy wait before he can join their squads.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

No formal bid or agreement has been reported for Conceicao. Nevertheless, the latest claims suggest Chelsea are prepared to explore another long-term investment in Brazilian talent rather than wait until the player becomes available for an immediate move.

Arsenal are increasing their interest in Cruzeiro youngster Eduardo Pape.

Despite the fact he has yet to play for the senior side in Brazil, the 17-year-old has attracted interest from a number of clubs. It is understood that Arsenal is keeping an eye on the youngster. Newcastle United and Bayern Munich are also linked with the midfielder.

The move could be a good fit with the Gunners liking to identify young talent early on. However, Pape is still very much in the early stages of his career, and any move would be seen as an investment into his future.

Arsenal are reportedly targeting Pape as a potential signing in 2027. The teenager is valued at around £33m.

Pape has already had previous experience playing for Cruzeiro’s Under-20s. He’s played 32 times and scored three goals and three assists.

He has left a successful headline in junior football as well. Pape has netted six goals in eight matches and strives for a place in the Brazilian U17 World Cup squad.

The tournament gives an opportunity to demonstrate his skills. The scouts will closely monitor the tournament, so any team interested in the player will be able to see his progress.

Of course, not just Arsenal would want to sign him. Clubs like Newcastle and Bayern Munich have already expressed interest in securing him. This is likely to cause a competitive atmosphere.

There is a concern that there hasn’t been any senior-level play from Pape. As he has never played first-team football before. It will be difficult to see how he will adapt to playing in Europe.

The contract is until December 2029, meaning Cruzeiro are in a strong position. There isn’t a huge need for the Brazilian club to rush into any decisions, meaning Pape can get some experience in a comfortable environment before moving abroad.

It gives us an insight into what Pape could hope to achieve.

It shows that Arsenal are looking further ahead with their recruitment. Whether they make a move for him remains to be seen. Pape will be one to keep an eye on as we approach the 2027 transfer window.

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Alex Scott and Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao have both featured in Thursday’s transfer coverage, with Xabi Alonso also preparing his players for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

His departure is understood to be amicable and will not take immediate effect. Stewart joined from Monaco in 2022, initially as technical director, before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley.

As detailed in our report on Stewart’s departure and Chelsea’s leadership reshuffle, Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields are expected to take on expanded responsibilities across recruitment, player development and the wider BlueCo operation.

The changes follow discussions about the club’s sporting structure that reportedly began earlier this year. There is no confirmed suggestion that Stewart’s departure resulted from a disagreement with Alonso.

Chelsea’s reported interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott remains a talking point, despite the south coast club’s determination to retain the England international.

The Blues reportedly had a £64m offer rejected during the summer, with Matt Law of The Telegraph subsequently identifying Chelsea as leading contenders for the 23-year-old.

However, as examined in our latest report on Chelsea’s interest in Scott, Bournemouth are not expected to entertain a January sale.

Scott’s immediate concern is recovering from a thigh injury suffered while representing England. The midfielder could face several weeks on the sidelines, potentially complicating Bournemouth’s plans as well as any future discussions about his next move.

Chelsea have also reportedly made contact with Palmeiras over 16-year-old forward Eduardo Conceicao, who is attracting attention from several leading European clubs.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, Chelsea have held discussions with the Brazilian club as they explore the possibility of a future deal.

Our report on Chelsea’s interest in Eduardo Conceicao explains that a valuation as high as €100m has been suggested, although that figure is not a confirmed asking price or evidence of a formal bid.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Real Madrid are among the other clubs reportedly monitoring the teenager. Conceicao would be unable to complete a transfer to England until he turns 18, making any prospective move a longer-term consideration.

Alonso’s attention will now turn to Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

The match kicks off at 3pm and will not be televised live in the United Kingdom because of the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

After Saturday’s fixture, Chelsea travel to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton on 17 October. Alonso will be looking for greater consistency as the domestic programme resumes.

The forward was loaned to Lyon for the second half of last season to get more regular game time.

However, his representatives are said to be open to looking for another move if things do not improve in Madrid.

It seems Arsenal are interested in signing Endrick on loan with a view to making the move permanent. This will give them time to see how he settles into the Premier League.

However, Real Madrid may be in a strong position. They are still loyal to the young player and would prefer to keep him at the Spanish club.

Arsenal will rely on Madrid being more willing to let him go.

The reported interest from Arsenal comes as Arteta looks to strengthen his attacking options.

Endrick would provide variety to an attacking line-up which has been under pressure of late. His age and potential make a loan deal with an option to make the move permanent an attractive option.

There is also positivity from his previous stint with Lyon. He has already been on a loan move from Madrid and has demonstrated that he can make progress when getting regular game time.

Arsenal have previously signed young talents from Real Madrid.

Martin Odegaard came to north London as a young player after failing to make an impact in the first team at Madrid. He then became a key player for Arteta, taking on the role of captain.

Endrick will be hoping to follow a similar trajectory.

There is no suggestion that any deal is near despite Arsenal’s interest.

Endrick remains an important part of Real Madrid’s long-term plans. His representatives are thought to be looking at other options to help his career develop.

This loan deal would provide a solution for all parties. Arsenal would have another attacker to bring in, Endrick would play more regularly and Madrid would still have an interest in his future.

It will also depend on how willing the Spanish giants are to move their stance before January.

For now, Arsenal are in contact with Endrick as they consider a move. The Brazilian’s future may soon become a topic of interest ahead of the winter transfer window.

#2110. Arsenal news: Arteta’s side secure landmark victory at Anfield

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

In Arsenal news, Arsenal have finally found a way to win at Anfield again. Their latest victory owed as much to defensive discipline as Kai Havertz’s decisive goal.

The Gunners claimed a 1-0 Premier League victory against Liverpool, ending their 14-year wait for victory at the iconic stadium. Declan Rice set up their opener as Havertz put the visitors ahead on the 16th minute.

It was a tough afternoon for Mikel Arteta’s side as they were put under sustained pressure by their opponents. The Reds also created a number of dangerous chances throughout the match, especially in the first half.

Arsenal held their composure, and the backline was calm throughout. David Raya made the crucial interventions to keep the lead safe.

They are now three points ahead at the top of the Premier League after Manchester City lost to Brighton.

While the attack has been a key aspect of Arsenal’s title charge, they were put under pressure defensively at Anfield.

Liverpool came out aggressively after going behind. Virgil van Dijk caused problems from set pieces, and Florian Wirtz hit the crossbar from a free kick.

Raya was quick to block Van Dijk’s dangerous flick on and prevent Alexander Isak from capitalising. However, Alexis Mac Allister did head over the bar as Liverpool looked to level the game.

Arsenal were forced into another stretch as Jurrien Timber blocked well. William Saliba and Gabriel helped to limit Liverpool’s chances.

The stats tell the story of how well the visitors defended. Liverpool had 17 shots but couldn’t get one on target.

Liverpool were unable to create a shot on target for the first time in recorded history (since 2003-04) in a Premier League game at Anfield.

Meanwhile, it was the first time that Arsenal had kept a clean sheet in the Premier League at the ground since September 2012. The result was especially important following their Carabao Cup heartbreak against Fleetwood Town earlier in the week.

Whilst they have made a great defensive stand, Arsenal’s two most influential players in the final third made the difference.

Rice won the turnover, drove down the right and played a low cross into the six-yard box. Havertz made his run to the back post and finished to give Arsenal the early lead.

The goal also takes Havertz to 46 Premier League goals, making him the most prolific German in the competition and overtaking former Manchester City midfielder Ilkay Gündogan.

Rice had a huge influence on the game. His performance in the middle of the park helped Arsenal deal with the intensity of Liverpool, and he was named man of the match.

Christos Tzolis provided an important attacking outlet. His pace created chances to ease pressure on Arsenal. He forced an incredible save from Alisson with a late first-time effort.

The win was Arsenal’s first at Anfield in any competition since September 2012 and their 300th away win in the Premier League.

Arteta’s team have had a stellar start to the season, taking 24 points from nine games. They have also proved they are capable of getting results in tough circumstances.

They will now look ahead to their Champions League game on Wednesday against Slavia Prague and then back to domestic action against Hull City.

#2109. Nuno’s West Ham Future Under Threat As Board Concerns Grow

Nuno Espírito Santo’s position as West Ham United manager is under increasing threat, according to a new report from The Guardian. With the Hammers slipping to eighth in the Championship following consecutive home defeats, patience is reportedly wearing thin among key figures at the London Stadium.

Writing for The Guardian, Hammers fan Jacob Steinberg reports that although Nuno is expected to be given more time to turn things around, influential figures at West Ham are becoming increasingly impatient with the club’s disappointing start to the season.

The report comes just two days after the 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion, a result which prompted further questions about Nuno’s tactics and his ability to get the best out of a squad assembled with the intention of securing an immediate return to the Premier League.

According to The Guardian, any decision regarding Nuno’s future would be taken collectively by the West Ham board, rather than by one shareholder acting alone.

Interim chief executive Karim Virani and recruitment director Nils Koppen are among those expected to have input.

The report also revisits the decision to retain Nuno following relegation, explaining that David Sullivan had wanted a change of manager while Daniel Křetínský favoured continuity.

However, that previous support does not necessarily mean the manager’s position is secure indefinitely.

West Ham have won just twice in their last six Championship matches, and the upcoming fixtures against Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers could become increasingly important ahead of the November international break.

The Guardian also highlights concerns about Nuno’s inability to settle on his strongest starting eleven, the lack of balance in midfield and the failure of the club’s strikers to provide sufficient goals.

The report states that West Ham’s three recognised centre-forwards, Joël Piroe, Pablo Felipe and Taty Castellanos, have scored just five league goals between them this season.

Meanwhile, Jarrod Bowen has scored seven, leaving the Hammers heavily dependent on our captain.

The continued absence of recognised defensive midfielders Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Álvarez from Nuno’s preferred selections is another issue raised.

These concerns will sound familiar to Claret & Hugh readers. Following the West Brom defeat, I questioned whether Nuno’s entire West Ham project was becoming fundamentally flawed, particularly given the lack of cohesion and the manager’s constant tactical changes.

And while I appreciate that managers need time, I struggle to see how West Ham can continue performing so poorly with a squad that should be capable of competing for automatic promotion.

Perhaps the most important aspect of The Guardian’s report is the suggestion that Nuno will face difficult questions if performances fail to improve before the international break.

There is no suggestion that a dismissal has already been agreed, and the report specifically indicates that West Ham still hope the manager can turn things around.

Nevertheless, it appears the pressure is no longer coming exclusively from frustrated supporters.

The next two matches now offer Nuno an opportunity to demonstrate that he can produce a convincing response.

Because as I’ve argued previously, West Ham’s problems haven’t suddenly appeared over the last fortnight. The warning signs have been there for considerably longer.

And if the manager cannot begin addressing them, it is becoming increasingly difficult to see how the club can justify continuing with the same approach.

#2108. Arsenal injury news: Eberechi Eze concern emerges as Bukayo Saka awaits scan

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal came out on top in their match against Liverpool. Mikel Arteta admitted they have a new injury concern to deal with after Eberechi Eze was hurt. Bukayo Saka is also still out for the Gunners as they face two more games before the break.

The 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield means they are three points clear at the top of the Premier League. Arteta will need to be careful with his squad ahead of their Champions League clash against Slavia Prague on Wednesday and home game against Hull City.

Eze was a surprise omission from the starting line-up, despite featuring well in recent games.

Arteta later revealed that the England international was suffering from a problem going into the game. He also praised the club’s medical and performance team for getting him fit enough to be included in the travelling party.

There is some light at the end of the tunnel, with Eze being named on the bench. There is uncertainty over whether he will be available for the trip to Prague.

Arsenal will look to train him to see if he can play against Slavia. However, Arteta’s comments suggest that the issue is significant enough that he couldn’t start against Anfield despite his recent form.

There is positive news on Declan Rice, Noni Madueke and Riccardo Calafiori. All three were able to overcome their fitness concerns to start the game against Liverpool and play the full 90 minutes.

The availability of these players provides Arteta with more options as he heads into a busy week. However, he will be keen to avoid any unnecessary risk to those that have only just returned to full fitness.

Saka is still the biggest injury concern for Arsenal as he has failed to play for the last three games after suffering a quad injury in the clash against Bayern Munich.

He was forced off after just 10 minutes of the Champions League draw. He will not be available for the fixtures against Slavia Prague and Hull.

There were concerns that Saka may miss up to eight weeks of action. Arteta hasn’t confirmed when he will be back on the pitch.

The Arsenal manager explained earlier that there was a need to scan Saka again to see how the fluid around the injury was behaving. The medical staff will also want to know if there has been any damage to the tendon.

This will give clearer information on when he will be able to return to play. Until then Arsenal will have to plan without one of their most important attacking players.

Another player looking to make his way back to fitness is William Saliba. The defender has not played this season after aggravating a back issue during his time playing for France at the World Cup.

However, he has avoided surgery and has been back in individual outdoor training at the club’s training ground recently. Arteta says there are positive signs that his recovery is going well.

The club plan for an MRI scan to see how he is recovering. They are hoping to get him back in December, but it has not been confirmed by Arsenal.

It would give Arteta a huge boost to his defensive options. For now he will have to keep monitoring his recovery.

They play Slavia Prague on Wednesday and then play Hull at home on Saturday. This gives them two more chances to build up their position ahead of the international break; however, Arteta will have to consider the latest medical reports.

#2107. Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC

Tottenham Hotspur fans enjoyed their first glimpse of summer signings Andy Robertson and Sandro Tonali in the shirt, with both players scoring penalties in the shoot-out that followed a 1-1 draw with Sydney FC.

Spurs took the lead through a first-half Mathys Tel free-kick, before Roberto De Zerbi’s youthful defence was undone by Takahiro Sekine, who tucked away one of the Australian side’s only chances of the game.

Magic from Mathys Tel 🪄A brilliant free kick from the Frenchman gets @spursofficial off to a flyer, as the striker puts it top bins to take a 1-0 lead in SydneyWatch #TOTvSYD live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/ntqTgleasJ

Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

Spurs win the shoot-out 4-2. That will be that.

Hoefsloot dives to his right and pushes Donley’s penalty around the post.

But then Dubravka saves from Popovic, and Spurs remain 3-2 up. Score the next one and they win the shoot-out.

Very similar placing to Tonali’s penalty. Does Dubravka have a save in him?

He doesn’t need to have one because Josh Lacey has hit the post. 3-2 to Spurs after three pens each.

Plenty of power and right into the side netting. No mistake from Spurs’s big money summer signing.

Dubravka then guesses the right way, but Toure finds the bottom left corner. 2-2.

The 17-year-old takes the mickey a little bit, dinking the ball straight down the middle. Spurs score their first penalty.

Then Popovic steps up and sends Dubravka the wrong way. 1-1.

Spurs were the game’s dominant force, but they did not convert that control into enough goals. No cause for alarm though, and no injuries from what we can tell. There will be some penalties on the way.

Williams-Barnett with a superb piece of control and turn forward, but the danger was snuffed out as he dribbled the ball into the penalty area. Then the youngster shoots from outside the box, deflected behind for a corner.

Andy Robertson has been impressive, and the goalkeeper makes a fingertip save to flick his low cross away from danger. Almost third time lucky for Yang who was waiting at the back post for a tap-in.

Andy Robertson's first outing as a Spurs player 🫡 pic.twitter.com/q5bdzQknJ2

Spurs controlling possession, pushing for the goal that would spare them having to take some penalties. As happens with this friendlies, the game has become more bitty since all the changes.

If the game finishes as a draw, there will be a penalty shoot-out. Donley has fizzed some crisp forward passes since coming on in midfield. Then Donley underlaps, picked out by Williams-Barnett but his low cross is straight at the goalkeeper.

Andy Robertson getting forward to good effect once again, standing up a cross for Yang in the middle but the substitute heads wide from seven or eight yards out.

Referee waves play on as Spurs pour forward and Robertson flashes a ball across the box, and the slight deflection was enough to put off Yang at the back post and he missed the target. Should have been a tap in.

Spurs close to a second, but Tonali’s shot from the edge of the box is pushed around the post. There was more good approach play from Williams-Barnett to tee up the Italian.

More Spurs changes: Andy Robertson is on, and takes the armband, he replaces Kyerematen. Up front, Richarlison and Solomon are off, replaced by Min-Hyeok and Dane Scarlett. Donley and Melia replace Gray and Gallagher in midfield.

A couple of appeals for a Spurs penalty after Kyerematen burst beyond the Sydney defence from left-back. He could have crossed sooner, but was tackled, and then there was a challenge on Richarlison. Referee waves it away.

Very youthful Spurs back four on the pitch now, which played a part in the nature of the equaliser they conceded. No Romero, Van de Ven, Van Hecke or Senesi available for selection today, but Andy Robertson is warming up on the touchline.

Spurs straight back into another long spell of possession, with Tonali winning a foul in midfield after a smooth turn forward.

A touch of ill fortunate for Spurs, the half-time substitute Takai inadvertently poked the ball through to Sekine who lifted the ball over Dubravka to equalise. Delicate finish, and Spurs are breached.

Conor Gallagher still closing down tirelessly, but he has been a little untidy with the ball at his feet. I suspect he was the bleep test winner in training. Sydney do well to play through the pressure and keep possession for a while.

Good industry from Tonali in midfield to regain possession, and Williams-Barnett shows real poise on the ball again. Easy to see why Spurs are excited about him.

Kyerematen defends well at the back post when it looked like Macallister was about to head at goal.

Then Spurs are away on the break, and Williams-Barnett skims the crossbar with a left-footed shot from a tight angle.

Three half-time Spurs changes: Tel, Bergvall and Davies off, Takai, Tonali and Williams-Barnett are on. Takai goes to centre-back with 17-year-old Williams-Barnett in an attacking midfield position.

A decent half’s work from Spurs, they look in a good place physically and their high pressing has caught the eye. Not quite clinical enough in the penalty area so far though, they have butchered some good chances.

Sydney have come to life as an attacking force, Spurs’s defence undone by a ball over the top. Dubravka caught in no-man’s-land, and Mac Allister poked the ball beyond him but did not generate enough power to score.

Cracking effort from the Sydney forward Macallister, trying to chip Dubravka from some 45 yards out. The goalkeeper was worried and scrambling, the effort misses the target.

Sydney looking ragged now, and Gallagher cracks a shot off the foot of the post from the edge of the box. Then Youlley takes on a shot from long range which is high, wide and handsome. Richarlison is then fouled by Popovic, dragging down the forward to stop a counter. Yellow card.

Conor Gallagher is charging forward at every opportunity, applying pressure on Sydney’s defenders whenever they have the ball. With no European football, Spurs can really lean into a high-octane approach this season.

Great take, right footed to the the goalkeeper’s side, and the strike was too powerful for Hoefsloot. A clean hit, and Spurs now lead. A well-deserved goal on the balance of play.

The game has slipped into a lull now, after a bright Spurs start. De Zerbi’s team do now have a free-kick at the edge of the D after Manor Solomon is fouled.

Tel amnd Gallagher threaten down the left for Spurs, with the midfielder finding the winger with a reverse pass. Tel’s cross is cleared.

Then Sydney muster their first shot of the game, Youlley with a strike from 25 yards out which Dubravka pushes away from danger.

Sydney FC starting to get their foot on the ball a little more now, but still no sign that they have capability to hurts Spurs going forward. Kyerematen is then fouled in the Sydney half.

Sydney are yet to have a touch in the Spurs penalty area, it has been one-way traffic so far. De Zerbi will be pleased with what he has watched so far, but no killer touch in the box as yet.

Conor Gallagher with a nice touch to win a free-kick near the left touchline. Sydney just about hanging on. The goalkeeper claims Tel’s cross from the free-kick.

Spurs’s closing down is choking Sydney’s build up play, and Gallagher wastes a good chance when free in the box. Shot blocked when there was time and space to pick his spot.

Lucas Bervall’s low cross is turned behind for a corner and Spurs remain in the ascendancy. Another threatening delivery, and Ben Davies may well have had a shout for a penalty, dragged to the turf by Grant. If this was a Premier League game, I’m sure VAR would have taken a close look at that.

Hoefsloot with a really poor pass from his six-yard box, straight into the path of Tel 25 yards out, but his side-footed effort was saved by the goalkeeper. Pitches like this make technical errors an inevitability.

Sydney’s goalkeeper Hoefsloot punches a corner clear under some pressure, attacking set-pieces were a rare positive for Spurs last season. The Premier League team are dominating possession in the early minutes.

Conor Gallagher and Richarlison leading an aggressive Tottenham press in the early exchanges. Tel enjoys plenty of touches down the left flank, but his inswinging cross from the left is headed clear. Rio Kyerematen is puhsing on from left-back.

After a rendition of Oh When The Saints Go Marching In on the trumpet, we are under way. A chance for Aussie Spurs fans to feel like they are in N17 for the evening.

The pitch looks slightly more lush than the surface Chelsea had to play on across town yesterday. The Allianz Stadium looks distinctly similar to the Etihad. Archie Gray captains Spurs.

No James Maddison in the squad for this game, perhaps still being managed physically after last year’s serious knee injury. Suspect we will see a more senior side picked for the friendly against Chelsea on Saturday.

The 21-year-old has a sweet left foot, on display when he scored this goal against Manchester City while on loan at Leyton Orient.

JAMIE DONLEY. THAT'S INCREDIBLE. 🤯The @SpursOfficial loanee with an incredible effort from distance that ends up in the net to give @leytonorientfc the opening goal against Manchester City 😱#EmiratesFACup pic.twitter.com/bHnKg92Q2y

Lucas Bergvall has been linked with a move away from Spurs, but he starts in midfield. No Fernandes in the squad at all. No summer signings in the starting line-up, but Tonali and Andy Robertson are on the bench.

Spurs starting XI: Dubravka; Kyerematen, Davies, Hardy, Tye Hall; Gray, Bergvall, Solomon, Gallagher, Tel; Richarlison

Subs: Kinsky, Robertson, Takai, Tingey, Byrne, Tyrese Hall, Russell-Denny, Donley, Tonali, Ajayi, Yang, Williams-Barnett, Scarlett

Spurs fans took their first look at summer signing Mateus Fernandes in a 2-0 victory over Auckland, and their pre-season tour continues today against Sydney FC.

Fernandes, an £85m purchase from West Ham United, also scored a stunning volley in a behind-closed-doors game against MK Dons.

Sandro Tonali is part of the travelling squad for these friendlies, as is new centre-back Jean Paul van Hecke. Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero and Pedro Porro have been given extra time off after their respective nations reached the World Cup final, won by Porro and Spain.

Van Hecke and Senesi ranked very highly among defenders for progressive passing, which offers an insight into the qualities Roberto De Zerbi is prioritising this summer.

The Italian likes his teams to bait opponents into pressing them high up the pitch, before moving the ball through central areas using third-man combinations and wall passes. The addition of two ball-playing centre-backs and two new central midfielders should mean Spurs can play like a recognisable De Zerbi team.

While Dane Scarlett and Richarlison scored against Auckland, Spurs’s squad still lacks high-class options in forward areas, with a move for Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi mooted earlier in the summer.

Spurs fans will be excited to watch 17-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett, the midfielder who is one of the outstanding players in his age group in the country.

“He’s a talent,” Ledley King said. “There’s a lot of hard work ahead of him, but there’s no doubt that he’s someone with great ability.

“He’s seen players like Harry Kane come through the academy and, through sheer hard work and determination, put themselves in a position to kick on. He couldn’t have a better role model.

“There’s no doubt we’re excited by his talent and the next part will be up to him.”

#2106. Scotland star eyes dream Nou Camp return after childhood visit

Aston Villa captain John McGinn does not want the Champions League clash with Barcelona to be another tourist trip to the Nou Camp.

The Scotland international went on a stadium tour as an eight-year-old when he was on holiday in nearby Salou and remembers it as the day Ricardo Quaresma signed for the LaLiga club in 2003.

But on Tuesday he will be leading Villa out at the famous stadium as the club’s remarkable journey under Unai Emery continues, which has seen them beat Bayern Munich and Paris St Germain in the Champions League and win the Europa League.

McGinn admits he is living out his childhood dream, but wants matches like this to be a regular occurence.

“I used to go on holiday to Salou, and I was here for the stadium tour the day that Ricardo Quaresma signed for Barcelona, so I think I was eight years old,” McGinn said.

“I’ve never been since, but tomorrow night I’ll be excited to represent Aston Villa on the big stage.

“I am 32 years old. The trajectory of this club is allowing me to dream the same way I dreamed since I was 9, 10 and 11, to play in front of the biggest crowds in the biggest arenas and obviously this is a very historic stadium.

“But what the club are trying to do now is make this normal, make this a yearly experience and make Aston Villa compete with the best in England and the best in Europe.

“So it’s a pleasure to be on this journey with the supporters. I’m sure they’ll enjoy tonight and tomorrow.

“But as professionals, we only enjoy the experience if we have three points and that’s what we’ll be trying to do.”

Villa have won their opening three matches of the league phase, but face their stiffest test yet.

Being back at the Nou Camp probably will not bring back as many happy memories for Emery as it will McGinn as the scars of the 2017 ‘Remontada’ still loom large.

Emery was in charge of PSG when they squandered a 4-0 first-leg lead in the last 16 after a harrowing 6-1 defeat in Barcelona, where the hosts scored two goals in injury time.

The Spaniard looked like a man who is yet to exoricse his demons when asked about it ahead of the match.

Asked what he learned from that experience, he said: “(It was) one match more. Everything that happened in that match I learned in my career.

“I started coaching in 2004, 22 years in a row. Played in Europe 16 years in a row, different competitions, Champions League, Europa League and Conference League, and I’ve learned in all of the competitions.

“And in that match I learned so, so much. One sport side and another not a sport side. The necessity of VAR for football in that moment. The necessity of VAR.”

Emery has lost 14 of 15 visits to the Nou Camp as a manager and says Barca are the favourites for the match.

“To play against Barcelona is to play against the elite,” he said. “Barcelona is among the favourite to win the Champions League, I could pick five teams vying for the title, and they are one of them.

“Barcelona have six points, we have nine, they lost to PSG. To play against PSG is demanding, it was a clash between two favourites.

“We need to adapt, but we need to play our own game.”

#2105. Arsenal transfer news: Arteta considers January moves for two highly rated attackers

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal could have two ambitious attacking signings in mind for January. Eli Junior Kroupi and Kenan Yildiz are reportedly attracting Mikel Arteta’s attention.

Both players have emerged as potential targets as the Gunners consider further changes to their forward line. However, Arsenal may face a battle to prise either youngster away from their current club.

Kroupi is already familiar with the Premier League after making an impressive start to life at Bournemouth. The forward arrived from Lorient and scored 13 goals in 35 appearances across all competitions during his first season in England.

His development was halted by a broken foot in pre-season which required an operation to fix and kept him out of action for around three months.

The 20-year-old has now returned to the Bournemouth squad and has played as a substitute in their last three games. He will be hoping to get more game time as he gets back into full fitness.

Arsenal were linked with a move for Kroupi in the summer. His return to action has reignited interest in the player. A number of other European clubs also understood to be watching his situation.

Kroupi has attracted interest from a variety of top clubs including Manchester United, Tottenham, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

The French Under-21 international has impressed with his goal scoring in his first campaign in England. At only 20 years old, he has plenty of development to do under an experienced manager like Arteta.

However, Bournemouth are said to be reluctant to let Kroupi leave in January. Selling a bright young forward would leave Marco Rose with a tough decision to make.

It could get even more complicated if Alex Scott is also being seriously pursued. Chelsea and Liverpool are both linked with the midfielder.

Arsenal may therefore struggle to convince the Cherries to part with Kroupi during the winter window.

Another exciting option for Arsenal comes in the form of Juventus winger Yildiz. The winger has been linked with a move to North London for a number of transfer windows. He has once again been in the news recently at the end of the summer.

However, the Turkish international has struggled to get going on this campaign. He has only featured once in Serie A and has failed to feature since he suffered an injury.

Juventus have previously shown little interest in letting him leave. Head coach Luciano Spalletti firmly dismissed the prospect during the summer. Indicating that even an offer worth €100 million would not change the club’s position.

However, things could change next season. There are reports from Italy that Juventus may have to sell their star player if they fail to make the Champions League.

The Turin-based outfit are currently sitting in seventh spot in Serie A after just 10 games and are six points away from the qualifying spots.

This means that if they don’t make it into Europe, then it could put more pressure on Arsenal’s pursuit of Yildiz. It could create more pressure on them to raise funds.

Arsenal had a very busy summer with the addition of Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, Ezri Konsa, Piero Hincapie and Illan Meslier.

But they also missed out on a few big names, such as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez.

Despite this, there is still interest in Kroupi and Yildiz, suggesting that Arteta is still looking to strengthen his attacking options. Both players would bring quality and potential to the squad; however, there are some issues with both.

There are many unknowns surrounding this situation. Bournemouth aren’t keen to sell Kroupi and Juventus aren’t in a great financial position.

This doesn’t mean that either player will definitely be moving to the Emirates but much will depend on what happens at their clubs in the coming months.

#2104. Arsenal U19s face tough Slavia Prague test in UEFA Youth League

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal’s under-19s face a significant challenge when they travel to Czechia to take on Slavia Prague in the UEFA Youth League on Wednesday.

The young Gunners have picked up four points from their first three games and will be hoping to build on that in the league phase. Two wins would definitely help their chances of getting into the knockout stages.

They kicked off their campaign with a win against Napoli and put on a great show in a 3-3 draw against Bayern Munich last month.

Those results have left them 18th in the standings, 16 places below their next opponents. With the top 22 teams progressing to the knockout stages, another positive result could prove important for their qualification hopes.

However, Slavia Prague has made a much stronger start and will provide a difficult examination for David Horseman’s side.

Slavia have won all three of their first games in the UEFA Youth League and are sitting in second place. Just behind Real Madrid on goal difference.

They began well with a 2-1 win against French side Lens. They then went on to beat Sabah 3-0 and then put in another strong display against Fenerbahce.

Despite falling behind in Prague, the players fought back to win the game 3-1. The three wins means Slavia are already past the number of points they scored last season in the league stage.

They also advanced to the knockout stages last time, finishing 20th before they faced Benfica.

Mubarak Suleiman put the team ahead twice, but they were pegged back by two goals in the last 30 minutes as their European run came to an end.

This season they have looked like a much stronger team. With a perfect record, they will be one of the hardest teams that Arsenal will face.

The meeting on Wednesday provides an opportunity for Arsenal to get revenge for their heavy defeat in Prague last season.

The two sides met during the 2025/26 league campaign, with Slavia winning 5-1 at home.

Arsenal were three goals down at the break after an own goal plus goals from Bartosz Szywala and Jakub Kolisek.

O’Neill pulled one back after the break, but the home side had the final word as Suleiman and Matej Kotrba scored in stoppage time.

This loss shows how tough it will be for Horseman’s side. Slavia have already proven their attacking prowess against Arsenal and are playing even better in this campaign.

The young Gunners will have to play much more disciplined if they are to leave Prague with three points.

Arsenal fans can watch the UEFA Youth League clash on Wednesday.

It will be streamed via the Arsenal app and Arsenal.com, with the match taking place at the Sports Centre Radotin.

Updates will also be posted here and on the club’s Academy X page.

A full match report, highlights and post-match interviews with Horseman and one of the young players will be published on Arsenal’s official channels.

With them still in contention to qualify for the knockout stages, Arsenal will be looking to get off to a good start. Slavia’s great early start means they will have to play some of their best football of the tournament.

#2103. Latest injury headache for Nuno as West Ham first teamer dispatched for scan

After thirteen games  this season, the general consensus is that West Ham are lucky to have suffered so few injuries compared with several Championship competitors, notably Cardiff City who will likely suffer eight absences against the Irons on Wednesday night.

After the loss against West Brom, the Irons have just one serious new injury which has resulted in one player being sent for a scan.

Walker Peters: West Ham awaiting scan results

Already waiting on the recovery of Dinos Mavropanos who is still recovering from the injury sustained against  Southampton, the Irons’ boss now has to sweat on a scan outcome on Kyle Walker Peters who limped off with what seemed like a thigh injury during the second half against the Baggies.

Fortunately Walker Peters’ replacement, Joel Veltman, returned from injury in time to take over the right back duties as Walker Peters was forced off.

Whether the 34 year Veltman old remains able to play two games in four days in back-to-back starts against Cardiff and Blackburn remains to be seen, presenting Nuno with another conundrum for his back line, depending on the scan outcome.

Other than that, Keiber Lamadrid was the only player considered still ‘doubtful’ in  Nuno’s pre-match press conference last week, so it will be key to see the manager’s comments regarding his squad ahead of the next vital two games and, in particular, whether there were any additional knocks suffered last weekend which might further deplete his squad.

#2102. Cardiff v West Ham Preview: Parker Era Beckons After Nuno Sacking

Cardiff City v West Ham United EFL Championship Cardiff City Stadium Wednesday 4 November 2026, 7.45pm GMT

West Ham United’s crucial Championship match at Cardiff City will take place against the backdrop of a dramatic managerial change. Nuno Espírito Santo has been sacked with immediate effect following consecutive home defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion.

Scott Parker is expected to replace him, with discussions at an advanced stage and an official announcement anticipated. However, at the time of writing, West Ham have only confirmed that Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville are preparing the squad for Wednesday night.

The change completely transforms the complexion of a match which had looked capable of determining Nuno’s future. West Ham now travel to Wales looking for an immediate response, a much-needed lift and the first glimpse of what could become Parker’s latest Championship promotion challenge.

Scott Parker knows how to get out of the Championship

West Ham confirmed Nuno’s departure following what the club described as a thorough review of the Championship season. Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also left, bringing the Portuguese coach’s reign to a complete end.

The decision is hardly surprising after Saturday’s dreadful 3-1 defeat against West Brom. West Ham showed little motivation, lacked a coherent tactical plan and were repeatedly exposed by a team operating with far greater organisation and purpose.

Nuno leaves the Hammers eighth in the Championship after six victories from 13 league matches. We are six points behind leaders Middlesbrough and four away from the automatic-promotion places, which is not an insurmountable position but is considerably worse than expected.

The official statement explained that the board believed change was necessary to keep the club’s objectives on track. That is difficult to argue with because West Ham’s target was never to scrape into the play-offs; it was to secure an immediate return to the Premier League.

The full announcement confirming Nuno’s departure can be read in West Ham United’s official club statement.

Scott Parker is now expected to become West Ham’s new head coach. The former Hammer has been identified as the leading candidate, with multiple reports suggesting an agreement has been reached and only the formal announcement remains outstanding.

Parker’s record in the Championship is the obvious attraction. He has won promotion with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley, meaning he understands both the division and the specific challenge West Ham face.

He also knows the club. Parker made 129 appearances for the Hammers between 2007 and 2011, captained the team and won Hammer of the Year in three consecutive seasons.

According to our latest information, Parker’s proposed contract is heavily linked to promotion. He is expected to receive a longer-term opportunity if he takes West Ham up, while the club would retain protection if that objective is not achieved.

The timing creates an unusual situation before Wednesday’s match. West Ham have stated that Noble, Potts and Prenderville are temporarily overseeing preparations, but Parker could still be formally appointed before the squad travels to Wales.

Whether he would immediately take charge from the dugout remains unclear. Even if he does, there will be very little time for Parker to introduce significant tactical changes or properly assess a squad he has not coached.

That means the team will probably have to rely upon a reaction to Nuno’s departure rather than any sophisticated new system. The players can no longer hide behind complaints about the previous manager’s tactics, selections or motivational skills.

This is now an opportunity for them to demonstrate that they are considerably better than recent performances have suggested.

Changing the manager does not automatically correct everything which went wrong against Southampton and West Brom. West Ham remain vulnerable defensively, disjointed in midfield and overly reliant upon Jarrod Bowen in attack.

My preferred formation remains a 4-1-4-1, accompanied by drastic changes. Alphonse Areola deserves an opportunity in goal because Mads Hermansen has not done enough to make himself untouchable.

Joël Veltman should start at right-back, with Airidas Golambeckis partnering Max Kilman if Dinos Mavropanos remains unavailable. Kyle Walker-Peters would play on the left if he recovers from the injury sustained against West Brom, although his fitness remains uncertain.

Soungoutou Magassa should operate as the holding midfielder, providing the defensive protection West Ham have been missing. Lewis Orford and Divine Mukasa would then be free to play ahead of him, rather than being asked to perform roles which do not suit their strengths.

Edvin Austbø and Bowen would provide the width, with Joël Piroe finally receiving a proper opportunity as the central striker. As I argued before Nuno’s dismissal, West Ham need to stop repeating the same selection mistakes.

The managerial upheaval makes an honest predicted XI almost impossible. This is therefore the team I would hand to Parker or the interim coaching staff, subject to Walker-Peters and Mavropanos being declared fit.

Cardiff sit 17th after gaining promotion as League One runners-up last season. Brian Barry-Murphy’s team had been unbeaten in three before suffering a 3-0 defeat at Wolverhampton Wanderers on Saturday.

The Bluebirds could also have up to eight players unavailable. Gabriel Osho is suspended, while Will Fish, Perry Ng, Dylan Lawlor, Calum Chambers, Krystian Bielik, Alex Robertson and Isaak Davies are injury doubts.

That does not guarantee West Ham anything, particularly during a turbulent 24 hours at the club. However, it gives the Hammers a very good opportunity to respond immediately and begin repairing the damage caused by consecutive defeats.

The mood around the squad should already have changed. Players who were overlooked or used incorrectly by Nuno now have the chance to impress a new coaching team, while those who had become automatic selections can no longer take their places for granted.

My original prediction was a 1-1 draw, largely because nothing about West Ham’s recent performances inspired confidence. Nuno’s dismissal introduces the possibility of a reaction, but it does not instantly repair the team’s defensive and attacking problems.

West Ham possess more than enough ability to beat a depleted Cardiff team. The uncertainty is whether the players can produce a coherent performance so soon after a major managerial change.

I expect greater energy and urgency, but I will retain my original prediction until we know whether Parker will be in the dugout and which players are available.

Prediction: Cardiff City 1-1 West Ham United

#2101. Tactical change could revitalise Arne Engels if Nuno is ready to grasp the nettle | West Ham News

Arne Engels needs to be freed from the defensive duties with which he’s weighed down by West Ham’s current formation.

At least, that’s the gist of a report published last night suggesting that the Hammers need an old fashioned defensive midfielder at the heart of their side, to block off teams who at present appear to be able to play through their non-existent defensive shield owing to both Engels and Mukasa venturing too far forward too often.

As the 4thofficial suggested, there’s a remedy already at hand, a player largely ignored by Nuno yet one who could possibly could have a role to play in a more defensively solid West Ham United team, which is, frankly desperate to stop the early goals going in: Recalling defensive midfielder Edson Alvarez.

“From West Ham‘s perspective, reinstating Álvarez should come before abandoning the entire tactical framework. Engels has potential, but expecting the Belgian to provide attacking quality and defensive protection simultaneously places unnecessary pressure on an inexperienced midfield partnership.

Álvarez could give the centre-backs greater protection when attacking full-backs advance, while allowing Engels more freedom to distribute and move forward. That adjustment would address an immediate weakness without forcing another expensive recruitment exercise.”

Many have written off Alvarez as being too slow or too volatile in view of his disciplinary record – which other than an infamous red card against Liverpool – is perhaps not as bad as projected.

Report suggests the scrap- heap midfielder could do a job for Nuno.. if the West Ham manager is  big enough to mend bridges with El Machin

Many Claret and Hugh readers have commented that Nuno’s side needs the extra solidity of a ‘number six’ sitting in front of the back line to which, in truth, Engels doesn’t seem to be best suited.

Perhaps, indeed, rather than abandon the whole ‘tactical framework’ or trying to fit yet another square peg into a round hole, Nuno could grasp the nettle and re-integrate the tailor made defensive minded midfielder Alvarez into his line up.

There’s a down side of course. Dropping one of Mukasa or Kanté  would reduce West Ham’s creativity going forward. It could mean reverting Kanté to the bench blunderbuss role for the second half of games, exactly as he started the season so successfully.

It might make the Irons harder to score against in the first ’45 minutes anyway, Which at the moment couldn’t be such a bad thing. Is Nuno ready to grasp the nettle? Something has to give because right now, ‘hard work’ and ‘talking about it‘ isn’t fixing anything.

#2100. The ‘biggest trick’ Celtic missed that could come back to haunt them

Martin O’Neill’s position at Celtic has come under fresh scrutiny following a run of six defeats in 10 matches.

The club remains top of the Premiership, but former Rangers midfielder Kevin Thomson believes the club missed a huge opportunity in the summer by keeping O’Neill as manager rather than moving him into a different role.

Speaking on The Breakdown alongside former Celtic defender Charlie Mulgrew, Thomson claimed Celtic should have appointed then-Motherwell boss Jens Berthel Askou and kept O’Neill around as a mentor or sounding board for the new manager.

Thomson said: “I do think, and it’s easy with hindsight, I did think how dramatic the last day of the season was, he should’ve just up sticks and left. But I still felt the club would be missing a trick.

“I think Martin would’ve been a brilliant foil, mentor or sounding board, somebody to speak to, somebody to confide in as part of whatever that looked like for Celtic, for the new manager coming in.

“Now he’s been the manager; he’s had it for a longer period of time rather than just short-term, you kind of feel as though Martin O’Neill wouldn’t work because he’s now attached himself to being the manager.”

O’Neill had led Celtic to the title last season after returning as manager, with the Hoops beating Hearts on the final day to seal the championship. He was already in the job on a permanent basis, while Askou left Motherwell to take charge of Toulouse.

Rangers-daft pundit sounds Celtic alarm with ‘Covid year’ warning

Celtic's tactics under Martin O'Neill torn apart as ‘biggest pet hate’ laid bare

Ex-Celtic star sends fresh Scotland message after stunning display

Mulgrew believes Celtic could instead have installed Askou as manager and found a different position for O’Neill.

He said: “If he walks away then, Celtic still weighed him in with good money because he deserved that because of what he did with the title and then gave it to a Berthel Askou and let Martin O’Neill be director of football or be on the board or whatever.”

Thomson was even more emphatic about Celtic’s failure to move for Askou. He said: “It’s the biggest trick Celtic have ever missed, not getting him.”

Mulgrew added: “It’s a big one, isn’t it? I think he would have been desperate for it.

Thomson believes Askou could have been well suited to Celtic given the resources available at Parkhead and the style of football supporters have been accustomed to. He added: “You think of the resources that he would’ve had at his disposal and the type of players.

“He would be as close as getting a replacement that I think Celtic fans have been pining for since Ange Postecoglou.”

#2099. Three Defeats And Gone: What Křetínský’s History Means For Nuno

West Ham supporters wondering how long Daniel Křetínský will continue backing Nuno Espírito Santo might find some surprising answers in the Czech billionaire’s history at Sparta Prague. Because while the Hammers manager currently appears secure in his position, Křetínský has previously been involved in managerial decisions that make Nuno’s recent difficulties look relatively modest.

In one particularly extraordinary example, Sparta dismissed a manager despite being nine points clear at the top of the league. Another departed following three damaging defeats in quick succession.

And having looked into Křetínský’s history, I’m beginning to wonder whether Nuno’s position at West Ham is quite as secure as many of us have assumed.

Kretinsky has a history of being ruthless with underperforming coaches

Křetínský became involved in Sparta Prague’s ownership and management in 2004, when investment group J&T acquired the club. He subsequently became chairman and has overseen an extraordinary number of managerial changes.

Perhaps the most remarkable came in December 2004, when František Straka was dismissed despite Sparta being nine points clear at the top of the Czech league.

Yes, you read that correctly. Nine points clear.

Even more interestingly, Křetínský explained the decision himself in an October 2008 interview with Czech newspaper iDNES.

The club’s sporting leadership had lost confidence in Straka’s footballing system. With Champions League qualification looking secure, Křetínský decided to make the change early to give a replacement time to prepare.

He subsequently admitted the decision was a mistake.

Nevertheless, it provides an extraordinary insight into his thinking. League position alone was not enough to protect a manager if Křetínský lacked confidence in his methods.

The example I found particularly interesting was Vítězslav Lavička, whose first spell as Sparta manager lasted just 123 days in 2008.

Lavička had started reasonably well, but three damaging defeats in quick succession changed everything.

Sparta lost 3-0 against Slovan Liberec, suffered European elimination against Dinamo Zagreb and were then thrashed 4-1 by Slavia Prague.

Lavička subsequently left the club, with the departing coach explaining that he had rejected conditions attached to his continued employment.

So this wasn’t quite a straightforward dismissal. Nevertheless, three damaging results had helped bring a very short managerial reign to an abrupt end.

Considering West Ham have just suffered consecutive home defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion, I find that particularly interesting.

In February 2021, Sparta dismissed Václav Kotal despite the club sitting second in the Czech league.

In Sparta’s official announcement, sporting director Tomáš Rosický explained that management believed the team’s objectives were under threat and performances were deteriorating.

In other words, second place wasn’t considered sufficient protection when the club believed things were heading in the wrong direction.

Similarly, when Lavička returned for a second spell, he was dismissed in April 2015 with Sparta five points behind the league leaders and several seasonal objectives already missed.

These later decisions were made within Sparta’s wider management structure, so it would be wrong to suggest Křetínský personally ordered every dismissal.

A loss against Cardiff could spell danger for Nuno

Until now, I’ve been fairly convinced that Nuno is extremely secure in his job.

After all, it was Křetínský who backed the manager during the summer despite David Sullivan apparently wanting a change.

My assumption was that having made such a significant decision, the Czech billionaire would be reluctant to admit he had backed the wrong man.

Having researched his Sparta Prague history, I’m no longer so sure.

There is nothing in that record to suggest Křetínský will necessarily stick with a manager simply because he appointed or supported him.

If anything, what he has consistently demonstrated is a willingness to sanction managerial change when his club’s principal objectives appear to be slipping away.

At Sparta, that generally meant winning titles or securing European qualification.

At West Ham, the equivalent objective is automatic promotion back to the Premier League.

And having dropped to eighth in the Championship, following another dreadful home defeat, Nuno certainly isn’t making that task look particularly straightforward.

Of course, Sparta Prague and West Ham have different ownership structures, and none of this proves Křetínský is currently considering dismissing Espírito Santo.

But it has changed my assessment of the situation.

I no longer believe Nuno can necessarily survive a sustained period outside the automatic promotion places.

And if Křetínský’s history tells us anything, it’s that backing a manager today offers no guarantee he’ll still be backing him tomorrow.

#2098. West Ham Sack Nuno As Křetínský Loses Patience

West Ham United have confirmed that Nuno Espírito Santo has been sacked with immediate effect following mounting pressure on the Hammers head coach over the past few days.

The Portuguese manager’s position had become increasingly precarious following consecutive defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion, with concerns growing behind the scenes that the club’s automatic promotion ambitions were slipping away.

As Claret & Hugh reported earlier, there had been growing indications from within the club that Nuno was no longer safe in his position. Daniel Křetínský was understood to be increasingly unimpressed with performances, and the decision to act suggests the West Ham hierarchy were no longer prepared to allow the situation to continue.

Rumours had also emerged yesterday that discussions were already taking place over the identity of West Ham’s next head coach, suggesting that preparations for a possible managerial change were underway.

The decision is particularly significant given Křetínský’s previous backing of Nuno. However, as our earlier research into his managerial decisions at Sparta Prague demonstrated, the Czech billionaire has a history of making changes when he believes a club’s objectives are under threat.

West Ham have now confirmed that the change has been made following a review of the Championship campaign.

In an official statement, the club announced:

West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect.

Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.

Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed.

West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future.

The process of recruiting a new Head Coach is already underway.

Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of squad preparations ahead of tomorrow evening’s EFL Championship fixture at Cardiff City, and the Club will make no further comment until the appointment of the new Head Coach is confirmed.

West Ham must now move quickly to appoint a replacement, with the Championship promotion race continuing and tomorrow night’s trip to Cardiff City fast approaching.

#2096. A bad bad night in a season that now has a real fear factor as it ends Newcastle 0 Everton 1

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Ah no, it’s one of these, as it ends Newcastle 0 Everton 1.

Just days after a demoralising defeat against an opponent we could well do without, they turn up again.

Ooo and it’s been moved by the TV to a slot that we never win in, brilliant.

This was particularly unhelpful when it came to the scheduling of The Mag Pod, as getting it means an unusual Tuesday record and subsequent release which completely throws the schedule out of kilter.

WON’T SOMEBODY THINK OF THE PODCASTERS??!!!

Anyway, here’s a thought – there’s actually slightly better than a one in ten chance that you get one of these double headers after a cup tie. The latter rounds are full of Premier League teams and, given that your cup-tie will have a league match either side, there’s a two in nineteen chance of it being the same faces you had a miserable time against in your underwhelming midweek exit. We could maybe call being away from home first a mild advantage, as theoretically any strengths displayed by Everton in their win can be worked on ahead of the opportunity to disappoint almost 50,000 people as opposed to a hard travelling near 8k.

This was needed as Everton have been a dreadful opponent for us over the past couple of decades. Yes we have worse records but they tend to be against dominant teams whereas struggling versions of the blue scousers seem to have become an Achilles heel for us. Going into Monday’s game (in the bin please Monday Night Football) it had been four years since a fine Miguel Almiron goal saw off the Ev at SJP. We went into this looking to course correct after two dispiriting and damaging defeats in the last two matches here, and confidence wasn’t at its highest against an opponent without an away win all season, or any sort of PL win since mid-September.

This lack of confidence was not misplaced as it transpired.

I’m affected here by deadlines. To get a report done in timely enough fashion before then getting up and talking about it on Radio 5 in the morning then combing over it again in The Mag Pod is a lot of dwelling on a game I’d rather have erased from my memory in the style of Jim Carrey in Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind. This may be affecting my reactionary mood when I say that was one of the worst performances I’ve seen at St James’ Park in years.

For all the dissection and misery-riven reflection that will be in abundance across NUFC media in the days ahead, the most telling moment of this evening for me was at the half-time whistle, when a cowed and muted crowd reacted with boos and mutterings despite the fact that the scores were level and Everton didn’t look particularly dominant. Newcastle were alarmingly bad and tonight was critical as United 2.0 crossed the line from which managers struggle to recover. They lost the crowd.

The first half was a shambles. The tactics seem to be a deep lying non-striker supported by a hard working but ultimately fruitless midfield, with desperate passes regularly finding blue shirts and aimless long balls landing several metres ahead of the retreated Osula, easily dealt with by Everton’s well-drilled defence. Harvey Barnes had a couple of swirling cross-shots that drifted past the far post early on but United returned their usual zero shots on target. The Ev threatened late in the half as Barry made a terrible hash of a shot when well placed in front of goal, then Armstrong fluffed his lines similarly with a wayward shot from inside the box. Signs were there though, as every visiting counter attack looked threatening while United’s pedestrian build up play and shocking passing saw our attacks look more threatening as possible counters for the opposition.

There were lingering hopes of a Palace-style second half revival but any thoughts of this were snuffed out when Everton scored a goal that was always likely to be critical in a match that had a 1-0 vibe from the early stages.

There were issues with the goal. The ref apparently allowing play to go on before dragging it back when Barry made a tremendous meal of a challenge, then a lengthy injury to Schar and the threat of VAR giving an offside reprieve amid protestations aplenty from the Newcastle players. It was not to be though, and everyone needs to have a serious look at themselves. The free kick was taken quickly and the napping defence allowed George to walk into the box unchallenged. His shot was straight at Hornicek but he joined the calamity club by flapping and letting the shot squirm through him. He’d done enough to stop the original effort going in but presented Barry with a tap in.

The rest of the half felt like a sentence. You knew we were not going to equalise, much less turn the result around in the ample time that remainded and more of the same dreary, tactically-bereft meanderings masqueraded as attack for United. The substitutions also have an air of desperate punts, as opposed to deliberate tweaks. The five people introduced seemed to constantly be moving position with each new introduction and the most damning indictment of the performance was that Baz Toure, introduced on 87 minutes, was a contender for United’s player of the match with a series of excellent crosses creating late mayhem.

The returning Elanga came the closest to an equaliser, smashing a shot that Pickford stopped, but allowed to squirm past and get so close to crossing the line that some half-celebrations were heard. At the other end Hornicek did better to bat away Branthwaite’s header, before a late turn up for the books. Wissa came off the bench and registered our first shot on target when firing tamely at Pickford on 85 minutes. He even repeated the trick with a slightly better effort which Pickford chose to boot away when it looked like he could have held again.

The rain was sheeting down as eight minutes of injury time were endured, with the only moment of note being Jacob Ramsey getting two yellow cards in two minutes to put a cherry on the top of it all.

I left the ground extremely worried. The stat of three consecutive home defeats to Everton is an embarrassment but the manner of this loss has real alarm bells ringing. Everton are not great, but they are organised and do the basics well, proper Moyes stuff. This is a game plan that’s always going to work against this incarnation of Newcastle, as failure to convert possession is complemented by a horrible habit of giving away goals. Sides less organised than the Toffees will have similar joy if they have decent counter attacking threat, as Dedic and Hall are regularly caught forward while the midfield tries to cover far too much space between two of them (no clue where Willock was meant to be here, at one point he was treading on Osula’s toes).

This may be reactionary in the moment but this season looks worryingly like a relegation fight and the crowd knew it tonight. I’m debating here whether Eddie Howe ever lost the crowd in the ground, but if he did, it took that poor derby defeat to undo him. Jaissle has unfortunately hit that wall worryingly soon and this crowd ain’t daft (except for when it comes to following instructions for a minute’s silence for Remembrance Day).

It feels like our best hopes at the moment are mugging teams in even greater states of disarray by snatching the breakthrough moment in battles of fragile confidence. Fulham are an ideal opponent in that sense and as a result, the manager faces a massive game at the weekend. The fixtures after the international break are not kind at all and if the alarm bells aren’t ringing quite yet, they could well be drowning out the Christmas bells as they grow more deafening.

A bad bad night in a season that now has a real fear factor.

#2095. West Ham Insider Reveals Nuno’s Striker Gamble Before Sacking

Following the dismissal of Nuno Espírito Santo, questions are inevitably being asked about what went wrong during his time at West Ham United. And while there are plenty of areas worth examining, one of the most revealing concerns the Hammers’ striking department.

As Claret & Hugh learned from a West Ham insider before Nuno’s departure, the club’s three recognised centre-forwards were all specifically wanted by the Portuguese coach. That information is particularly significant given the team’s struggles in front of goal and the manager’s apparent reluctance to use some of the players he recruited.

The source’s assessment was straightforward: “They were all Nuno’s picks.”

It is a revelation that makes some of the decisions taken during the Championship campaign even harder to understand, particularly now that the manager has paid the price for West Ham’s disappointing performances.

The transfers attributed to recruitment director Nils Koppen have enjoyed varying degrees of success, and I still believe the jury is out on whether West Ham overpaid for Arne Engels.

But as Koppen himself explained, he had a very short period of time at the London Stadium before the summer transfer window closed.

What is not in doubt, according to our source, is that Nuno wanted Taty Castellanos, Pablo and Joël Piroe.

And it is the situation surrounding Piroe that I find particularly interesting.

“Nuno pushed really hard for Piroe because of his Championship goalscoring record. I’m surprised he hasn’t played more.”

Nuno pushed hard for Piroe but didn’t play him

Piroe arrived with a proven record of scoring goals in the Championship, something West Ham desperately needed following relegation.

Yet despite the Hammers’ continuing struggles in front of goal, he was given relatively limited opportunities to establish himself.

If Nuno was so determined to sign him, why was he so reluctant to play him?

It’s a perfectly reasonable question, particularly when neither Castellanos nor Pablo has done enough to make himself indispensable.

As we have already highlighted, the constant chopping and changing in attack did little to help any of West Ham’s forwards find form.

And if all three were Nuno’s preferred signings, it becomes considerably harder to blame the recruitment department for the lack of goals.

There had also been growing concern behind the scenes at the London Stadium that Espírito Santo did not know his best team.

It was a criticism supporters had been making for some time, and one that became increasingly difficult to dismiss as the manager continued changing personnel and formations.

The defeat against West Bromwich Albion provided another example of a team struggling for cohesion, creativity and confidence.

Ordinarily, in times gone by at West Ham, a certain amount of player frustration would eventually find its way back to David Sullivan.

Whether that happened in this instance remains unclear, particularly given the uncertainty surrounding the club’s ownership and decision-making structure.

But irrespective of any input from players, it had become increasingly evident that concerns were growing within the Hammers hierarchy.

The subsequent decision to dismiss Nuno confirms that the board believed a change was necessary, although it does not establish which individual concerns proved decisive.

Of course, Nuno’s departure doesn’t magically solve West Ham’s goalscoring problems.

Castellanos, Pablo and Piroe remain at the club, and whoever takes over will have to find a way of getting considerably more from them.

But that is also what makes the appointment of a new manager so interesting.

We have spent months wondering whether the problem was the players themselves or the way they were being used.

Now somebody else will have an opportunity to find out.

And perhaps the most revealing test will be what happens to Piroe, the proven Championship goalscorer whom Nuno apparently wanted so badly but seemed so reluctant to select.
