Lavelli blasts his shot down the middle, and Inter have won the Asahi Trophy!

The teenager sizes things up, and sends Donnarumma the other way.

A stuttering run, and Provedel beats it away.

Frattesi misses! Donnarumma stretches out and flings up his left arm for a great save.

Khusanov misses, firmly striking against the post.

Donnarumma dives to the right, the shot in the opposite direction.

Rayan Ait-Nouri misses! Spooned over the bar.

We’re onto the penalty shootout. The pressure builds for the Asahi Trophy.

Echeverri is fouled in midfield, he takes it quickly, but the move breaks down and Inter get back into position again. The end nears.

Three more minutes of this have been indicated.

Gonzalez finds McAidoo, and City look for room on the right. Inter sit back and stay compact.

The game has slowed to a near-halt. It seems everyone is resigned to penalties.

Ait-Nouri finds McAidoo’s run to the back post with a fabulous low cross, but the winger’s return ball is cut out by Provedel.

If McAidoo does not stay on at City for the season ahead, you’d expect plenty of sides to be looking to bring him in on loan.

Ait-Nouri is offside as he takes the ball on the left wing, and Inter have it back briefly.

McAidoo yet again gets forward and almost forces a cross past Provedel. The ball comes back to Sangare, but his effort is blocked. City are getting closer.

Khusanov is booked for a foul in midfield, and then is on hand to block a shot on the line as Inter fail to convert.

McAidoo, yet again. A shot to the far post, yet again. A miss, yet again. He looks dangerous though.

McAidoo repeats the trick, but this time he keeps his shot low and hits the bottom of the far post. The best moment of the half so far.

However, with the scores still level, it’s only 10 minutes from a penalty shootout.

McAidoo scoots into the box from the right and curls a shot wide of the far post.

Savinho slices a shot wildly high and wide. Changes are coming.

Reis claims to meet a corner at the back post, but it comes off an Inter player. The corner switches to the right, and this one is cleared, for now. City keep the ball and Ait-Nouri picks out Gonzalez’s run, and he strains to shin it over.

McAidoo is released down the inside left, he clears his marker and aims for Semenyo, but Bisseck clears for a corner.

Pavard goes down after he is caught late from Ait-Nouri, but he’s fine to continue.

More subs now  Topalovic replaces Stankovic. Provedel replaces Martinez in goal.

Savinho wriggles into the box but just fails to find Semenyo.

Foden commits his own foul in midfield, this time on Mkhitaryan. There are a few minutes left before half-time, at which point we may see a few changes from both sides given the early stage of pre-season.

Foden swings in a corner that Savinho briefly keeps alive before Diouf clears, and Dimarco cannot quite reach the ball before it’s played back to Donnarumma.

Mkhitaryan receives the ball on the left, inside the box, in another dangerous position. Lewis had drifted  too far inside, but the danger passes when the forward is flagged offside.

Inter are keeping the ball calmly at the back, finding spaces between the pressing City attackers.

Benjmain Pavard scores! Manchester City fail to clear their lines and Pavard, who started the move, is on hope to finish with the keeper stricken.

Divin Mubamba gets the opener! Semenyo beats his right-bacck and crosses to the six-yard box for Mubamba to tap in.

Stankovic goes close with an early header after Inter win their first corner of the match. It’s an open game so far.

City win two early corners, but they are both cleared. A bright start for the Premier League side. Esposito then goes close at the other end, but he was offside anyway.

Here is an examination on how Manchester City’s early, £116 million deal left the rest of the transfer market dealing with the implications.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester City and Inter Milan.

The two sides meet  at Kai Tak Sports Park, Hong  Kong as their pre-season work kicks up a gear ahead of the new campaign.

City are still getting used to life without Pep Guardiola, the coach who left after a decade of high spending and high performance.

In his place is Enzo Maresca, who is not shy with the chequebook himself.

Ayyoub Bouaddi, the outstanding 18-year-old Moroccan international, should soon arrive from Lille when a fee is agreed, but Elliot Anderson and Jeremy Monga have already been signed.

City were runners-up last season, so Maresca is under pressure not just to keep things going without Guardiola, but to get the team back to the top of English football. That looks to be a tough prospect with Arsenal likely to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle in the coming days.

Inter, meanwhile, have swooped to pick up John Stones on a free transfer after his contract ended at the Etihad Stadium, and he is joined by Manuel Akanji, another former City centre-back whose loan turned permanent in the summer.

Inter won Serie A last season under head coach Cristian Chivu, and they are still one of the best sides in Europe.

While this friendly is likely to be played at a reduced pace, and will be disrupted by rustiness and substitutes, we could still learn a lot about both sides going into the new campaign, and there may be the odd surprise thrown up by a young player looking to stake a claim ahead of his senior colleagues this year.

#2073. Premier League star Thierno Barry and his partner suffer 'distressing and violating' burglary while he's playing for Everton - a month after posting video displaying haul of designer handbags in their walk-in wardrobe

Published: 05:41 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 06:38 EDT, 30 October 2026

Thierno Barry and his partner became the latest victims of footballer-targeted burglary on Thursday night while he was playing for Everton in their Carabao Cup win over Newcastle.

Barry, 24, and girlfriend Charlene, with whom he shares a one-year-old daughter, were victims of an 'extremely distressing and violating experience'.

Charlene posted on her Instagram story about the incident and requested anyone with information that might help catch the criminals come forward. Just one month ago, she showcased a haul of designer handbags at the property on a TikTok post.

Barry and his family are the latest victims in a string of footballer-targeted burglaries, with Morgan Gibbs-White's Nottinghamshire home raided just three days ago. Man United's Bruno Fernandes also had his Cheshire home burgled while he played in Como two weeks ago.

Barry's partner wrote: 'Unfortunately, our home was burgled this evening while we were at the football match.

'Thankfully, nobody was home at the time, but this is still an extremely distressing and violating experience for us and our family.

Thierno Barry and his partner Charlene appeared in a TikTok video on her profile recently dancing with different designer handbags in their walk-in wardrobe

'If anyone has seen or heard anything suspicious, or has any information that could help, we would be incredibly grateful if you could get in touch.

'We are also willing to offer a financial reward for any information that helps identify those responsible. Thank you to everyone for your support.'

The opportunistic thieves no doubt would have known Barry would not be at home, with his other half also out of the house watching him in action at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Last month, Charlene shared a video with her 20k TikTok followers inside the walk-in wardrobe in their house, dancing with designer handbags, which the burglars may have targeted during the break in.

Football stars have previously been warned about the dangers of sharing pictures or videos from within their luxury houses or alerting criminals to when they're out of the house on holiday.

A gang of burglars who targeted John Terry's house while he was away skiing in 2017 were jailed for a combined 28 years and the judge said: 'It might have been a mistake to post a family photograph on social media to show he was away on holiday.

'As a result his home was deliberately targeted and the master bedroom suite was ransacked.

'They spent some time searching for items to steal. Not content with the original haul they returned with a third man and an angle grinder determined to get into the safe.'

Barry and his partner Charlene, pictured on holiday in the summer, suffered the distressing and violating incident of being burgled while they were at the Everton game

Thieves took handbags worth £126,00, £220,000-worth of jewellery and signed first edition Harry Potter books worth £18,000.

Insurance companies have also warned against footballers sharing holiday snaps that may alert criminals of their absence.

Barry joins Gibbs-White as the second Premier League star burgled this week. The England international's partner Britney De Villiers, who lives with him and their two children, issued the statement on Instagram in an attempt to warn others to remain alert.

She wrote: 'I wasn’t going to publicly share this but our home was burgled a few days ago and after hearing about another one since, I feel it’s important to just warn others.

'It’s incredibly unsettling knowing that homes are being targeted. Please be extra vigilant, make sure your security systems are on whether you’re in the house or not and report anything suspicious.

'Thankfully, nobody was home when it happened and material things can be replaced but it’s a horrible feeling knowing someone has violated your home, especially when you have young children.'

United star Fernandes, wife Ana Pinho and their two young children were not at their luxury £4million property in Nether Alderley when three thieves struck at around 8.30pm on October 21 before making off with designer jewelry and other expensive items.

Barry scored for the Toffees in their 3-1 victory over Newcastle on Thursday night

Bruno Fernandes pictured at home with his wife Ana Pinho. The pair have two young children and were also victims of a burglary recently while he was away in Como

The intruders were said to have been in the house for around five minutes before police arrived after being alerted by a neighbour who spotted them acting suspiciously in the back garden.

It’s understood that the house backs on to woods and the burglars jumped over the fence before breaking in, despite the Fernandes having installed CCTV and a high-tech alarm system.

Everton's neighbours Liverpool have had a number of players suffer the same experience over the years, with Sadio Mane, Dejan Lovren, Steven Gerrard, Dirk Kuyt, Pepe Reina, Robbie Keane and Lucas Leiva all going through the ordeal during their times at the club.

Peter Crouch and Abbey Clancy were victims on two separate occasions and a hooded gang raided Roberto Firmino's house in 2017. Thieves stole £70,000 worth of jewellery, watches and clothes on that occasion.

Another Everton player, Phil Jagielka, suffered a particularly harrowing episode in 2009 when he was held at knifepoint by an armed gang who broke into his house and forced him to open the safe.

Barry and his family are the latest victims of the highly upsetting targeting of footballers, with burglars fully aware of valuables kept on site.

Charlene appealed for any information that might lead to the burglars being caught

On Thursday evening before he heard the news of the break-in, Barry played the full 90 minutes for Everton and scored in the impressive victory.

The Toffees ran out 3-1 winners in the fourth-round clash and will travel to play Fleetwood in the next stage.

Despite the win, much of the discussion on the night surrounded Jack Grealish's absence as he was dropped for failing to turn up to training.

Grealish was said to be ill when he missed Saturday's trip to Arsenal, which Everton lost 2-0.

But now the Manchester City loanee has been reprimanded for failing to show for Monday's work-out and was not part of the matchday squad on Thursday night.

Unusually, the club gave the reason in a statement on social media which accompanied the team news: 'Jarrad Branthwaite remains sidelined for a second successive game due to concussion protocols, while Jack Grealish is unavailable for selection due to a breach of Club discipline.'

#2072. “I’m asking myself why…” – Steve Nicol frustrated by one thing Iraola did in Liverpool defeat

Steve Nicol was left frustrated by one tactical decision from Andoni Iraola during Liverpool’s defeat to Arsenal on Sunday.

The match was settled by Kai Havertz’s goal in the 16th minute and contained some controversial flashpoints, including a blatant penalty that the Reds should’ve been awarded and some unwelcome theatrics from Alexis Mac Allister after a clash with Noni Madueke.

Despite being on the losing side, the hosts were competitive for most of the game at Anfield, and it wasn’t until the surprise withdrawal of Trey Nyoni just before the hour mark that they began to lose the impetus they had in the middle of the park.

Speaking on ESPN FC as he reflected on the match, Nicol felt that Iraola’s substitution of the teenager for Dominik Szoboszlai was a poor decision.

The ex-Liverpool defender said: “The one thing that frustrates me more than anything else is the substitution that Iraola made after 60 minutes.

“Other than the little spell in the first half just before and just after Arsenal’s goal, Liverpool were dominating the game. Mac Allister and Nyoni had locked the midfield up and Arsenal were under pressure.

“It was the same at the start of the second half, and when he made the substitution and brought Nyoni off and Szoboszlai on, I’m asking myself why is he not taking Wirtz off and leaving Mac Allister and Nyoni to dominate the way they have been. From that point on, this game changed.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

We agree with Nicol that the decision to withdraw Nyoni – who’d been enjoying a terrific game on his first Premier League start – seemed surprising at the time and, in hindsight, wasn’t a smart move by Iraola.

We’d understand it a bit more if the 19-year-old was on a yellow card and in danger of being sent off, although we’ll admit that he was fortunate to avoid going in the book for a couple of aggressive fouls early in the match.

While possession stats can sometimes be misleading, it seems indicative that Liverpool had 59.9% of the ball at the time that the teenager was substituted, and 56.4% by full-time (WhoScored), a notable drop-off after Nyoni’s withdrawal as the Reds lost a measure of control in the middle of the park.

Florian Wirtz – the player that Nicol had wanted to be subbed off instead – has been excellent in recent weeks but didn’t exert as much influence yesterday, and the midfield was much less balanced with him and Szoboszlai on the pitch for the final half-hour.

Whatever you make of Iraola’s substitutions, it’s a testament to how brilliantly Nyoni is doing that Liverpool lost impetus after he went off, and the case for keeping him in the starting XI has been strengthened after Sunday.

#2071. Pedro Caixinha back in Europe after joining 13th club of managerial career

Former Rangers manager Pedro Caixinha has been appointed head coach of Cercle Brugge.

The Portuguese has signed a contract until June 2027, with the option of a further season, after the Belgian club parted company with Lars Friis.

Cercle Brugge beëindigt de samenwerking met Lars Friis. De Portugees Pedro Caixinha (55) volgt hem op als hoofdcoach van Groen-Zwart. De Vereniging bedankt Lars voor zijn inzet de voorbije maanden en wenst hem het allerbeste voor de toekomst. Met Pedro Caixinha haalt Cercle een coach met ruime internationale ervaring in huis. Hij tekent een contract tot juni 2027, met de optie op een bijkomend seizoen. 🔗 Lees meer via https://t.co/jsgsDLclPU

— Cercle Brugge (@cercleofficial) November 2, 2026

Cercle made the change after collecting six points from their opening 10 league matches, leaving them 17th in the table.

Caixinha, 55, spent seven months in charge of Rangers in 2017 during a managerial career that has taken him across Europe, South America, Mexico and the Middle East.

His most recent position was with Mexican club FC Juarez, while he has also managed Santos Laguna, Cruz Azul, Talleres, Red Bull Bragantino and Santos.

Caixinha won the league title, domestic cup and Supercopa MX with Santos Laguna and later lifted the Copa MX and Supercopa MX with Cruz Azul.

Cercle technical director Luciano Murchio said: “In Pedro, we welcome an experienced head coach who has demonstrated his qualities and achieved success at the highest level across different leagues and circumstances.

“We are convinced that he can help us achieve our objectives while respecting our playing principles and identity.

“We expect Pedro to have a positive impact on the team in the short term and help us turn around the current sporting situation.”

Caixinha will be assisted by Pedro Malta and Guilherme Gomes and will take charge of his first training session on Tuesday.

#2070. ‘You need to improve…’ – Ex-PGMOL chief urges Howard Webb to act after Anfield controversy

Pro Ref chief executive Howard Webb has been urged to take drastic action after some controversial flashpoints at Anfield on Sunday.

Liverpool’s 1-0 defeat to Arsenal was pockmarked by incidents such as the Reds being denied a blatant penalty when Jurrien Timber clearly tugged Alexander Isak’s shirt inside the box, and Alexis Mac Allister going to ground theatrically after mild contact from Noni Madueke’s forehead.

The home fans in L4 vented their spleen at referee Andy Madley as he left the pitch after full-time, and one former top-flight official believes that the 43-year-old should be demonstrably penalised for his performance on Merseyside yesterday.

Keith Hackett was surprised that the Yorkshire native was appointed to such a high-profile figure and said that, if it were up to him, the whistler would be stood down from Premier League duty next weekend.

The former PGMOL chief told Football Insider: “I was surprised, having watched his recent performances, that Andy Madley was appointed to this game. We have elite referees within the group. We have a pecking order, and those referees that are in form should get this game.

“There are going to be knocks on the door saying, ‘Boss, why haven’t I got a game?’; and I would be saying, ‘You need to improve your performance and be more consistent’.

“I don’t think he had his best game, and I don’t know what his best game is. We’ve highlighted a number of ifs, and I’ve highlighted one that is 100% incorrect. That says to me, next week if I was doing the appointments, he [isn’t getting] a game.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Some media outlets highlighted in the days leading up to Sunday’s fixture that it was Madley’s first appointment to a Premier League fixture between clubs in the traditional ‘big six’ for more than two years, with eyebrows being raised at that decision from Webb.

Some of the referees who are regarded as among the best in England have had their share of controversial moments too, so we had no complaints with the 43-year-old getting the Liverpool-Arsenal game, but he did himself no favours yesterday.

How he (and especially Stuart Attwell on VAR) can stand over the failure to award a penalty for Timber’s clear shirt tug on Isak is a mystery – that was a major error which wasn’t corrected when the opportunity arose, and it had significant consequences for the game as a whole.

Had the spot kick been awarded in the 21st minute (shortly after Kai Havertz scored) and the Reds equalised, the momentum of the match could’ve swung substantially. Andoni Iraola will surely have felt that way afterwards.

In his role as the head of Pro Ref, Webb bears ultimately responsiblity for ensuring high standards of officiating in the Premier League, something which hasn’t been the case for as long as we can remember.

If Madley is removed from top-flight duty next weekend, he could have no complaints after his error-strewn performance at Anfield on Sunday.

#2069. Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

United fought back after conceding an early goal against Atletico to secure their second win of pre-season.

They fell behind in the sixth minute when Arnau Ortiz’s cross into the box evaded everyone, including United keeper Tom Heaton before hitting the back of the net.

United got the equaliser their performance deserved when the impressive Shea Lacey showed his skill in the box and was fouled. From the resulting penalty, Bryan Mbeumo sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

In the 72nd minute, Mbeumo got his second of the afternoon after he bundled the ball home after the United press forced Atletico into a mistake.

The Spanish side hit the post twice in the closing stages but United held on to win.

“We had a clear plan before the game, everyone stuck to it and made the game enjoyable,” Mbeumo said. “We work really hard during training for these games, the main goal is to be ready for the season starting. I have done great things on the right but also as a striker.

“I think I am more experienced on the wing but I enjoy playing as a striker. For an offensive player, it is always good to score for the team.”

The visit to the Strawberry Arena means United are back at the stadium where they won the 2017 Europa League.

Gianni Infantino is facing an ultimatum from Uefa: resign or face an emergency no-confidence vote.

It is understood all 55 of Uefa’s member nations would opt to oust Infantino in a vote of no-confidence if he refuses to step down. Uefa can trigger such a vote with just 43 member nations.

European football’s governing body announced a loss of confidence on Saturday morning and has demanded change after Infantino was forced to scrap his £15bn plan to sell a stake in the World Cup.

Uefa’s statement followed widespread opposition and a revolt within Fifa’s ranks that staff are calling “kill the monster”.

The Football Association backed Uefa’s stance, saying: “We fully support Uefa’s position. It is time for a full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”

Atletico: Oblak, Domínguez, Le Normand, Hancko, Ruggeri, Koke, Obed Vargas, Castillo, Arnau Ortiz, Carlos Martín, Lookman

United: Heaton; Yoro, Maguire (c), Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Amad, Lacey, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Bayindir, Mee, Vitek, Amass, Armer, Kamason, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Thwaites, Gabriel, Williams, Zirkzee.

Good afternoon and welcome to pre-season coverage of Manchester United against Atletico Madrid.

Michael Carrick’s squad continue their preparations for the new season with a trip to the Swedish capital, Stockholm, where they face Diego Simeone’s La Liga side.

Last week, United cruised to a 5-0 victory over Rosenborg but today will be their first real test. They are slowly starting to get players back but the likes of captain Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans will not be involved.

“I think we’re in a good place. I think there’s four weeks to go to the start and we’re gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress,” Carrick said.

“But I think a little bit of patience and time and trying to keep ahead and as I said, keeping everyone fit but moving forward is a really good direction to go in. And as it stands right now, I think we’re in a pretty good place. So, the boys will get better as we go.”

One player who will be looking to impress is Mason Mount. He has had an injury-hit spell at Old Trafford but is fit and ready to go for the season. He is also growing into a leadership role at the club.

He told BBC Radio Manchester: “You have different types of leaders, you have ones that are very vocal. I always want to see myself as one that leads by example and never stops working on the pitch.

“I’ve been captain previously years ago. I love the role especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable in the game and off the pitch as well. It’s a role that I really like and loved having it [the captain’s armband] in the second half.”

#2068. Dominik Szoboszlai and Andoni Iraola seemingly disagree on one thing after defeat to Arsenal

Dominik Szoboszlai and Andoni Iraola appear to have had contrasting takes on whether Liverpool need to become more ‘streetwise’ after the controversial defeat to Arsenal on Sunday.

The main talking point from the game at Anfield was the failure of the officials to award the Reds a blatant penalty for a clear shirt pull by Jurrien Timber on Alexander Isak inside the box, just five minutes after Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the match.

The Basque admitted afterwards that he’d advise the Swedish striker to go to ground if the same thing were to happen to him in a subsequent fixture, with the 27-year-old staying on his feet despite the obvious infringement from the Dutch defender.

Speaking to reporters as to whether his team might need to be more savvy in trying to influence referees when fouled, Iraola said (via Liverpool Echo): “It’s a shame you ask me this question, but honestly, yes we have to tell them [to] go down.

“They’re not going to call it otherwise, and then referees complain why they go down, because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it. Then it’s like: ‘No, you are all the time going down’.”

However, Szoboszlai argued that the Reds shouldn’t feel a compulsion to more readily indulge in gamesmanship, saying (via Liverpool Echo): “It’s a penalty. I don’t know what they expect from us, to dive or something? I don’t think we are the type of team or players to do that but from now on we might need to do it.”

The Hungarian added: “Should we be more streetwise? It is not our type of play. I don’t think in this moment you can think this way that, ‘Oh, let me wait for someone touching me and I’ll fall down’.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

That there’s now a debate as to whether Liverpool need to become more streetwise and be prepared to use the ‘dark arts’ to their advantage is a sobering reflection on events at Anfield yesterday.

This is professional, elite sport at the highest level, with every match having the potential to earn or lose millions of pounds for every club, so it’s understandable that those involved will be ruthless in bending the situation to their will as much as possible.

However, we think Szoboszlai makes a fair point in saying that he and his teammates shouldn’t feel obligated to influence referees – ultimately, the onus is on officials at that level in the game to get the big decisions right, especially when they’re as obvious as Timber’s shirt pull on Isak.

Liverpool players aren’t totally averse to indulging in some gamesmanship, either, as Alexis Mac Allister showed yesterday with his theatrical fall after mild head contact from Noni Madueke. The Argentine was pilloried for his actions, and it isn’t the kind of behaviour that we want to see from any footballer.

Just like life in general, elite-level football often isn’t fair, as much as we’d all like it to be. It’s a cut-throat business where naivety is pounced upon, and in all likelihood the Reds would probably have had a penalty if Isak did go to ground after being pulled by Timber.

Ultimately, though, players shouldn’t feel a compulsion to do so; it’s up to the referees to penalise blatant rule-breaking.

#2067. BRYAN ROBSON: Stretford End's 'standards' banner made me sad - I never needed reminding of them. It's not about you, it's about hard work and Man United winning... I would never have called out Sir Alex Ferguson in public

Published: 08:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 08:00 EDT, 30 October 2026

Standards. The demand has always been to keep them high at Manchester United; you were aware the minute you walked through the door.

I'd like to think I never needed reminding of them by the Stretford End at least. Ron Atkinson, my manager, made me aware but I knew myself what was expected.

This was a club that had won the biggest trophies with Sir Matt Busby and Sir Bobby Charlton, great football names renowned throughout the world. I got to know both, as well as other greats, George Best and Denis Law.

You knew you were striving for excellence, to win, to be the best but when I met Sir Matt and Sir Bob, their fundamental message was ‘work hard’. Work hard, pull no punches in training, train as you mean to play and the enjoyment, the success, will come.

Sir Matt had been a miner as well as a player. He was an army man in the war, a company sergeant major, so that military influence, the work ethic, that discipline on the training ground, was born out of that.

It was instilled in you at United. He wanted his players to carry that forward. Yes, entertain but you must work hard, then you will have pride in what you represent.

I'd like to think I never needed reminding of Manchester United's standards. Work hard, pull no punches in training, train as you mean to play and the enjoyment, the success, will come

When Sir Alex Ferguson (left) came into the club, he had the standards already ingrained in him - and took United back to the top as Sir Matt Busby (right) had before him

Sir Matt (second left) and Sir Bobby Charlton (right, pictured celebrating winning the European Cup in 1968) gave the United players that followed them a fundamental message: ‘Work hard’

When Sir Alex Ferguson came into the club, he had that already ingrained in him. When we won the Cup Winners’ Cup in 1991 then the league title in 1993, I'll never forget the smile on Sir Matt's face; the realisation we were back at the top. It is what he had always dreamed of.

He and Sir Bob loved talking about how important it was to do well both domestically and in Europe. Perpetuating that legacy of the Busby Babes: ‘Remember who you are representing.’ Dress smartly, a good haircut, club tie, club blazer. No earrings, no ponytails. Standards.

So when you see the Stretford End unfurl a banner, reminding players today what they believe is missing, it’s sad to see. That my face adorns that banner, alongside Roy Keane and Eric Cantona, I’m thankful. Thankful that I’m appreciated because I always set out to give the fans everything and because Roy and Eric carried on the same work I put in with them as captain.

United’s players today must give full commitment to the club, those fans and ultimately, themselves. Representing Manchester United with all its history is a privileged role, the responsibility never weighed heavy on me, I always enjoyed it and today’s players should equally embrace the challenge.

I was fortunate to have good tutors in my younger days at West Brom. Hardened professionals such as John Wile, Tony Brown, Len Cantello and Asa Hartford. I saw the value of how they fostered team spirit, building friendships on trips to Worcester races, going for dinner together and playing charity golf or cricket tournaments.

You got to understand your team-mates better. You realised what was going on at home may be affecting how they were at training. Who could take a telling off, who needed an arm round the shoulder. It brought you closer and you looked after each other, on and off the pitch.

When I was made captain at United, I took those practices with me. Importantly, we always stuck together. If I were in the United dressing room now, I’d be saying, first and foremost, statistics tell us work rate must change. Step it up. Secondly, stick together.

Nothing should be coming out on social media or television, certainly not criticism of the staff. Those players know who they are. What needs to be said stays in the dressing room. If you need to have a fight, have the fight but it stays in-house.

The Stretford End unfurled a banner with my face alongside Roy Keane and Eric Cantona last weekend. The message was clear

Representing Manchester United with all its history is a privileged role, the responsibility never weighed heavy on me, I always enjoyed it and today’s players should embrace the challenge

Nothing should be coming out on social media or television, certainly not criticism of the staff as has happened recently with Bruno Fernandes attacking Michael Carrick (left)

I saw many a fight in the dressing room but it wasn’t for the public’s benefit. And I certainly wouldn’t challenge the manager in public. I had no problem saying I disagreed with Sir Alex to his face, but behind closed doors. You can't agree all the time, that's life, but the only way you progress is to stay together.

On the pitch, predominantly, you adhere to the tactics you've been given but if you're losing control of a game then work it out yourselves. For example, if Steve Bruce and Gary Pallister were getting overloaded, I'd sometimes ask Brian McClair to drop back into midfield to pick up my man so I could drop deeper and help the defence. When I got back into the dressing room the gaffer would either say 'great, now reorganise' or I'd get the hairdryer! But that was why you were captain, to take responsibility.

I always wanted to set an example by how I played but it’s not always possible to play well and it was important, because of that team bond we built, that the other lads were equally confident in giving me a rollicking if I needed it too.

It doesn't matter who you are, it's not about you, it's about Manchester United winning. Michael Carrick doesn't need players throwing their arms in the air, he needs them to knuckle down.

Michael invited me in to Carrington a few times earlier in the year and the training and attitude looked good. It got results. They know what's required. As Sir Matt said, hard work is the base for any improvement.

#2066. The £3m-rated Scottish winger with 16-goal contributions after SPFL exit for nothing

Dinamo Bucharest president Andrei Nicolescu has revealed they will allow Scottish winger Danny Armstrong to leave the club for £3 million....just over a year after he left Kilmarnock for free.

The 29-year-old has scored six goals and provided ten assists in just 14 league games this season and has helped Dinamo reach the top of the Romanian league

His club are trying to win the title for the first time in 20 years, but Nicolescu admitted if an offer came in for Armstrong in January that was too good to turn down, they would have to accept it.

He said: "The only way Danny Armstrong would leave in the winter would be if an offer came in that broke our expectations.

"So yes, if a bid came in for £3 million for him, he is definitely leaving because there is no way we can say no to an offer like that.

"That would still apply even if we were still challenging for the title.

"Let's be realistic. £3 million for a transfer of a player in Romanian football is a very large sum."

#2065. Homegrown Besiktas insider offers Celtic intel ahead of European showdown

Besiktas' only outfield Scottish player in their history reckons Celtic can snatch their first point in Thursday's Europa League showdown.

The Hoops are second bottom in the league phase after three defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo. They meet the Turkish giants this week after a shock 2-0 defeat to Falkirk at the weekend.

Besiktas have only ever had two Scots play for them - former Everton, Leicester City and Scotland midfielder Ian Wilson - and ex-Rangers keeper Allan McGregor, who is now back at Ibrox as a coach.

Wilson was not only the first Scot to play for Besiktas, he was also their assistant manager under Gordon Milne. And the five-times capped Scotland international believes there will be goals in Glasgow.

He said: "If Besiktas attack Celtic from the wings and play their normal game, they will create chances. "But they need to be mentally strong. They can cause problems for Celtic, find opportunities, and score against them. My prediction for the match is 2-2.

Ex-Celtic star’s £22m move takes fresh twist as manager who signed him axed

The ‘biggest trick’ Celtic missed that could come back to haunt them

Rangers-daft pundit sounds Celtic alarm with ‘Covid year’ warning

"Celtic has been inconsistent for the last year, but they will press and attack from the first whistle. They will press high, so Besiktas should be careful not to lose possession in their back three.

"However, Celtic have some injuries in defence, Besiktas will definitely create opportunities. Celtic remind me of Besiktas because both clubs have fanatical supporters and are very passionate. The fans are very similar.

"As we saw in the World Cup, Scottish fans are the best in the world. Both groups of fans are equally passionate about supporting their teams, but if they don't perform on the pitch, they make sure the team knows about it.

"I think Besiktas will be faster in recovering and regaining possession, which is a big advantage in Europe. "But if Celtic attacks all night at home, Besiktas will have to defend for their lives. That's why I think there will be goals at both ends.

"I loved my time at Besiktas. I was 29 when I played there and have made friends for life. We still visit Istanbul regularly."

#2064. Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Teenage sensation Max Dowman was the star of Arsenal’s first pre-season match, as he scored one goal and assisted another in a 4-1 victory over Girona.

Dowman, 16, was joined on the scoresheet by new signing Christos Tzolis, who struck with a low effort in his first game since his £34m move from Belgian side Club Brugge.

Established attackers Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also scored for the Premier League champions, who were largely comfortable against opposition from the Spanish second tier.

Here are four things Telegraph Sport learnt from the match:

It was this time last year that Dowman first announced his remarkable talent to the wider world. Then only 15, he sparkled in pre-season and made it clear to Mikel Arteta that he was ready to impact matches at the highest level.

A year on, Dowman is now an established first-team player. He is the youngest ever Premier League winner and the competition’s youngest ever scorer, and he looks set to make even more of a mark this season.

In this friendly against Girona, Dowman created Arsenal’s opening goal with a gorgeous defence-splitting pass for Havertz. He did so after receiving the ball under pressure and spinning into space. Dowman then scored Arsenal’s third with a powerful low drive from the edge of the box.

Dowman is in competition with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for a place on the right wing, which means this summer represents a huge opportunity for the teenager. After playing for England at the World Cup, Saka and Madueke will both miss most of pre-season.

Dowman, therefore, has a serious chance of going into the new campaign as the starting right-winger. The Community Shield on August 16 must be a target in his mind.

“We know what he’s capable of doing,” Arteta said. “We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver, but I think today he had a really good game.”

Arsenal are close to completing a deal for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães but, for now, their only outfield signing of the summer has been Tzolis. This was the Greek winger’s first match in front of supporters and he immediately demonstrated why Arsenal were willing to pay £34m to buy him from Club Brugge.

With Tzolis, it is all about the final product. Goals and assists. He struck 22 times for Club Brugge last season, and registered 29 assists.

How did he produce such impressive numbers? The answer could be seen in his first-half goal against Girona. Receiving the ball on the left wing, Tzolis quickly accelerated towards the penalty area and unleashed a low shot. It was perhaps a more direct approach than Arsenal would usually have seen from Leandro Trossard, the player Tzolis has replaced, and it caught Girona off-guard as the ball deflected into the net.

“I’m very pleased with him,” Arteta said. “First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, to the team. The connection he’s already generating with the boys. I think you’re going to love the player.

“A player who’s very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes. He has a lot of similarities with Leo [Trossard] in a lot of the things that he can do and the spaces he can occupy. And then the work rate that he has... He’s a boy that comes with so much hunger. He wants to prove himself, it’s a dream for him. And we are here to help him.”

Havertz was one of the few Arsenal players who benefited from playing at the World Cup. His injury issues mean that, unlike most of his team-mates, he did not end the 2025-26 season in a state of exhaustion.

After returning to the pitch in the spring, Havertz enjoyed an impressive end to the campaign for Arsenal. He then performed well at the World Cup, scoring three goals for Germany.

He remains one of Arteta’s favourite players, not least because of his versatility. He started in attack in the crucial end-of-season games in May, but played in midfield against Girona. His low finish, from Dowman’s pass, represented his eighth goal in his last 12 matches for club and country.

Girona’s goal, scored by Arnau Martínez, was perhaps the only alarming moment of this comfortable pre-season victory. Martínez was unmarked from a left-wing corner when he powered a header into Arsenal’s net.

For a group of players who pride themselves on their set-piece prowess, this was a disappointing moment. It also perhaps showed Arsenal’s reliance on their two first-choice centre-backs, William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães, when they are defending crosses into their box.

Gabriel arrived at Arsenal’s pre-season training camp a few days ago, so he should be in good shape by the start of the new campaign. Saliba, though, will be missing for months with a back problem.

Without Saliba’s height and power, will Arsenal be as effective from set-pieces in the opening chunk of the campaign? Coventry City, Arsenal’s opponents on the first night of the season, will undoubtedly look to test the champions in these situations.

The reigning Premier League champions are handed the Costa Brava Trophy, which is half-heartedly lifted into the air by White. There will be far bigger trophies on offer to Arsenal in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal have cruised to a routine 4-1 win over Girona, with Havertz, Tzolis, Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all finding the net. Arteta will be delighted with his side’s professionalism and ruthlessness.

Meslier takes too long on his goal kick, gifting a corner to Girona. However, the delivery from the hosts is so poor as it flies harmlessly out of play. That sums up Girona’s difficult evening.

There is another round of substitutions for both sides.

Two more changes in the offing...↩️ Jesus, Copley🔛 Agustien, Julienne🔴 1-4 🔵 (85) pic.twitter.com/3qt6N63qzq

Once again, Meslier makes a pivotal stop on his Arsenal debut. Martin clips an exquisite pass over Arsenal’s defence to the onrushing Ruiz, who is through on goal. The striker takes the chance first time, but Meslier is there to make another crucial save.

Arsenal’s makeshift line-up, which is full of Hale End graduates, is holding firm, with Girona evidently struggling for attacking inspiration. If Arsenal can see out this victory without any injuries, then it would have panned out exactly how Arteta would have wanted.

Girona carelessly give possession away in defence, allowing Nelson to dribble towards the penalty area. The winger floats a cross into the box, which is met by O’Neill, but the forward’s lofted header hits the top of the bar.

There is cooling break in this second half to give both sets of players a quick breather. It’s been a professional performance from Arsenal, who now have various academy prospects on the pitch. Can any of them follow in Dowman’s footsteps and make an eye-catching impression in this match?

The 16-year-old prodigy now has a goal and an assist. Dowman picks up the ball in the right attacking pocket, palms off Moreno, who bizarrely throws himself to the ground holding his face, before firing a resounding effort into the bottom corner. He’s such a talented footballer and looks at home in Arsenal’s first team.

Out of nothing, Girona have pulled a goal back. Kim whips a corner into the box, with the unmarked Martinez slamming a magnificent header into the top corner, leaving Kepa rooted to the spot. Arteta will be furious with his side’s complacency there.

The team known as “Set Piece FC” looked alarmingly vulnerable at that Girona corner. Perhaps this is simply the reality of life without William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes. The good news for Arsenal is that Gabriel is back with the squad and should be ready to go for the start of the campaign. The bad news is that Saliba’s back injury will rule him out for months. Will that lead to more sustained vulnerability over the opening chunk of the season?

Girona have sent a host of players out to warm up. They’re playing in their fourth pre-season match, with their league campaign due to start on August 16 against Leganes.

We are back under way for the second half.

That was a straightforward half for Arsenal. Arteta will be pleased with Havertz’s showing in his 33 minutes on the pitch. After missing so much of last season through injury, it has been a good summer for Havertz so far. He scored three goals in Arsenal’s final six games of 2025/26, and then netted four times for Germany in June.

The 2009-born playmaker was Arsenal’s standout player in that first half. Dowman’s confidence and class on the ball has been brilliant, with his expertly-crafted assist for Havertz’s opener an obvious highlight.

Arsenal are in complete control here in Spain thanks to first-half strikes from Havertz and Tzolis.

Dowman dribbles into the penalty area with ease, drifting past a couple of defenders before he is apprehended by Moreno. He goes down, but there is very little in the challenge.

Arsenal are in cruise control here. Girona are chasing shadows. Unsurprisingly, there’s a real gulf in class and quality between the two sides.

Once again, Dowman dances away from Moreno. The youngster sets up White with a reverse pass, but the Arsenal captain’s disappointing cross drifts out for a goal kick.

Tzolis registered 22 goals and 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He is an end-product machine, and that goal was a little indication of how he racks up such eye-watering numbers. After receiving possession on the left wing, he was so quick to shift the ball onto his right foot and fire the shot at goal. He describes himself as a “direct” player and that was evidence of it.

There are three early changes for Arsenal, with Gyokeres, Havertz and Hincapie taken off for Gabriel Jesus, Vieira and Salmon.

The new winger is one-on-one with Martinez and darts inside, before firing a low effort into the bottom corner. It took a slight deflection, leaving Gazzaniga with no chance. Tzolis has looked lively and slotted into Arsenal’s attack seamlessly so far.

Tzolis is slipped into the penalty area from his left-wing berth, but instead of shooting, he tries to find Gyokeres with a pass. Girona surround the Swede before Dowman’s follow-up strike is blocked.

Since their goal, Arsenal have assumed real authority of this encounter and look like the far superior side.

Arsenal are hunting for a second, with Lewis-Skelly picking out Havertz with a floated pass. After his extraordinary breakthrough campaign last year, Max Dowman has a huge opportunity this summer. With England wingers Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke not returning until later in pre-season, Dowman has a chance to take ownership of the right wing position ahead of the Community Shield. His assist for Kai Havertz, a lovely measured pass after an excellent piece of skill in midfield, was a sign that Dowman means business.

Dowman drifts inside and pops up in the right channel, wriggling past Moreno, before threading a delightful pass through to Havertz. One-on-one, the German calmly slots a close-range effort into the bottom corner, giving Arsenal a well-deserved lead. So much credit must go to Dowman, who has started this game excellently.

Girona have some sustained possession to take the sting out of the game then burst into Arsenal’s penalty area, with the ball attempted to be pulled back to Van De Beek. The visitors have good numbers defending and comfortably deal with the danger.

It’s been a confident start from Arsenal, who are stroking the ball around in a very assured manner. Havertz looks to pull the strings by firing a low cross towards Gyokeres, but the delivery is scrambled clear by the Girona backline.

White leads Arsenal out onto the pitch to face Girona, who boast the likes of Van de Beek, Gil and Moreno in their starting XI.

Talking earlier this week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta sent out a determined message to other clubs by outlining their ambitious transfer plans.

“A lot is happening,” Arteta said. “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

Arteta also believes that last season’s Premier League title has served as added motivation for his squad to improve and hit new heights.

“This has to be the start and this has to be the standard,” he said. “Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future. The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition, because we’ve shown that we’ve got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

It had been a relatively quiet transfer window for Arsenal, who have recruited just goalkeeper Illan Meslier and winger Christos Tzolis.

However, Arsenal are now moving very bullishly, closing on Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães, while also targeting Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior.

Sam Dean has the full breakdown of a potential deal for the Real Madrid star and how Arsenal are prepared to continue flexing their muscles in the transfer market in what would be one of the biggest moves in Premier League history.

It was January 2025, with Arsenal earning a hard-fought 2-1 comeback victory in the Champions League courtesy of first-half goals from Jorginho and Ethan Nwaneri.

Since this European encounter, Girona have been on a seriously downward trajectory, enduring lowly 16th and 19th finishes in La Liga, with the latter ensuring relegation to the Segunda Division, where they’ll play in the upcoming campaign.

August 5: Arsenal vs Real Betis (Dublin, Ireland)

August 9: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (London, England)

August 12: Arsenal vs Como (London, England)

August 16: Arsenal vs Manchester City (Cardiff, Wales)

Mikel Arteta’s side will then begin their defence of the Premier League title on August 21 when they host newly-promoted Coventry City on August 21.

Arsenal are closing in on one of the statement signings of the summer, with Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães getting closer to joining the Premier League holders.

This deal means that Christian Norgaard is expected to leave and seal a move to Everton for around £7m.

As previously reported by Telegraph Sport, Guimarães has been Arsenal’s top target for weeks. It is believed that he will cost around £80m.

Sam Dean has the full story via this link.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

#2063. ‘Not ready’ – Liverpool told to forget about partaking in title race after Arsenal reality check

Liverpool aren’t yet ready to mount a serious Premier League title challenge this season, despite signs of ‘progress’ under Andoni Iraola.

That’s according to Ian Ladyman in his column for the Daily Mail after the Reds lost 1-0 at home to Arsenal on Sunday, a result which leaves the Merseysiders nine points behind the reigning champions with just under a quarter of the campaign having been played.

It was a second defeat at Anfield in the last month for LFC, who were also beaten by second-placed Manchester City in a game which swung on the incredibly harsh dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch.

In taking stock of viable Premier League title contenders, Ladyman wrote in his Monday column: ‘As for Liverpool, they are simply not ready. Not yet.

‘That was apparent before yesterday’s home defeat to Arsenal, in which they played well. Andoni Iraola’s team also played nicely at home to City last month but lost that one too.’

The journalist added that ‘there has been progress’ under the Basque, particuarly in terms of their defence, but he feels that the Reds ‘remain a puzzle in the final third’ and lack a ‘calm intelligence and threat just when it really matters’.

In terms of realistic aspirations for Liverpool this season, Ladyman outlined: ‘A third-placed finish, a journey to the last eight of the Champions League and a tilt at a domestic cup would represent progress for Liverpool.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

A win for the Reds would’ve put them within three points of the summit and fuelled talk of potential title race involvement, especially as beating Arsenal would’ve represented a significant statement.

#2062. Inside Marc Guehi's 'complicated' month - and why Enzo Maresca won't drop his Man City 'lieutenant' despite errors for club and country

Published: 08:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 08:09 EDT, 30 October 2026

Manchester City’s famous five were all afforded holidays at the start of this week and there must have been some discussion about making that number half a dozen instead.

The quintet were all on the touchline during the warm-ups before City progressed through to the quarter-finals of another Carabao Cup defence on Wednesday night. With Erling Haaland’s oversized wool coat and Ruben Dias in leathers with a cap on backwards, it could’ve been mistaken for fashion week.

Enzo Maresca’s decision to grant three days off after defeat by Aston Villa was made with mental and physical fatigue in mind. The five, also including Gianluigi Donnarumma, Elliot Anderson and Josko Gvardiol, had all played over 850 minutes each so far this season.

But so too had Marc Guehi. And yet as those not required took their seats behind the dugout, he was straightening the captain’s armband and cajoling a group who traded blows with Brighton and then squeezed through on penalties.

Another full match to his name, the centre-half jogging 30 yards from the centre circle to console Mateo Kovacic after the Croatian’s miss in the shootout.

‘After two complicated games, I think he was very good,’ Maresca said of the only member of his leadership group called to participate in midweek.

While the rest of the Manchester City leadership group sat out Wednesday night's victory over Brighton in the Carabao Cup, Marc Guehi was captain and played the full 90 minutes

Rayan Cherki, Guehi and Enzo Fernandez celebrate the penalty shootout win over Brighton

Guehi was at the World Cup longer than Haaland, Dias and Gvardiol. He also featured in 332 of the 360 minutes comprising England’s four-game international window last month and will surely earn a rest at some point soon. Not that he thinks he needs one.

Maresca clearly felt there were compelling reasons for keeping Guehi going. If it was a straight decision between him or Dias for Brighton – with one needing to shepherd the back line against dangerous opposition – then the Portuguese’s extra game-and-a-half worth of minutes probably contributed. Guehi is younger and can likely bounce back quicker.

And then there is the recent form, some high-profile slips, and the manager’s psychology around that. Guehi admitted fault for both Ipswich Town goals in a 3-2 victory – caught the wrong side on both occasions – and then miscontrolled a Dias pass in the opening moments at Villa, allowing Nicolas Jackson to open the scoring.

Maresca hooked a booked Guehi at half-time in the Midlands, something ex-City defender Joleon Lescott feared could ‘shatter’ the defender’s confidence when discussing it on television. These mistakes came after Lamine Yamal had picked his pocket in the Nations League defeat by Spain at Wembley last month.

City’s manager has been defiant about Guehi this week. Aside from the praise after Brighton, he has talked up the 26-year-old’s ability to compartmentalise and react to setbacks.

Guehi is good at holding his hands up to team-mates and taking ownership, not hiding in the dressing room. It was one of the reasons why Maresca – who felt he needed an Englishman among his captains – chose Guehi as a lieutenant for first-choice skipper Dias. ‘I love Marc to be honest,’ the City boss said, somebody he chose to feature in central midfield on the opening weekend of the season.

There is definitely a school of thought around City that Guehi is best playing his way back into proper form, that Brighton provided a decent opportunity for that. His overall performances this season have been an improvement on his first six months at the Etihad Stadium, an imperious display at Old Trafford when the team were a man light his finest to date.

That followed a similarly impressive night in Porto, while he was the only defender to come out with real credit from the manic 5-3 win over Sunderland. Those were before the independent commission’s findings of City’s guilt for systematic breaking of financial rules, with England manager Thomas Tuchel revealing that the City players in his squad were naturally worried about the immediate future.

Ruben Dias has a word with Guehi after the Englishman's mistake led to Aston Villa taking the lead at Villa Park last weekend

Guehi had his pocket picked by goalscorer Lamine Yamal in England's loss to Spain in September

Concerns were allayed during meetings with chief executive Ferran Soriano and Maresca, with Guehi later stressing his ‘trust’ in the club’s insistence of their innocence.

This has been a whirlwind year, Guehi's move to Liverpool collapsing last summer as he lay inside the MRI scanner during a medical and then City accelerating interest in January to give them a defensive boost amid an injury crisis.

Guehi has barely had time to stand still, wrapping his head around the unique demands of working with Pep Guardiola after being so settled at Crystal Palace and then meeting another new manager within months.

Maresca has brought a slightly new way of defending, a more aggressive press – with even Dias storming into midfield at Villa on Saturday – and that has left more gaps to contend with at the back. It’s high risk and the likes of Guehi have to remain hyper-vigilant. It will likely take time for them all to settle into this.

#2060. ‘Really poor’ – Steven Gerrard left raging over ‘absolute embarrassment’ at Anfield on Sunday

Steven Gerrard described the failure of Stuart Attwell on VAR to intervene over a crucial decision at Anfield on Sunday as ‘an absolute embarrassment’.

There was controversy in the 21st minute of Liverpool’s defeat to Arsenal when Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak’s shirt inside the penalty area, a clear foul which somehow went unpunished just five minutes after Kai Havertz’s winning goal.

Reds boss Andoni Iraola went as far as to suggest that he’d encourage his players to go to ground in such situations, with the Swedish striker staying on his feet and not protesting to the referee despite the obvious offence on him.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Gerrard was aghast at how Attwell on VAR failed to intervene over the incident involving Timber and Isak.

The ex-Liverpool captain said: “The speed of the cross and how it happened and the reaction, you can understand how a referee could possibly miss that or think there’s not much in that, but for someone to sit in [the VAR room] with all these screens around – how you miss that in the VAR seat is an absolute embarrassment.”

He added: “To hold someone’s shirt for that long and have three or four opportunities to see that and slow it down, and the amount of cameras that are in stadia at the moment, it’s really poor from Stuart Attwell.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Gerrard’s incredulity over the lack of intervention from Attwell is quite justified – the official on VAR majorly dropped the ball in that instance.

We can absolve on-field referee Andy Madley to an extent, although the shirt tug was so blatant that he could viably have spotted it too, but there’s no excuse whatsoever for those in Stockley Park to let it slide.

VAR was brought in with the intetention of correcting ‘clear and obvious’ errors, and what Timber did to Isak yesterday very much meets that description. Why, then, did Attwell not recommend a pitchside review to the ref when it would’ve been very much warranted?

Some decisions are quite subjective even when slowed down or viewed from multiple angles, but this seemed like one of the more clear-cut calls to make, yet nobody with the power to take action was proactive enough to do so.

#2059. How 'football geek' Kim Hellberg turned Middlesbrough into the 'PSG of the Championship' - thanks to 'Del Boy and Rodney', the next Harry Kane and the transfer strategy that's taken them to a new level

Published: 13:14 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 08:53 EDT, 30 October 2026

I was sat in the press conference room at St Mary’s Stadium back in May when Kim Hellberg forced back tears as he talked about everything he’d sacrificed. All the time spent away from his family, all those nights when he called them to say he wouldn’t be coming home because he had more Southampton matches to watch.

And despite them all, there the Middlesbrough manager still sat, beaten in the second leg of the Championship play-off semi-final by a manager who sent staff to spy on his training session and who was, for now, going to Wembley.

‘I have nothing to say to him,’ Hellberg had replied when asked if he had spoken to Southampton boss Tonda Eckert. Hellberg had already completed his TV and local radio interviews but informed club staff that he still had things, about sacrifices, that he wanted to say.

In the end, of course, it was not over for Hellberg and Boro. Thanks to Daily Mail Sport’s stunning Spygate exclusive, Saints were eventually expelled and Boro went to Wembley in their place. By then, though, the chaos had taken its toll. Those who saw Hellberg in the build-up to the play-off final described him as exhausted and drained.

As did his players, who were left in limbo as they tried, somehow, to remain fit and alert. Luke Ayling, the club’s captain, found out they were going to Wembley while he was bathing his young son just days before the final. Middlesbrough lost to Hull, and had to prepare for a 10th successive season in the Championship. They should have gone up automatically but blew it, having spent most of the season second in the table.

All of that madness and heartbreak could, quite easily, have left Boro with too many scars and yet they host Charlton this weekend sitting top of the Championship, on a 10-game unbeaten run. Somehow, Boro have kicked on again and sources close to the dressing room believe they are better set than ever for a return to the top flight.

Kim Hellberg has led Middlesbrough to the top of the Championship as they banish all memories of Spygate

Aidan Morris celebrates scoring against Burnley last month - Boro are flying as they welcome Charlton on Saturday on a 10-game unbeaten run

For a start, Spygate has barely been mentioned. There’s been no talk of it, according to club insiders, except to discuss the impending return to St Mary’s at the end of November, one which everyone expects to be poisonous.

That has certainly not been helped by the FA’s decision to, effectively, let Eckert off scot free, and how much the Saints and their fans have appeared to revel in it. ‘Everyone in football knows it’s nonsense,’ said one source.

Boro, meanwhile, have just got better. It helps when you play like Paris Saint-Germain. ‘People might laugh,’ said Hellberg, who twice made a point last week of claiming Boro’s style of play shows similarities to the French giants. Hellberg watched PSG’s clash with Barcelona in the Champions League and was drawn to the similar ‘massive spaces’ left in their midfield as they look to be brave in attack.

That is how Hellberg wants his side to play, as risky as it sometimes looks to the casual observer, because it means creating a horde of good chances. They have the most xG (expected goals, which measures the quality of chances created) of any team in the league. Their 'expected goal difference', the gulf between the chances they create and concede, has rocketed since Hellberg took over from Rob Edwards almost a year ago.

Now, they have the player they needed to take those chances in striker Will Lankshear, the Championship’s top scorer, who has recently been labelled the ‘next Harry Kane’. No pressure.

Having been released by Arsenal, then gone through the Tottenham academy (via Sheffield United) before being sent out on loan to several clubs, there are plenty of parallels there, not least because Lankshear is proving himself to be one of the most lethal English strikers around.

His 11 goals so far in the Championship make him the leading scorer across the top four divisions of English football, with two more than Erling Haaland. Like Kane, he’s a superb technical finisher.

There was some surprise when Tottenham agreed to sell him in the summer for an initial £8million that could rise to £20m. But with Roberto De Zerbi showing little interest in academy players, Lankshear knew he had to make a move to get game time. Spurs inserted a matching rights clause should anyone try to swoop in for him.

Will Lankshear's 11 goals so far in the Championship make him the leading scorer across the top four divisions of English football, with two more than Erling Haaland

Sources close to the dressing room talk of a thoughtful, intelligent lad – ‘his head’s screwed on right,’ says one – who left money on the table to join Boro despite more lucrative offers from elsewhere in the Championship, Europe, and Premier League, including Leeds, because he knew he would be given the minutes to flourish, in a team that creates heaps of chances and just needed someone to finish them off.

‘I’ve learnt as much as I have my whole life in one week under Kim,’ said Lankshear recently.

So much of Boro’s hopes, say insiders, rest on Lankshear’s shoulders. Hellberg rested him for their recent game against Cardiff, only for the 21-year-old to come off the bench to score the equaliser. You suspect he won’t be making the same mistake again.

Sources describe Hellberg as a ‘football geek’. He grew up, like many men in their 30s, playing Football Manager. When previewing Boro’s trip to Bolton last week, a thumping 5-1 win that sent them top, Hellberg said he hadn’t been there before but remembered playing against the likes of Jay-Jay Okocha and Kevin Nolan on the video game. One of his heroes, Frank Lampard, phoned him to offer some words of advice ahead of the play-off final.

Hellberg celebrated the Bolton win by rewatching the game three times. He’d likely have watched it more if they lost.

When he was asked by a Charlton reporter last season if he had ever been to the Valley, Hellberg revealed he had with his dad Stefan, also a football coach in Sweden, during tours of a few grounds in London when he was a young boy.

Hellberg is described as a hands-on coach, one who likes to bombard his players with video clips about the minutiae of their game, and their opponents'. He’s hot on his data. Those who see him week in, week out, say he’s forever dropping stats into conversations and press conferences.

His first role was in the part-time Swedish seventh tier, during which he worked as a gymnastics teacher, and in a kindergarten teaching three to six-year-olds. ‘They are more like the players than you think,’ said Hellberg.

Sources talk of Lankshear as a thoughtful, intelligent lad – ‘his head’s screwed on right,’ says one – who left money on the table to join Boro despite more lucrative offers

So much of Boro’s hopes, say insiders, rest on Lankshear’s shoulders

As with many clubs on the rise – and on the slide – the foundations for that success, or failure, come from far above the grass. Just days after the Wembley heartache, Hellberg sat down with head of football Kieran Scott and head of recruitment Chris Jones to draw up their plans and key targets for the summer. Boro landed most of them.

They beat lots of clubs to Lankshear, whom they had tracked for a while. They snapped up Ashley Phillips, also from Spurs, who was their top defensive target. And Radek Vitek, from Manchester United, their top goalkeeper target.

The loan arrival of Brighton winger Amario Cozier-Duberry was described as the ‘icing on the cake’. Adilson Malanda, the French centre back, was described by one source as the ‘nearest we’ve had to Jonathan Woodgate since Jonathan Woodgate’.

‘We signed the quality that we didn’t have 12 months ago,’ said one club insider. ‘They are a level better. That’s the huge difference.’ This is what Boro have got really good at. Signing players to improve them, develop them, and sell them on at a huge profit.

Scott and Jones, who describe themselves as ‘Del Boy and Rodney’ due to their constant need to sell the club to potential signings who might have glitzier offers, don’t have hordes of analysts but sit there themselves with data software SkillCorner and StatsBomb. And it’s working.

A report by the CIES Football Observatory showed that Boro’s players have appreciated in value by nearly £150m over the last five years – the ninth-highest total in the country, ahead of Villa and Arsenal and just behind Chelsea.

They consistently make a profit on their stars. They signed Morgan Rogers for £1m in 2023 only to sell him to Villa for up to £17m seven months later. When he joined Chelsea this summer for £117m, they banked another £21m as a world-record sell-on fee.

Finn Azaz signed for £2m and was sold to Saints for £12m. Emmanuel Latte Lath, signed for £5m and flogged for £22.5m. Rav van den Berg, signed for less than £500k and sold for £11m.

The loan arrival of Brighton winger Amario Cozier-Duberry was described as the ‘icing on the cake’

Morgan Rogers (centre) was bought for £2m, sold for £17m seven months later and earned Boro another £21m in sell-on fees when he moved to Chelsea this summer

‘There is something special happening around this place,’ said one source. ‘On the field, off the field, recruitment. Everything is coming together’

Academy players have brought in huge profits, too. Like Hayden Hackney, who joined Everton in the summer for £16.5m, Djed Spence, who headed for Spurs in a move worth up to £20m and Marcus Tavernier, who signed for Bournemouth for £12m. As Del Boy would say, lovely jubbly.

The last time Boro lost in the play-off final, to Norwich in 2015, chairman and owner Steve Gibson gave a rousing speech to his troops to promise they would come back stronger, and they did. They went up automatically the following season. There is a similar feeling now around Teesside.

Club insiders talk of the strongest bond between the club and the community since the days of Juninho and Fabrizio Ravanelli in the 90s. Their attendances, in what is the year of their 150th anniversary, are their highest since they were last in the Premier League.

‘There is something special happening around this place,’ said one source. ‘On the field, off the field, recruitment. Everything is coming together.’

#2058. (Video) Half-time tunnel footage from Anfield on Sunday will only add to Liverpool fans’ fury

Liverpool fans’ sense of injustice over their defeat at Anfield on Sunday will be compounded by footage from the tunnel during half-time.

Arsenal triumphed 1-0 courtesy of a 16th-minute Kai Havertz goal, but the main talking point came five minutes later when Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak’s shirt inside the penalty area and somehow avoided any sanction.

The failure of referee Andy Madley and VAR Stuart Attwell to award a spot kick caused widespread fury, with Jamie Carragher screaming at the officials to ‘do your job‘ and Steven Gerrard describing the situation as ‘an absolute embarrassment‘.

In a clip posted by @LFC_Oman on X (via the Daily Briefing), the referee appears to tell the Brazil international: “Gabriel, be careful, yeah? You have already got two fouls.”

Maybe it was nothing more than a harmless exchange between Madley and Gabriel, but in the context of how the match went on Sunday, this clip will only add fuel to the fire from a Liverpool perspective.

If indeed the referee dished out a brief heads-up to the Arsenal defender, it could be perceived as him deviating from the neutrality he’s supposed to maintain, and the manner in which those involved were smiling after his words makes it seem like they were being too friendly with each other.

Also, that it was swiftly followed by a fist bump makes it seem even less professional from the official in particular, and he should’ve exercised more awareness in recognising that there were 60,000 or so home fans at Anfield already on his case over the failure to award a penalty for Timber’s blatant foul on Isak.

Madley should be less interested in sharing friendly chats with one team’s players inside the tunnel at half-time and more focused on his own performance and what he could’ve done better on the day.

This footage will only add to the prevailing sentiment among football fans in this country that refereeing standards at Premier League level leave an awful lot to be desired, especially for a division which is often proclaimed with chest-out bravado as the best domestic league in the world.

#2056. Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds

Leeds United came from 2-0 down at half-time to beat Liverpool 4-2 at Soldier Field in Chicago as Andoni Iraola’s side were undone by sloppy defending in the second period.

Liverpool’s dominant first-half display was underlined by goals from Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz. However, Daniel Farke’s men replied with four strikes in 25 second-half minutes through Sean Longstaff, Brenden Aaronson and two alarmingly similar goals from Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

🎯 "CALVERT-LEWIN ARRIVES!" pic.twitter.com/CaHOeXQn7E

🤩 "Calvert-Lewin makes it FOUR!" pic.twitter.com/mEEi882OWi

Liverpool centre-back Chambers, 22, who spent last season on loan at Charlton Athletic, opened the scoring on seven minutes, pouncing on a Dominik Szoboszlai corner which had been flicked on at the near post by Milos Kerkez.

Jeremie Frimpong, serviced by a wonderfully flighted cross-field ball by Trey Nyoni, then set up Wirtz to make it 2-0 five minutes before the break, but on the hour Leeds began their recovery when Aaronson scored following a mistake by Kerkez – who gave up possession to Ethan Ampadu in his own half.

GOAL! Aaronson pulls one back! 2-1 pic.twitter.com/tdy17cITSd

Ampadu’s long throw was flicked on to Calvert-Lewin to level the score, then minutes later Curtis Jones’s carelessness allowed Longstaff in to put Leeds in front.

🔥 "LONGSTAFF! WHAT A TURNAROUND!" pic.twitter.com/G9LvLIk0Mi

And it was a familiar story five minutes from time when Ampadu’s throw again prompted chaos in Liverpool’s back line, allowing Calvert-Lewin to steal in front of Jones and seal victory.

Liverpool return to Anfield for friendlies against Monaco and Como before they begin their Premier League season away at Newcastle United later this month.

Leeds have matches against RB Leipzig, Manchester United and Augsburg before their league campaign gets under way at Nottingham Forest.
