#2040. The Bushtucker dressing room! 'Woke' football club to make players change in a sea of 60 HOUSEPLANTS 'to reduce stress' - after banning meat pies and making their kit vegan

Published: 11:42 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 11:44 EDT, 30 October 2026

Forest Green Rovers' changing room has undergone a dramatic transformation and been left looking more like an I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! set.

The National League football club, renowned for their quirky and unconventional approach and often branded the world's most 'woke' team, have installed more than 60 plants in a bid to improve the players' mental health.

Environmentalist owner Dale Vince – who is worth around £100million – has had his club team up with Plants & Flowers Foundation Holland and a psychologist in a bid to help the squad relax in what can be a high-pressure environment.

Footage of the new-look changing room shows greenery everywhere, with the lockers themselves filled by vegetation.

While it may appear to be Rovers' latest wacky publicity stunt, the club insist there is science behind their re-design.

A statement on the carbon-neutral football club's website explained: '30% of Brits report that having living houseplants in a room noticeably lowers their stress levels and restores a sense of calm.

Forest Green Rovers have installed 60 plants in their changing room to reduce stress

The club are renowned for their environmental practices and quirky schemes

'Despite this, ‘plant paranoia’ is holding many back, with over a quarter of Brits (27%) put off by buying greenery because they are terrified the plants will die despite their best efforts.

'To prove that introducing greenery doesn't have to be a high-stress commitment, Plants & Flowers Foundation Holland is testing the theory in one of the most notoriously stressful indoor environments possible: an elite football changing room.'

The move coincides with International Stress Awareness Week ahead of their fixture against Harrogate and Dr Josephine Perry, a sports psychologist, said: 'Living greenery acts as a natural buffer, actively reducing nervous system arousal, which helps sharpen our cognitive abilities, allowing us to focus and perform better.

'Adding greenery to high-pressure spaces is one of the simplest, low-effort and accessible habits anyone can adopt to stay in control when the pressure mounts.'

Vince posted a video on X on Friday morning explaining: 'Up early this morning doing TV interviews. I'll show you what it's all about, it's in the changing room, all about plants. There's a little bit about Peterborough as well, the news that we have begun a legal process for the tapping up of our ex-manager Robbie Savage. That's the day so far, plants and what would you call it... hassle.'

He then moves into the newly decorated changing room and says: 'Here it is, chock full of plants. Quite chilling, really.'

Regarding the Savage lawsuit, Peterborough chairman Darragh MacAnthony previously denied that his side had made an illegal approach. Vince told Sky Sports on Friday: 'We're suing Peterborough and Robbie Savage for two million quid which was the buyout clause we were cheated out of and that process started last week.'

Controversial owner Vince, praised by some for his eco-focus and dismissed by others for what they perceive as 'woke' management, has found his club in the spotlight on numerous occasions for their unorthodox practices.

Their kits are made from recycled, sustainable materials and are officially certified as vegan.

The food in the canteen is completely vegan, with players also provided with vegan meals to take with them to away matches. Meat is completely off the menu and everything provided to players, fans and staff is plant based.

The players are seen in their new environment, with plants in each locker space

Rovers' pitch is maintained without chemical pesticides, herbicides, or synthetic fertilizers and cut using solar-powered mowers.

There's even a urine filtration system from the away toilets that is used to irrigate and water the turf.

There are also plans to build a new stadium made of timber with the lowest carbon footprint of any ground in world football. The club also promote cycling to matches and have electric charging points at the ground.

Vince, an eco tycoon who made his money in renewable energy, came under fire earlier this year after the club often branded the world's 'wokeist' made the decision to scrap their women's team, hardly the most progressive move.

The Gloucestershire-based outfit are spending their third consecutive season in the fifth tier, having failed to achieve promotion back to League Two at the first time of asking.

The club reached a record high of League One in 2022 but suffered consecutive relegations, ending their seven-year stint in the English Football League in 2024.

Vince has chosen not to directly replace Savage, who left on October 2, instead opting for a three-man coaching team from existing staff.

#2037. One thing Italy boss Roberto Mancini did recently shows exactly what he thinks of Giovanni Leoni

Giovanni Leoni appears to be firmly in the mind of Italy head coach Roberto Mancini, judging by one recent report from his homeland.

The Liverpool defender has been out injured for more than a year after rupturing his ACL on his debut for the Reds against Southampton in September 2025, with the 19-year-old since undergoing a lengthy road to recovery.

Despite some hopes that he’d resume team training during the most recent international window a month ago, Andoni Iraola has since indicated that such a step will hopefully be taken during the upcoming round of national team fixtures in mid-November.

Even though Leoni hasn’t played a match of any description for more than 13 months, it seems that he hasn’t been forgotten by Mancini.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the Italy head coach travelled to England in the hope of seeing the Liverpool defender (among several other candidates for Azzurri selection) on the pitch, but the teenager hadn’t recovered in time for the 61-year-old’s visit.

The report stated that the Reds’ number 15 ‘may return after the international break’, although that didn’t specify whether it’d be in the form of team training or clearance to finally resume playing.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Even with Leoni sidelined for so long, that Mancini reportedly wanted to see him in action on his vist to England attests to how highly the Italy boss regards the Liverpool defender.

The heartbreaking ACL injury overshadowed just how well the centre-back played on his Reds debut against Southampton before the cruellest intervention of fate, and the ex-Manchester City manager clearly has plenty of faith in the 19-year-old’s abilities.

The day that the young Italian is finally back in action will be one to cherish, although it’ll naturally take him time to get back into the rhythm of playing after being ruled out for 13 months and counting.

He could also have a difficult task on his hands trying to break up the uncompromising centre-back partnership of Virgil van Dijk and Jeremy Jacquet, with the latter particularly excelling since coming to Liverpool from Rennes in the summer.

Right now, though, simply getting back on the pitch will represent a seminal moment for Leoni, who should be given a tremendous boost by knowing that Mancini has him in his plans for the Italy squad.

#2036. PREMIER LEAGUE LIVE: Xabi Alonso on Estevao's future with Chelsea, Roberto De Zerbi confirms James Maddison IS available for Tottenham - and Andoni Iraola on why Liverpool fans can dream

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER and JACK GAUGHAN and MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER and LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 11:16 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EDT, 30 October 2026

It's another action-packed Premier League weekend ahead and the managers have been having their say. Follow the best of it here with Daily Mail Sport...

Xabi Alonso insists there are zero talks being held inside Chelsea about allowing Estevao to leave in January on loan for game time, despite the Brazilian wonderkid struggling for chances to impress.

The 19-year-old stayed sat on the bench during Chelsea’s Carabao Cup shootout-loss to Liverpool on Wednesday. In the Premier League, he has been a late substitute six times, and unused twice. It has seen questions asked of Alonso’s plan for a highly-promising talent.

There is no shortage of rivals who would be willing to take Estevao temporarily. As revealed by Daily Mail Sport this week, multiple clubs at home and abroad are watching his situation.

Before Manchester United visit Stamford Bridge for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off, Alonso was asked if they would consider finding him a temporary home in this winter window.

‘No, no, no,’ Alonso said. ‘No discussions about that. The season is long and there will be moments for everyone. It's a process for the team, for Este, for myself, but I'm sure that in the season, he will have his games, his minutes. We are still early in the season, but he will be there.

Xabi Alonso insists Chelsea are not discussing sending Estevao out on loan in January

‘It's not about attitude. It's been about the context of games, it's been about the start of the season, and he's a great guy. We are still in October and he will be important.’

Chelsea fans feel as if they have heard this before, and then watched as he failed to come on as a substitute in their Carabao Cup trip to Liverpool. The Blues signed Estevao from Palmeiras for £29million rising to £55m, and he is tied down to a deal lasting into the 2030s.

He had some magic moments in his first season, including scoring a stoppage-time winner against Liverpool in the Premier League and upstaging Lamine Yamal of Barcelona in the Champions League. His lack of opportunities this term has come as a surprise to supporters, who sang his name at Anfield, and led to speculation in Brazil that the youngster is frustrated.

‘It is no secret that all players want to be on the pitch,’ Alonso added. ‘When any of them haven't had enough minutes because of my decision, I have to take the responsibility for that, that they are not as happy as they could be. But everyone has to be ready because in any game, they could be important, they could be part of the team, and Este, his training and his attitude has been good.

‘We are back in Premier League mode, and that is, for me, the main competition for us this year, and it's a big one. It's one that we didn't have that much time to prepare, but it's really important after the last home game that we had (a 2-0 loss to Tottenham).’

Meanwhile, Maxence Lacroix has a hamstring injury which will sideline him for several weeks. Moises Caicedo and Pep Chavarria are fit to face United, but Jorrel Hato is injured. Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez may return sooner than expected – perhaps even before the international break – as Alonso said: ‘In case he's ready to play, he will need a face mask probably.’

Enzo Maresca has shrugged off Fabian Hurzeler’s thirst for revenge and the suggestion that Manchester City were lucky to beat Brighton in midweek as the managers face off for the second time in four days.

City progressed to the Carabao Cup quarter finals via penalties on Wednesday night, with the Brighton boss insistent that they had created more than enough to knock out the holders.

Maresca’s side are looking to open up an eight-point gap with the Seagulls, who are flying high in third. Hurzeler has confessed to being a ‘bad loser’ but has moved on from Wednesday night.

‘Revenge is more about him [Hurzeler] and not about us,’ the Italian said. ‘This is what he said. Every manager can say something different.

Enzo Maresca does not feel that his side were merely lucky to beat Brighton in midweek

‘It depends on what you see with your eyes. But I respect what he said. Probably the reason why it's so difficult to play against them is because they are always front foot, aggressive and their attack is also very good.’

Instead of returning to the south coast between fixtures, Brighton have remained in Manchester through the week and trained locally on Friday.

Maresca added: ‘If you see the Premier League games they have played, they scored three, four, five goals against any team. That's why I was so happy after Wednesday.

‘It's because yes, they scored two goals, they had some more chances. We also created chances. But we knew that it was a difficult test for us. We dealt quite well.’

Meanwhile, Maresca has claimed that no City star has a guaranteed place in his team despite revealing that shootout hero deputy Geronimo Rulli is not rivalling Gianluigi Donnarumma for the No 1 spot.

‘I think one thing is to say that in this moment Gigio is plus 10 others,’ he said. ‘And another thing is to say undroppable. Yes, there are two different things. There is no player who is undroppable. But in this moment it is Gigio plus 10. In this moment I see it like this.’

Tottenham playmaker James Maddison is available for Saturday’s visit of Crystal Palace despite an injury scare during the victory at Chelsea.

Maddison sparked more fitness fears when he limped off in the 51st minute of Spurs’ 2-0 victory at Chelsea.

After Maddison had endured a slow start to the campaign with caution preached over his fitness following a May return from anterior cruciate ligament damage, his substitution last Saturday looked to be another setback.

But, ahead of the Palace game, Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi said: 'James is available. This week he didn’t work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us. A special player because of the character and he has unique characteristics.

James Maddison is available for Tottenham despite an injury scare suffered against Chelsea

'For James Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks he is working very hard and consistently.'

'So, I think it’s not a problem if he loses two days (training), but then we have to analyse if we take risk or not.

'If we take risk like Pedro Porro (against Aston Villa) or (Dejan) Kulusevski.

'We are lucky to have a big squad and it’s important to not take risk with new injuries.'

Andoni Iraola is happy for Liverpool fans to start dreaming of a Premier League title challenge ahead of Sunday’s clash with champions Arsenal, but insisted it is too early for him to start looking at the table.

Victory at Anfield would see Liverpool move to within three points of the Gunners as they look to continue a five-match winning run in all competitions, but Iraola said his focus remains on improvements in performances early in his reign.

'It is still October,' Iraola said. 'We have to take one game at a time and I always say the reference is more or less when we’ve played against each other once so halfway through the season. That’s when you can start to look at the standings.

'Right now, we are in a position where we need to improve and keep getting better.'

Liverpool supporters are able to dream of winning the Premier League - but Andoni Iraola isn't getting ahead of himself

But when asked if he welcomed the growing optimism amongst Liverpool supporters, Iraola added: 'For fans, it is good if they have expectations or they think we can win.'

Arsenal moved level with Manchester City at the top of the table last weekend with a 2-0 win over Everton, but were then on the wrong end of a huge cup upset in midweek, dumped out of the Carabao Cup when they were beaten on penalties by League Two Fleetwood.

'We know Arsenal and how good they are,' Iraola said. 'They have very good players, working a lot in synchronicity and we have to be ready for that challenge.

'It’s going to be a demanding game but we also trust our players, trust ourselves and in the good atmosphere we will for sure have on Sunday. I hope we will be at level to win this game.'

#2034. Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR

Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7

Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

The final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

Victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i

The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

When Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

Gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

For 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

Maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

Abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

Bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

Bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

That is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

Should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

Just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

Good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

Tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

Bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

Bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

That was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder shows good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

Bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

Bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown is starting at left-back for Bayern today with Saibari not involved as he closes in on a return from a knock picked up at the World Cup with Morocco. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

Aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is currently out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

The ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

Good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

The first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

Interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

Chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

Currently, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Kamara, Joao Gomes, Hemmings, Buendia, Guessand, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Abraham, Nedejkovic, Bogarde, Rowe, Burrowes, Carroll, Lynch.

Bayern Munich: Neuer, Kim, Tah, Brown, Boey, Laimer, Bischof, Pavlovic, Ibrahimovic, Binder, Cardozo. Substitutes: Ulrich, Podar-Stiube, Urbig, Kimmich, Luis Díaz, Palhinha, Ito, Chávez, Pavic, Bara, Manuba, Stanisic, Della Rovere, Assomo.

The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return to training after their World Cup exploits and Aston Villa are also without captain John McGinn and new signing Alejandro Garnacho, who picked up knocks in their win over BG Pathum the other day.

Aston Villa have already sold Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers this summer, with Lucas Digne on the verge of a move to PSG, but could another starter be on the way out of Villa Park? England defender Ezri Konsa has been linked with moves to the likes of Arsenal and Liverpool but will Unai Emery be able to keep hold of the 28-year-old?

The atmosphere is building with our fans in Hong Kong! 🔴⚪️#AudiFCBTour pic.twitter.com/m4fFXAWxGb

It has been a big summer of change at Aston Villa already and there could be more changes before the end of the window. Left-back Lucas Digne is set to move to PSG and is set to be replaced by Atlético Madrid’s Matteo Ruggeri. Joao Palhinha, who is on the bench for Bayern Munich today, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa.

“Aston Villa are a top side with a very good coach. They have a large squad and will field plenty of talent. They have already played more friendlies than us, but for us it is a good challenge. It is a match in which we will learn a lot about our team’s fitness. It will be a good match for us.”

“It is difficult to improve; after all, it is not just about the trophies we have won, but also about the number of goals and matches we have won. It is possible, but difficult. Right now, I would say our aim is to win the Champions League; there is no doubt about that. And throughout the season, I will be saying that we need to focus on the next match. To achieve that; to win the Bundesliga, the cup and the Champions League, we need the whole squad to be fit and healthy. We need to make good use of them and improve the squad. We have already done that, but hopefully it will help us achieve our goals.”

July 21- Walsall 0 Aston Villa 5July 25- Porto 2 Aston Villa 1July 28- Aston Villa 2 Real Sociedad 4August 1- Indonesia All Stars 1 Aston Villa 3August 4- BG Pathum 1 Aston Villa 3Today- Aston Villa vs Bayern MunichAugust 12- PSG vs Aston Villa (Uefa Super Cup)August 15- Borussia Monchengladbach vs Aston Villa

Aston Villa’s preparations for the new season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some new faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

Unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

Bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

After today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

#2032. ‘Hopefully…’ – Andoni Iraola hints at potential Ryan Gravenberch return date after injury blow

Andoni Iraola has provided an update on the injury which has ruled Ryan Gravenberch out of Liverpool’s Champions League fixture against Fenerbahce.

The Merseyside club confirmed on Tuesday morning that the midfielder hasn’t travelled with the rest of the squad for the game in Istanbul tomorrow due to a heel injury and will instead undergo recovery at the AXA Training Centre.

While that obviously comes as a body blow for the Reds for the match against Dirk Kuyt’s side, it appears that the 24-year-old is unlikely to be sidelined for long.

Iraola was prompted for an update on Gravenberch during his pre-match press conference in Istanbul this afternoon, and the Liverpool head coach is hopeful that the Dutchman will be cleared to resume playing quickly.

The Reds boss said (via Liverpool Echo): “It’s a day-to-day thing. It’s a heel injury. He’s had some discomfort. He was warming up against Arsenal and was not 100%. Hopefully he can be available for the weekend, but we cannot say for sure.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

If Iraola has left the door open for Gravenberch to potentially return against Crystal Palace next Sunday, it suggests that the midfielder’s injury is relatively minor.

The 24-year-old mightn’t make it back in time for the visit to Selhurst Park, but the two-week international window should hopefully enable him to be fully fit for the grudge match against Manchester United later this month.

The Dutchman was criticised for his performance against Chelsea in the Carabao Cup last week and in recent games has been disapponting by his standards, but he remains a vital player to Liverpool and one of the best midfielders in the Premier League when operating at his top level.

Even if he’s cleared to play on Sunday, Gravenberch seems unlikely to start given the form of Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni in the middle of the park, and he mightn’t be able to feature for a full 90 minutes if he’s touch-and-go for the weekend.

Fingers crossed that our number 38 will at least be available to Iraola when the Reds take on Palace with one eye on revenge for their last-gasp defeat in this fixture last season.

#2031. Opposition insight for Milan-Inter: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

It’s the biggest game of the first half of the season on Saturday, as AC Milan face Inter in the Derby della Madonnina.

Saturday’s game could be make-or-break for Milan. Whilst it’s early to suggest that, the Rossoneri are desperate for three points to keep them in the title conversation, whilst a loss could put them 10 points behind.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

After their first Serie A defeat of the season in midweek, Ruben Amorim will be keen to bounce back, and he’s not alone in that regard. Indeed, Gerry Cardinale has spoken highly of the atmosphere around Milanello today.

➤ Manager: Cristian Chivu ➤ Form (all comps): L-W-W-W-W (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Marcus Thuram – 5 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Andy Diouf – 4 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Pavard, Jones, Stones, Martinez, Henrique.

In the summer, Inter oversaw a period of change, with several of the old guard departing. Davide Frattesi headed to Lazio on loan, Denzel Dumfries left to Real Madrid for €20 million, whilst Stefan de Vrij, Yann Sommer, Francesco Acerbi and Matteo Darmian all departed as free agents.

Changes would also come with the incoming mercato, though, as the Nerazzurri spent more than €100m. Djed Spence, Manuel Akanji, John Stones and Curtis Jones arrived from the Premier League, for a combined fee of €75m. Then, Aleksandar Stankovic returned from Club Brugge, with Ivan Provedel also making the switch from Lazio.

Whether those names have been an upgrade so far is difficult to tell, but it’s certainly been an introduction of a new wave of talent.

After dominating in Serie A last season, Inter have started the season in similar fashion, only dropping points to Roma so far. However, they’ve been something of comeback kings, regularly finding an escape when behind.

In fact, in their last three Serie A games, they’ve conceded the first goal – including the midweek disallowed goal against Venezia – yet they’ve always ended up with three points. The inevitability from recent seasons hasn’t disappeared.

What makes this potentially more frustrating is that they’re also struggling with injuries, but still getting results. Without Lautaro Martinez, Stones, Jones and Benjamin Pavard, a drop-off would’ve been understandable, but it hasn’t happened.

After their win in midweek, considering their schedule has also been rough, Chivu rotated slightly. So, there will be a few changes made this weekend to rotate back to their full-strength XI.

In the backline, Manuel Akanji will return to the centre of the back three, replacing Carlos Augusto. Whilst Alessandro Bastoni and Yann Bisseck will start either side of the Swiss defender. Of course, Ivan Provedel remains between the sticks.

Across the midfield, changes will be slightly more common. Federico Dimarco and Andy Diouf will remain on the flanks, whilst Piotr Zielinski retains his starting spot. Though Nicolo Barella and Hakan Calhanoglu both return to the starting XI.

Marcus Thuram will be given a starting role, hoping to continue his fine form this season, but Ange-Yoan Bonny will return to the bench. Pio Esposito will take his place instead.

Predicted Inter XI (3-5-2): Provedel; Bisseck, Akanji, Bastoni; Diouf, Barella, Calhanoglu, Zielinski, Dimarco; Thuram, Esposito

Predicted bench: Martinez, Di Gennaro, Augusto, Jakirovic, Bovio, Mkhitaryan, Lavelli, Mosconi, Spence, Bonny, Stankovic, Sucic.

#2027. Hearts' Riccarton Three - 20 years on: The dressing-room rebellion that pulled back the curtain on the madness of Vladimir Romanov's Tynecastle reign and altered the club's trajectory for generations to come

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:23 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 13:51 EDT, 30 October 2026

Only those individuals who’d been living in a cave for a year or so would have believed that all was well in Hearts’ world when they recorded a storied triumph over Hibs at Hampden 20 years ago.

A thumping four-nil win in the Scottish Cup semi-final on April 2, 2006, came courtesy of Paul Hartley’s hat-trick with Edgaras Jankauskas also getting in on the act.

As if there wasn’t enough for the maroon hordes to gloat about that afternoon, Ivan Sproule and Gary Smith were sent off for Tony Mowbray’s team.

With lower-league Gretna awaiting Hearts in the final, it should have felt like the good times were rolling. And, to an extent, they were.

The following month, the Gorgie men would beat Aberdeen to wrap up second place in the top flight and earn a place in the Champions League qualifiers.

With Gretna beaten on penalties ten days later, an open-top bus wove its way through the streets of the capital with the old trophy being shown off.

Paul Hartley, Steven Pressley and Craig Gordon hit out at the club's ownership in October 2006

Only six months earlier, Hearts had thumped rivals Hibs in the Scottish Cup semi-final

But the jubilant scenes were a distortion of the real picture. Vladimir Romanov, the Russian-Lithuanian business leader, had bought into the club in February 2005, becoming the majority shareholder eight months later.

He promised lavish investment to establish Hearts not only as the dominant club in Scotland, but as a European force to be reckoned with. Many supporters wearing Cossack hats lapped it up and were disinclined to look beyond the bluff and the bluster — or examine the price tag.

Those with a stronger grasp of the situation saw Romanov for what he was: An erratic egomaniac who’d be ruinous for the club in the longer term. The only question was how quickly it would take for it all to come crashing down.

It hardly required inside knowledge to appreciate that his eccentricities were going to test the patience of Hearts supporters from the get-go.

Despite the side sitting on top of the league after winning their first eight games of the 2005-06 season, Romanov sacked manager George Burley with chief executive Phil Anderton also fired.

Graham Rix, a convicted sex offender, was hired as Burley’s replacement before Valdas Ivanauskas was brought in on an interim basis in March 2006.

The former FBK Kaunas coach was given the full-time gig after winning the cup only to be put on sick leave with stress at the start of the following season.

Ivanauskas’ temporary replacement, Eduard Malofeev, the sporting director, barely spoke a word of English.

The preposterous turnover of managers was just the tip of the iceberg, though.

Rumours abounded that Romanov was in charge of team selection and would often fax in his line-up before kick-off — a matter Rix subsequently confirmed as being true. Players who were fit were routinely shunted to the sidelines for no reason.

At the owner’s behest, a mysterious woman from Eastern Europe joined the physio department. Brandishing a divination stick, she claimed to be able to identify injuries before they happened.

Accustomed to training in mornings throughout their careers, players were told to report for work in evenings — with no explanation. One recalled a session in the dark winding down with a wheelbarrow race.

For many, the final straw arrived when Romanov started to deliver his own motivational team talks.

It may have had the veneer of a professional football club, but it was a circus.

‘The place was an absolute shambles,’ said defender and future Hearts manager Robbie Neilson.

Behind the scenes, the senior players spoke privately about their deepening concerns and contemplated going public with them.

After weeks of procrastinating, they agreed that doing nothing was no longer an option. And so, on October 27, 2006 — just six months after that routing of Hibs — ‘The Riccarton Three’ were born.

Vladimir Romanov promised  Hearts fans that the club would dominate Scottish football

Hearts had lost at home to Kilmarnock the previous Saturday and were scheduled to play Dunfermline at Tynecastle the following day.

The press pack which descended on the training ground inside Heriot-Watt University was larger than normal on that cold morning for a reason. They’d been tipped off that something remarkable would unfold. ‘Bring your popcorn,’ wrote a message from one of the squad.

With Malofeev elsewhere in the building and the rest of the squad sitting in a dressing room, at 12.02pm the doors to the seminar room opened and the show began.

In walked Hartley and Craig Gordon, stony-faced. Between them, beanie hat on his head and holding a piece of paper, was captain Steven Pressley.

By the time the trio took their place at a table filled with microphones, it was clear that the next few minutes were going to blow the doors off the club. This was a dressing room revolution.

‘It was the crossing of the Rubicon,’ said Neilson. ‘As soon as you did that there was no way back.’

Despite knowing that he was unleashing a verbal grenade, Pressley delivered the words with complete calmness.

‘Chaps, just to make you aware that I’m going to make a statement and we’ll answer no questions,’ he said.

‘This is a statement on behalf of a number of the players.

‘I have tried along with the coaching staff and certain colleagues to implement the correct values and disciplines, but it has become an impossible task.

‘There is only so much a coaching staff, a captain, and certain colleagues can do without the full backing, direction, and coherence of the manager and those running the football club.

‘While, publicly, I have expressed the need for unity behind the scenes, I have made my concerns abundantly clear.

‘The last two years have been very testing for the players. Together, we have faced a number of challenges and worked hard at retaining some degree of unity.

George Burley was sacked by Romanov despite winning his first eight top-flight fixtures

‘However, due to the circumstances, morale, understandably, is not good and there is significant unrest within the dressing room.’

Pressley didn’t mention Romanov by name but he didn’t have to. Hartley and Gordon remained silent throughout the address.

And with that, they rose and left, the hush in the room in sharp contrast with the chatter of a normal post-match conference.

Although even the most experienced journalists present were stunned at what they’d witnessed, they knew this much: Nothing would ever be the same again.

Predictably, the fallout was nuclear. Seething with what he saw on Sky Sports bulletins elsewhere in the building, Romanov addressed the entire squad and told them they’d be sold if they didn’t beat Dunfermline. The game ended 1-1.

The three actually started the match. Malofeev gave a strange post-match interview where he angrily insisted there were no problems at the club and the players could say what they liked because it was a ‘democracy’.

A short time later, the actions of Romanov would prove this was not the case.

Pressley was dropped for the game against Falkirk on November 13, was an unused substitute against Rangers on November 19, was then stripped of the captaincy and left the club on December 9 ahead of a January switch to Celtic.

Bizarrely, on the day he was told he’d no future at Hearts, he was offered the assistant manager’s job.

‘I was probably seen as the figurehead of the club at the time,’ he later said. ‘Everybody leaned on me to try and get things done, or get answers within the club.

‘The treatment of some individuals was horrendous. The honesty, the transparency, all the things that I think are really important in the foundations of a club — they were being disregarded.’

Hartley was a substitute against Falkirk and also moved to Parkhead in the January for £1.1million.

Gordon, the most valuable asset, was dropped for away games with Dundee United and Rangers, but remained at the club until he joined Sunderland for £9m in the summer.

As for Malofeev? Hearts didn’t win a game under him. He stayed in charge until Ivanauskas resumed his duties in late November.

With Hearts knocked out of the Scottish Cup by Dunfermline in the New Year, a game in which Gordon was a substitute, Ivanauskas then made way for Anatoliy Korobochka, the latest director of football to be promoted to head coach.

Despite an upturn in results, Aberdeen claimed third place ahead of the Tynecastle side. So much for winning the title.

While the Riccarton Three were never going to topple Romanov purely by speaking out against him, their actions ensured he was never viewed in the same light again by supporters.

Eduard Malofeev failed to win a single match during his short spell in the Tynecastle dugout

When Stephen Frail was made manager in January 2008, he was able to demand that he would have full responsibility for team selection.

By the following year, Romanov had ceded the day-to-day running to Campbell Ogilvie. His visits to Tynecastle became increasingly less frequent.

No doubt, this had much to do with what he knew was coming down the track.

Although Hearts did defeat Hibs 5-1 in the 2012 Scottish Cup Final, the recklessness of the Romanov years was catching up with the club.

The following year, the collapse of his Lithuania-based Ukio Bankas triggered Hearts calling in the administrators who uncovered debts of £15m. A 15-point deduction and relegation followed.

Were it not for the mobilisation of the Foundation of Hearts and the largesse of Ann Budge, one of Scotland’s great sporting institutions would have gone under.

From the rubble, the club was rebuilt. With Tony Bloom involved these days, there’s an authenticity to the current talk of Hearts winning major honours, perhaps even the title one day.

As their supporters prepare to march on Hampden again tomorrow to face Hibs, the part of all of those who stood on the right side of history won’t be forgotten.

#2023. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

Possession: Chelsea 50%-50% AC MilanShots: 18-5Shots on target: 8-0Corners: 7-2

The final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

What a performance! 👏 pic.twitter.com/GcUZXwXbRj

Ramos is picked out after making a run into the Chelsea box and is denied by Sanchez. However, the offside flag has gone up anyway against Ramos. AC Milan have barely threatened the Chelsea goal in this second half.

A late change for Chelsea as Sarr replaces Fofana.

Chelsea are seeking their fourth goal as Quenda strikes a shot powerfully from just outside the box but it goes narrowly wide. Xabi Alonso’s side have dominated this second half.

Estevao has the chance to score moments after coming on after good work from the Brazilian down Chelsea’s right but is denied by a good save from Torriani.

Chelsea make a triple changes as Estevao, Mudryk and Watson come on. Mudryk made his return after his doping ban against Juventus during the week.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal once more. Jackson gets the better of Vladimirov down Chelsea’s left and moves into the AC Milan penalty area. Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

Ricci goes for an audacious strike with the outside of his right foot from outside the box but his effort misses the target.

Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

Chelsea made a substitution during that break as Anselmino comes on for Hato. Thus far, Chelsea have made three changes in this game and Alonso did confirm before the game that some players should be able to go the full 90 this far into pre-season.

Chelsea hit the post. Quenda receives the ball on the right side of the penalty area and quickly moves the ball onto his right foot. The 19-year-old then smashes a shot towards goal and the ball flies into the outside of the post. Quenda struck that with some venom.

Palmer has a chance to get Chelsea’s fourth from the left side of the box but AC Milan keeper Torriani makes the save down to his left.

AC Milan have offered very little going forward since the break and Sanchez has not been troubled in the Chelsea goal.

AC Milan have a good chance to get a goal back. Musah finds space on the right side of the box and cuts it back towards the penalty spot. He picks out Nkunku but the former Chelsea man wastes the opportunity.

Palestra is found with a cross from the right to the far post. Palestra takes a touch but his shot goes into the side netting.

Ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

Chelsea have their third and their new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee will be delighted with that one. Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their new record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. It is rather farcical how long Chelsea took to re-emerge for the second half and they just saunter out as if nothing is up. Why on earth did the officials just allow Chelsea to take over 20 minutes for half-time?

Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

Possession: Chelsea 58%-42% AC MilanShots: 6-4Shots on target: 3-0Corners: 4-2

The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Caicedo’s delivery from the right picks out Pedro, who has a free header inside the six-yard box and makes no mistake, picking out the corner. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

Palestra makes a run in behind the AC Milan defence and is found but De Winter gets back to put it behind for a corner...

Due to the water break, there will be three additional minutes at the end of this first half.

The first booking of the game goes the way of AC Milan as Pavlovic clears out Palestra. A deserved booking.

Neto and Pedro exchange a good one-two down Chelsea’s right to put the former racing down the right wing. Neto then tries to find Welbeck in the centre of the box but it is just behind him.

Then, moments later, Pedro spurns a great chance for Chelsea. Palestra’s cross from the left is just out of Palmer’s reach but falls straight to Pedro, who blazes over from 12 yards out. He was leaning back and should really be hitting the target.

The space opens up for Palmer to take on a shot from range but his effort is blocked by De Winter. Palmer has not managed to have that much of an effect on this game thus far.

Pavlovic drives forward from his defensive position through the Chelsea half. He gets all the way to the Chelsea box before shooting but he looked to lack conviction, firing off target.

We will pause for a drinks break, which unfortunately we became accustomed to during the World Cup. Palmer takes the chance to take a seat on the bench whilst taking on some fluids.

Neto takes a first-time shot from outside the box and looks to curl it into the far corner, forcing Torriani into a decent save diving down to his right.

That is good one-vs-one defending from Achemapong. Estupinan plays the ball into the path of Leao, who drives through the Chelsea half down AC Milan’s left. As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

Chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

Chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

A big, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

Chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

Neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

INS:Marco Palestra ⇠ Atalanta, £42mGeovany Quenda ⇠ Sporting, £42mMorgan Rogers ⇠ Aston Villa, £117mMaxence Lacroix ⇠ Crystal Palace, £51mDanny Welbeck ⇠ Brighton, UndisclosedJordan Henderson ⇠ Brentford, FreeValentin Barco ⇠ Strasbourg, Undisclosed

OUTS:Andrey Santos ⇢ Manchester United, £50mMarc Cucurella ⇢ Real Madrid, £50mTyrique George ⇢ Everton, £24mAlejandro Garnacho ⇢ Aston Villa, Loan

Chelsea are on the verge of making yet another signing with Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria close to securing a move to Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea: Sanchez; Palestra, Acheampong, Fofana, Hato; Palmer, Caicedo, Lavia, Neto; Welbeck, Joao Pedro.Substitutes: Sharman-Lowe, Penders, Sarr, Anselmino, Tosin, Subuloye, Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Watson, Walsh, Satpayev, Quenda, Gittens, Estevao, Mudryk, Jackson, Delap.

AC Milan: Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlovic; Chukwueze, Modric, Comotto, Estupinan; Loftus-Cheek, Leao; Camarda.Substitutes: Ricci, G. Ramos, Diawara, Nkunku, Fofana, Tomori, Athekame, Odogu, Jashari, Bartesaghi, Vladimirov, Pittarella, Gabbia, Saelemakers, Cisse, Musah.

The English forward joined Chelsea from Borussia Dortmund last summer for just under £50m. He struggled to make an impact last season in his first year at Chelsea, failing to register a goal in the Premier League or Champions League but did spend most of the second half of last season on the sidelines due to an injury. Gittens, who is on the bench for Chelsea today, has been speaking this week to CFC+:

“I am feeling, I would say, more confident now, in my body as well. The injury that happened [impacted my first season], but I am feeling better every day. I am trying to improve every day to be the best version of myself. It has been good to be back with the boys. I am really enjoying it right now and it has been really good to be part of this team.”

Have a great day, Jamie. 🥳 pic.twitter.com/QeX83XrXAM

In Chelsea’s defeat to Juventus in midweek, Ukrainian forward Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 after a long doping ban was resolved. You can read all about that game right here. Mudryk is on the bench for Chelsea today.

Our line-up to face AC Milan! pic.twitter.com/MK2hd0c708

Current Chelsea defender Tosin Adarabioyo has been catching up with former Chelsea men Ruben Loftus-Cheek, who starts for AC Milan today, and Fikayo Tomori.

The team news is in from Jakarta! 🗞️ pic.twitter.com/BRBjmlgwz8

The atmosphere is building. 🇮🇩📈 pic.twitter.com/fhXfDVAf6s

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#2020. Why Sebastien Pocognoli picked James Penrice as he talks up Rangers star's quality

Scotland manager Sebastien Pocognoli insists the selection of Rangers' James Penrice was "logical."

The left-back, who has also operated in midfield, has been rewarded for his form so far since moving to Ibrox on loan from AEK Athens. He immediately impressed since joining but was left out of Pocognoli's first squad for the last camp.

Now, the 27-year-old will get the chance to win his first cap when the national team takes on North Macedonia and Switzerland this month.

The Scotland boss says the quality Penrice possesses, and his readiness for his system, made him an obvious choice.

Rangers game rescheduled as a result of Premier Sports Cup final participation WATCH: Nico Raskin turns interviewer after Rangers teammate's Scotland joy

He said: "We have a list of players that we select regarding the performance at their clubs, but also the style of play or the way that we want to play.

"We have some missing players around the left side.

"So, combined with his quality and what we are looking for on the pitch, it's a logical choice for me and it can be very useful for the system that we want to play and also I think he deserves it."

Scotland face North Macedonia at Hampden on November 13 before an away game in Switzerland on November 16.

#2018. Chivu discusses poor derby record, new San Siro and Milan’s quality: “At our best”

Ahead of tomorrow’s game against AC Milan, Inter boss Cristian Chivu spoke to the media about his team’s chances.

For Inter, this is perhaps the biggest derby in the recent run. After all, they’re without a win in seven games and if they fall to defeat, they’re inviting more pressure in the title race. Right now, though, they sit in a very comfortable position.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Having dropped points once this season – a draw against Roma – they’re rightly the favourites heading into this game, especially with the injuries plaguing Ruben Amorim’s side. Nevertheless, there are never really favourites in these games.

Speaking before the game on Friday, Ruben Amorim spoke about a number of things, admitting that his team still needed to improve this season and he’s not the only side of the derby to say that.

In his own press conference this evening, Chivu admitted the same, as MilanVibes relayed.

“We’re coming prepared and aware of how important this match is for everyone. In a derby, you shouldn’t think about the standings, but only about doing everything you can to win.

“Our approach will depend on the team’s physical and mental condition, but also on the opponent’s characteristics. We know Milan’s quality, their dribbling, and their ability to hurt us through technique and speed. We’ll have to be ready and stay calm at all times.”

“If we haven’t won a derby in such a long time, it means we need to ask ourselves some questions and figure out what we can improve on. I don’t think we lacked commitment, because in matches like this, incidents can also have an impact, but we definitely need to improve.

“We can’t settle for recent results, nor for last season’s, nor for what we’ve done so far this season: we need to show our best.

“The derby is a match that can give a lot to the winner and take a lot away from the loser, but we’re only at the tenth matchday, and last season’s history shows that the result of a derby doesn’t always determine what happens next.

“In a tournament, every match has its own importance. There are no favourites, and the pressure is on both teams: we need to avoid getting caught up in thoughts that only risk sapping our energy.”

“Our pressing is often misinterpreted. We don’t go looking for a man in every area of ​​the pitch, but rather work on references. In recent games, we’ve tried to be more organised, choosing when to attack and when to wait. We can’t have the same attitude throughout the entire match: we need to understand the moments and always find the right balance.”

“We need to rediscover that hunger that allows us to go beyond individual qualities. We can’t think that individual talent is enough to resolve every situation. We need to be more aggressive in duels, in pressing, and in defensive runs, putting in even more sacrifice.

“This is precisely what struck me about Nicola’s Venezia: the aggressiveness with which he approached tackles and the determination to win the ball back. These are characteristics we must always have, too.”

“Thuram is fine and has no energy issues. He’s a player with great leadership, capable of changing situations on the pitch and making a difference. It’s precisely this responsibility that gives him extra motivation, and I’m confident he’ll have all the energy he needs tomorrow.”

“When you’re forced to come from behind, you inevitably expend a lot more energy. It also happened against Shakhtar, when we managed to win despite being down to ten men. The game we really messed up was the one against Brugge.

“As for Venezia, there are issues we’ve addressed in the dressing room that the players are well aware of. They can’t always be 100%, but mentally they give it their all. Sometimes, though, just playing well isn’t enough: you also have to know how to sacrifice yourself and find other solutions.”

“I have to deal with injuries and find the best combinations through rotation. The situation forces me to carefully evaluate my options: otherwise, I’d have to rely on some young players, but this type of match isn’t the ideal context for launching them.”

“I’m not a coach who prioritizes not conceding goals at all costs. I demand balance, maturity, and the ability to read the different moments of the game from my players. It bothers me when someone tries to exploit the situation or forgets the team principles, especially when it comes to pressing, running, and sprinting: trotting along doesn’t get you anywhere.

“They say a 0-0 draw is a good result, but if you win 1-0, aren’t you still satisfied? At Inter, on the other hand, you always tend to find something wrong.”

“It’s a trick question. I know there are those who are very attached to San Siro, and I am myself, but I’m also in favor of innovation. There are fundamental aspects to consider, such as revenue and the possibility of owning a stadium.

“Nowadays, in football, without financial resources you can’t move forward. So I welcome the changes, even though I admit I have a nostalgic side too. New things can be scary at first, but once you get used to them, they can bring great satisfaction.

“As for the possibility of coaching there in 2031, I prefer not to commit myself. Leading Inter is demanding: judgments often turn into sentences, and it won’t be easy to stay that way for long. Perhaps, if the sporting culture changes, it will be different.

“Who knows, maybe I’ll get to that point with a few less gray hairs and without having to end up in the hospital…”

#2008. Romano: Defender an ‘absolute priority’ for Milan whilst Cardinale continues Endrick ‘obsession’

AC Milan are expected to be busy in January, and Gerry Cardinale’s words today have only fuelled those beliefs.

It was clear to everyone that Milan ended the summer unsatisfied with the squad, especially after the last-minute pursuit of Goncalo Inacio. So, reports emerging about January targets in the days after were not a shock. In fact, they were a welcome statement of intent from the club early on.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Since then, there have been several links to a number of interesting players and with two months to go until January, there will be several more, especially after Cardinale’s statements today. However, there have been a few repeated names that haven’t disappeared, with Inacio’s being one of them.

In the attack, the name of a Brazilian starlet has been thrown around constantly and it seems that it won’t be stopping anytime soon.

Speaking on his YouTube channel tonight at length, Fabrizio Romano looked at a few names linked with the Rossoneri, and MilanNews have relayed his words.

“I’d also add that Cardinale had some very important words about the transfer market, because over the past few months, we’ve often said that Milan did a lot of good things during the summer transfer window, but lacked others. So, Milan needs to strengthen their squad.

“They finished the summer transfer window by looking for central defenders, but then failed to sign him, and in the end, Tomori was reinstated.

“Milan certainly intends to make a move in January. Cardinale confirmed this: ‘ We’ll have to be aggressive in the January transfer window. In the summer, I wasn’t able to do everything I wanted, so I’ll have to strengthen the team, I’ll have to strengthen the bench.’

“It’s clear that when he talks about the bench, he’s talking about rotation because Milan are involved in multiple competitions and need more depth in the squad. This was also evident against Bologna when the team looked very tired in the second half; they’re clearly feeling the strain of playing so many games in a short time.

“Milan will be active in the winter transfer window, so much so that they’ve already started making calls. The central defender is absolutely a priority , so they’ll sign a new defensive reinforcement and have already started contacting him. It’s clear that there are some names that AC Milan already know very well by heart.

“I’ll name one: Gonçalo Inacio is a player Amorim mentioned at the start of last summer’s transfer window. He’s a player AC Milan has been working on, so he’s a name that should always be kept among their favorites. He’s not the only one; AC Milan is also evaluating others.

“I believe that the central defender is one of the things AC Milan wants to do in January, but not the only one, because there’s the possibility of seeing something more. Obviously, this depends on the opportunities and the right names.

“Cardinale’s idea remains to make some additions, but he wants to do it sensibly and with a clear approach. He doesn’t want to sign someone just for the sake of signing them. AC Milan wants to add the right pieces who can be useful today, but also for the future.

“Many of you continue to ask us about the AC Milan striker, because it’s clear that at the moment, even in terms of alternatives, Camarda hasn’t found much space so far and when he did find one he wasn’t seen, so it’s clear that many of you are asking us about the striker.

“I’ll tell you one thing about Endrick: the Brazilian is an absolute obsession of Cardinale; he’s an absolute obsession of AC Milan. In the sense that AC Milan tried to sign him last summer, but found the doors closed.

“Real Madrid didn’t want to release him and that remains Mourinho’s idea even now. The Portuguese continues to repeat in the press and elsewhere: ‘I don’t want Endrick to go, Endrick will be successful here at Real Madrid, we’re counting on Endrick.’

“So Real Madrid, through José Mourinho, is sending signals of absolute permanence. It’s clear that what AC Milan did in the summer was to position themselves; that is, AC Milan knew in August that they couldn’t sign Endrick because Real Madrid had already closed the doors, but they still chose to show their appreciation and to position themselves if a door were to open, whether in January or next summer.

“Right now, Real Madrid have no intention of releasing him. However, Milan will be there when and if a door opens. He won’t be the only one, because Endrick is liked by Roma, Aston Villa and there are also many other teams following him, but this is the scenario today.”

#2007. Frank McAvennie apologises after criticising Celtic star's grief absence

Former Celtic striker Frank McAvennie has apologised after criticising Auston Trusty for missing games after the death of his father.

The defender went public two weeks ago after sadly losing his dad, paying tribute to him online on October 21.

He sat out games against Celta Vigo, Hibs, Dundee United and Falkirk. In the build-up to the latter, manager Martin O'Neill revealed Trusty was heading back to America to "celebrate his dad's life."

McAvennie was critical of how much football the defender was missing, saying on the Let Me Be Frank podcast: "I've got every respect for that, but how long do you want off? Martin (O'Neill) says he's away to celebrate the life of his dad.

"Celebrate the life? You've got football. You're getting paid and we're in trouble. How long is it going to be?

Former Rangers player to stand trial accused of killing woman in road collision £750,000 padel club with four covered courts to open at Ayr United’s stadium

"It's nonsense. My dad was the best man, the only man I looked up to when he died, but you've got to get on with it."

The comments prompted outrage online, with the pundit accused of being insensitive.

That has prompted an apology in the form of an online statement.

McAvennie said: "I’ve seen some of the reaction to comments I made on the podcast about Auston’s absence from football following the death of his father.

"I can understand why people feel my comments were insensitive, and looking back, I should have chosen my words more carefully.

"Everyone deals with grief differently, and I certainly meant no disrespect to Auston or his family. Celtic need the big man back, and that’s what I was clumsily trying to say.

"I wish him and his family all the very best."
