#1995. GdS: Ten-point risk and high ambitions – three keys for Amorim in Milan-Inter

AC Milan are taking on their city rivals Inter this morning, and for Ruben Amorim, there is one key player in each department.

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Milan are entering the derby at a pretty clear disadvantage, currently seven points behind Inter in the standings. Ruben Amorim made it clear yesterday that the Scudetto remains the goal, but if the gap is increased to ten, it will be tough.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s true that Stefano Pioli, in February 2022, also risked going ten points behind until Olivier Giroud turned the game around. The problem is that his successor Goncalo Ramos hasn’t even scored a goal in the league since the end of August.

Furthermore, Cristian Chivu and his Inter have been in very good form lately and will be looking to end their seven-game run without a win in the fixture. It’s going to be a night with a lot of emotions, so let’s see how it will pan out on the pitch.

Mario Gila’s return is absolutely essential for Milan, but it will take more from them to regain solidity at the back. The Rossoneri have conceded four more goals than they did at this point last season, and six in their last two home games.

Switching from Max Allegri’s low block to Amorim’s more proactive style of play has clearly come with a cost. Yet, it’s not like the Rossoneri have been pressing like crazy so far, which is obvious when you compare them with Inter.

The Nerazzurri have a much higher centre of gravity (54.7-48.5 m), they steal more balls in the final third of the pitch (41-28), and they shoot more from offensive recoveries (13-7). Meanwhile, Milan are continuing to concentrate, play vertically and run quickly.

There is also another truth that needs to be highlighted: too many goals have been conceded due to individual errors. Amorim is well aware of this and it might have something to do with the decision to start Sankhoun Diawara on the left, with effectively four centre-backs in the back four.

In midfield, just like with Gila in defence, Amorim can count on another crucial return: Adrien Rabiot, the team’s top scorer along with Alphadjo Cisse (4 goals). For Milan, the midfielders are crucial with their goals.

The midfield is indeed the centre of Milan’s power, where the Ballon d’Or winner Luka Modric reigns supreme and where counterattacks that end up in goal are born. Amorim’s choices in this department weren’t easy.

The most tested on the eve of the match: a 4-3-3 with Musah and Rabiot on either side of Modric, and an attacking trident of Moreira-Ramos-Pulisic.

There were fewer doubts for Chivu who has a tested midfield and, in general, the most coherent team in the league. But that doesn’t mean they don’t have problems. Against Venezia, Inter suffered six dangerous transitions, against Roma there were seven.

In the middle of the pitch, due to the pressure of pressing or laziness in the return, there have often been gaps to exploit. It’s extremely dangerous to leave that space against galloping players like Diego Moreira, Christian Pulisic, and Rabiot.

The Frenchman, who already crippled Inter on the counterattack as a Juventus player (goal and assist for Kostic), could become a key factor in the derby.

Despite conceding one fewer goal than a year ago (10-11), as the pink newspaper continues, Inter appear to be more vulnerable at the back. The centre-backs have dipped in form and the conceded xG is much higher, which Milan will try to exploit.

Ramos is pushing hard to score his third league goal, which he desperately needs despite adding a lot to Milan’s game: 14 balls recovered (Thuram 4, Lautaro 5, Pio 8), 21 lay-offs (Thuram 7, Lautaro 8, Pio 13). All he has to do is find the net.

However, if the player that Milan fear the most is Thuram, then that player is Pulisic for Inter. He decided the penultimate derby, scored in the one that stopped the haemorrhage of six defeats, and also impressed in the Supercoppa Italiana.

He knows the art of hiding between the lines and striking from the attacking midfield, which Inter’s 3-5-2 often struggles to achieve. Perhaps he can celebrate his contract renewal by deciding yet another derby.

#1994. Pocognoli reveals plan to get best from returning McTominay, and from Scotland

As Scott McTominay returns to the Scotland squad, a nation expects. The current Tartan Army talisman was back among the list of names selected by Sebastien Pocognoli yesterday after recovering from a heart issue, and then immediately recovering his goalscoring touch with Napoli.

A disappointing World Cup in the summer, both collectively for Scotland and on a personal level for McTominay, is largely being put down in hindsight to the mild benign arrhythmia that left the midfielder struggling in the sweltering summer heat in the States.

“It was much harder,” McTominay explained after the tournament.

“Two days before the first match I felt unwell and didn’t know whether I’d play or not.

“It was tough to prepare myself mentally. Then, the high temperatures made the situation even more difficult. Looking back, it’s a huge regret of my career.”

Pocognoli, interestingly, has another theory about why McTominay never shone in the way that Scotland had hoped in the World Cup, citing a lack of structure in the team. Regardless, with a corrective ablation procedure safely behind him, McTominay is now back and raring to go, having bagged four goals in seven matches since his return to club football.

But his new manager is hoping that his masterplan can eventually lead to Scotland being a team that consistently carries a threat, rather than one that constantly looks to individuals like McTominay to produce moments of magic.

“It was a big reflection for me over the last weeks, to try and reduce the expectation here on two or three players,” Pocognoli said.

“The first thing is, why? When you have players who have made the difference in most of the games through individual actions or a situation from nowhere, it’s normal that people then expect them to do it in every game.

“But for me, I have to find a way of playing to give Robbo [Andy Robertson] an opportunity to score two or three goals like he nearly did in the last camp. Or to give John McGinn an opportunity to score. The strikers, Billy Gilmour - it’s about giving everyone the chance to shine as a collective.

“That will maybe decrease the expectation of one or two players. That’s something I’d like to try to do.

“It’s normal that people expect Scott to always be the best, if that’s what he’s had to deal with in the past. In the World Cup, it was less because the structure around him was less. But expectation was still big on him, it didn’t matter.

“It’s up to me to have a good structure around him so he can shine, but not only him - all of the players.”

All that being said, Pocognoli is as excited as any member of the Tartan Army to see McTominay back in the dark blue, and to see how he will fit into the system that he has implemented since taking the reins.

“I just want to know him a little bit more, from the personal aspect,” he said.

“We all know his quality. I think he can fit into the way we want to play. So, I’m just excited to see him on the pitch, to see if he can bring something extra in the way we want to play.

“Also, to see how he fits into the group with my own eyes. I want to make a real contact with him because before it has only been on the phone or by video call. I’m looking forward to meeting him.

“He’s a big player. He’s a very complete player on the pitch. Scott is good on the ball, he can infiltrate without the ball. He can press high on the pitch or he can be box-to-box.

“It’s a massive boost for us. My job is to combine his quality with other players around him and I think we will.

“I’ve watched most of his games. His first game back was difficult in the last 20 or 30 minutes which was normal. After that, he started to find his way again. He’s now ready. He’s scored goals playing in a similar shape as us at Scotland.

“It was good to see him higher and lower in that shape on the pitch. Is he hungry? Yeah. He was really disappointed to miss the first camp and was already talking about the next camp.

“At that point we weren’t sure because we had to see his rehabilitation. But he was excited to try his best to reach the November camp and he’s still excited now, which is good.

“He will bring experience, quality, an expectation of goals, a presence in the box - and he’ll bring leadership as part of the captain’s group.

“He has a strong voice. He’s a different character to the others but it’s up to me to produce the game plan for him and the players that allows him to shine, and not him to make the team shine, if you know what I mean? That’s the challenge.”

#1991. Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel dies after on-field collision

Tenerife player Jesus De Miguel has died after an on-field collision in a match on Monday, his club have announced.

The collision occurred as Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono raced from his goal to challenge De Miguel for the ball in stoppage time of a Spanish second-tier game at Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Canary Islands club said in a statement on Tuesday: “Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.

“There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness.

Late on Monday night Tenerife issued a statement confirming De Miguel had been admitted to hospital and was initially described as “stable despite the severity of his condition”.

An update in the early hours of Tuesday morning said his condition had “worsened neurologically”.

Owono was immediately sent off after he charged out of his goal to challenge De Miguel in the centre circle, his knee appearing to connect with the Tenerife player’s head.

Andorra and Tenerife players beckoned on medical staff immediately and appeared visibly upset by De Miguel’s condition.

The match was suspended after the incident.

Opponents Andorra issued a statement on X which read: “With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace.”

LaLiga said in a statement: “We wish to express our deep sadness over the tragic passing of Jesús de Miguel Alameda. We share in the grief of his family, his loved ones, and @CDTOficial during these very difficult times. All our affection and support. Rest in peace.”

Meanwhile, other Spanish clubs posted messages of condolence to Tenerife and De Miguel’s family.

Barcelona said: “From FC Barcelona, we are deeply saddened by the tragic news of the passing of Jesus de Miguel, CD Tenerife player. Our thoughts and support are with his family, friends and loved ones during these difficult times.”

Real Madrid said the club “wishes to express its condolences and affection to his family, his teammates, his club and all his loved ones”.

#1990. Guys like Makhanya and Sterling should feel welcome to speak the truth more often if Rangers are to finally throw off their serial losers tag

Published: 14:15 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 15:19 EDT, 30 October 2026

Olwethu Makhanya is shaping up to be everything Rangers needed in their search for defensive reinforcements in the summer.

A solid presence at the back, a young and hungry talent very much on the up and a leader with real personality.

If it didn’t look so likely that someone will come in before long and offer the Ibrox board the chance to make a healthy profit on the £3million they paid to Philadelphia Union for the 22-year-old, you’d put him down as a nailed-on future captain.

He’s helping set the standards required if Rangers are to overhaul arch-rivals Celtic in the title race and was absolutely spot-on after rescuing an ill-deserved point with a late equaliser at Tynecastle on Wednesday when bemoaning a lack of character at the start of the second half and the fact Hearts worked harder and showed more desire.

It’s the kind of honesty many Ibrox sides of recent years have needed. A public kick up the backside for underperforming team-mates, the footballing equivalent of getting the whip out and a necessary form of assurance for frustrated supporters that there is at least someone inside the dressing room who feels the way they feel, who wants what they want.

It’s why it is to be hoped that manager Derek McInnes’ remarks the morning after were not some attempt to gently slap down the South African.

Defender Olwethu Makhanya questioned the character of this Rangers squad midweek

McInnes, of course, is entitled to his own opinion about the reserves of character within his squad. Maybe he did disagree with Makhanya’s version of events, or his questioning of the side’s resilience.

Alternative viewpoints delivered respectfully are fine. More than fine. They are a sign of a healthy workplace.

It just felt like it was all skirting a little too close to a chastisement of the big centre-back’s comments.

And whether that was the intention or not, being seen to chastise a player whose sentiments are clearly coming from the right place, from a burning desire to make a club with one league crown in 15 years be successful again, is not necessarily the right course of action to take.

It happened, if you remember, with Dujon Sterling back in Philippe Clement’s first season as boss when an April collapse that involved a home draw with Celtic, a 3-2 loss at Ross County and a stalemate at Dundee pretty much killed off hopes of lifting the title.

‘We owe ourselves a performance… because we have been s**t the past three games,’ said Sterling in the aftermath at Dens Park. ‘We are fighting for a title and the way we are playing, it is as if we are not playing for anything. It’s like the season is dead and it is a dead-rubber game.’

It felt like a cry from the heart, a desperate plea to those around him to breathe life into a dying campaign. It was a truth that had to be told.

Clement, meanwhile, was already well on the way to losing the plot at that point, claiming his side were ‘moral winners’ after snatching that draw with Celtic thanks to a late goal and insisting that he was happy his side ‘bossed it’ at Dens.

Criticising Sterling afterwards just made him look even more like he didn’t get it, had lost all sight of what being at Rangers — or any club that has to win at all costs — was about.

‘It’s the words of a player who is disappointed because we lost points and maybe lacks a bit of experience in that way,’ stated the Belgian waffler. ‘That’s things for young players to learn and become better in. It’s more talking out of frustration.’

Manager Derek McInnes disagreed with Makhanya's comments following the Hearts game

That’s the standard response from football persons, of course. The whole business, for some time, has revolved around young players having it battered into them that it’s better to say nothing, to drone on dead-eyed through interviews, bat everything away, put their personality on the bonfire, ‘don’t get too up or too down’.

It’s nonsense, though. McInnes honed his trade in a Nine-In-A-Row Rangers dressing room full of huge characters who built unbreakable bonds while still being able to dig each other out, demand more, be confrontational.

Sure, it happened more behind doors than in the public gaze, but things are different now from the way they were 30 years ago. Social media has changed the landscape so drastically. Fan narratives do drive boardroom decisions and that has arguably been clearer at Ibrox in recent times than anywhere.

There’s a concern still living just under the surface among a large number of Rangers fans that there is an ingrained loser mentality at their club and plenty of evidence to back that up.

Admittedly, the playing staff has changed drastically since then, but it is impossible to forget Billy Dodds reflecting on his time as a first-team coach for interim boss Barry Ferguson and talking about how 70 per cent of signings had been wrong and that the dressing room had a number of weak characters who couldn’t handle adversity.

Even before Danny Rohl left for Red Bull Salzburg last season, he talked about players being ‘too lazy to recover’ in key moments. He also spoke about how some of the squad were ‘very quiet’ when he first took over.

Supporters of Rangers, treated to some amount of failure and in-house claptrap over the last decade or more, need to see evidence that those on the field care the way they do.

The kind of frank analysis delivered by Makhanya — in a calm and considered way, it should be said — need not be the negative so many inside football are programmed to think.

If anything, seeing guys wear their hearts on their sleeve can serve to strengthen the relationship between fans and their favourites in difficult times.

The modern-day audience have had enough of failing players promising to learn lessons and move on. At outfits judged on league titles and facing pressure to win every week, learning lessons is the last thing on the agenda. You really ought to know what needs done by that stage.

Rangers have drawn two of their last three and currently trail leaders Celtic by four points

Punters want to see the real people behind the branding, measure their minerals. And we’re on about more than just those cringeworthy features on club TV where players quiz each other on whether they prefer Jaffa Cakes or KitKats while playing a game of ping-pong. It’s showing a bit of what’s really inside, being properly authentic, that resonates.

In fairness to McInnes, his messaging as Rangers boss has generally been good so far. He didn’t shy away from the paucity of those performances in losing in Europe to Jagiellonia Bialystok and Jablonec.

He hasn’t indulged in deflection. He confronted the speculation that was already beginning to swirl about his future after that Jablonec catastrophe, handled it well and steered the side to safer ground with two excellent back-to-back wins against Celtic.

He has been honest and upfront and entirely understanding of the expectations that rest upon his shoulders.

His team is still guilty of switching off in games. Centre-back Manny Fernandez, although the manager must back him publicly, is the epitome of that.

His players still have to show they can be consistent enough to prevail against a Celtic side that is most definitely there for the taking. They need to keep the pedal to the metal and to deliver 90-minute performances or, at least, maintain control throughout.

It is a squad light on trophies on the CV and with a number of younger players. It is going to need regular reminders as this race plays out.

If Makhanya or Sterling or anyone else want to take it upon themselves to put those reminders out there, it shouldn’t be regarded as a bad thing. And it definitely shouldn’t be discouraged.

#1989. Pocognoli on 'special' Rangers kid Curtis as he explains Penrice call-up

Sebastien Pocognoli has called Findlay Curtis ‘a special kid’, as the Scotland manager backed the Rangers youngster to be a difference-maker for his country.

Curtis has been included in the senior squad for the games against North Macedonia and Switzerland after impressing Pocognoli during his first camp. He shone in training in La Manga before producing a standout performance for Tony Docherty’s under-21 side in their win over Azerbaijan at Rugby Park.

That earned him a recall to the ‘A’ squad for the game against Slovenia at Hampden, and he has retained his place after proving to Pocognoli that he offers the kind of attacking stardust that is all too rare within the Scottish ranks.

“I think he is a player who can make the difference,” Pocognoli said.

“We do not have many in the squad. Sometimes I try to make some targets about the quality we need in the squad, and we need a game changer.

“Sometimes I would like a little bit more speed, but yes, we have a strong midfield and we have good wingers – offensively but also like Andy (Robertson) and (Aaron) Hickey, who are not only defenders, but they can also be good in an offensive way. I believe the front players can sometimes compensate for lack of speed [at the back], this is my belief. That is the way I like to coach.

“I try to target all the positions regarding the specific qualities that the position needs, and I think Findlay is one of those players who can make an impact from the bench, because we have to be honest, it is to come on from the bench right now in the timeline.

“The moment he comes on for Rangers he always brings something special. And we need this.”

Curtis’s teammate, James Penrice, was also called up by Pocognoli for the first time, and the Belgian explained why he felt now was the right juncture to draft the attacking left-back into his squad.

(Image: COLORSPORT/BRUCE WHITE / Shutterstock)

“Josh Doig is out and will need some rest in the next international window,” he said.

“We are proactive for each position – two, three or four names. And James is one we have followed closely, because of his qualities also as a wing back.

“He has this offensive impulse and a good left foot for crossing. So, I think he is a good option.”

#1985. 'Hard but fair': Celtic supremos get grilling from fans as club releases statement on events

Celtic say that their manager Martin O’Neill and members of the club’s hierarchy faced “hard but fair” questioning during a recent Q&A with some supporters.

Chairman Brian Wilson, chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay, O’Neill and other club officials took part in a meeting at Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday night, which was attended by a number of fan groups.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

O’Neill is coming under increasing scrutiny after winning just three of his past ten matches, while the Celtic board have been widely criticised by supporters over the past 18 months. Prominent Celtic groups have called for major shareholder Dermot Desmond to attend this year’s AGM after he was represented by his son Ross in 2025.

A statement from Celtic on the meeting read: “The Celtic manager and board faced ‘hard but fair’ questioning when they took part in a well-attended meeting at Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club last night (Monday).

“Members from Greenock, Port Glasgow, Gourock, Johnny Doyle, Port Glasgow Hibs and Largs clubs were among around 120 Celtic supporters who attended to seek information and voice concerns.

“Martin O’Neill joined chairman Brian Wilson, chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay and other club officials in a two-and-a-half-hour question and answer session.”

On the event, Wilson said: “We were grateful to the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club for hosting this event in a way that allowed everyone to make their points, many of them critical, and to ask searching questions which we did our best to answer.

“We didn’t expect an easy ride and didn’t get one, but the meeting was conducted in a constructive and mutually respectful way and the messages delivered by supporters will be taken on board and learned from.”

O’Neill said: “I asked to attend the meeting because I want to meet supporters as much as I possibly can.

“We have had a few difficult weeks in recent times and I understand our supporters’ frustrations, but my resolve and the commitment of the players is as strong as ever to continue to bring success and progress to the club as we have done before.”

Michael Nicholson said: “I thank the committee and members of the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club for inviting us to their club, and all supporters attending for the opportunity to discuss their concerns and the issues that mean so much to us all. Everyone in the room wants the best for Celtic and that was evident.

“We are grateful for supporters’ input and look forward to continuing to meet with supporters as we work on improving communication and engagement in the weeks and months ahead.”

Celtic confirmed that “issues raised by supporters included recruitment, transfer policy, communications, and the club’s ambitions and strategy”. They plan to release further details in due course on new engagement initiatives.

The event in Greenock follows similar sessions held across recent months with the Affiliation of Registered CSCs in Glasgow and the Association of Irish Celtic Supporters' Clubs in Cork. The club says it plans to hold more in the coming weeks.

Celtic have two matches ahead of the next international break - both at home. They play Besiktas in the Europa League on Thursday before the visit of Kilmarnock in the Premiership on Sunday.

#1984. 'We must improve': Pocognoli spells out where Scotland have to up their game

Sebastien Pocognoli has told his Scotland players that their grace period is over following his maiden camp, and that they have to produce better displays and results when they take on North Macedonia and Switzerland to round off their Nations League group campaign.

Pocognoli was willing to give his men a little leeway in the condensed four-game sequence that kicked off his reign as manager, given that the squad included many new faces and the players were getting used to the preferred system and demands of their new head coach.

Scotland produced a creditable display, particularly in the second half, as they were unfortunate to be held to a goalless draw during Pocognoli’s first game in charge away to Slovenia, but they followed that up with a 3-0 loss to Switzerland at Hampden after Jack Hendry’s early red card.

They bounced back to beat North Macedonia 2-0 in Skopje, but rounded off the opening round of group fixtures with a disappointing 2-1 defeat to the Slovenians at Hampden.

That has left the Scots needing to win both of their remaining matches to have a realistic chance of qualifying for the playoffs for League A in March, and Pocognoli - speaking as he announced his latest squad - has left his players in no doubt over what he expects from them.

“The first camp was to get to know each other. I saw things in training and in the games, we produced some very good moments. We created a lot of chances, maybe more than in previous years against those types of opponents.

“But the next step is to score more goals and clean up the mistakes we made. Because we conceded goals from nothing. We must try to be consistent in the way we want to play.

“We have a different system, different players and different approach to the game. I’m sure we can shine in that way but we need to make the standard higher and win games. That’s the idea for the next camp.

“We need to improve but every country who started with a new coach in September would say the same. Many players in the first camp took it as a new experience with a new style of play and system.

“That needs a little bit of time, but it doesn’t mean we can’t now ask for more and reach the level we want.

“We now have Che Adams back, Scott (McTominay) back, Kieran Tierney and we’re still missing Kenny McLean.

“These players bring stability. I’m pleased with this selection because we feel we have a good mix.”

#1983. Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Arsenal: Kepa (Meslier 46); White (Julienne 78), Mosquera (Ogunnaike 78), Gabriel (Salmon 60), Calafiori (Hincapié 60); Lewis-Skelly (Vieira 78), Havertz (O’Neill 78), Odegaard (Nwaneri 33); Dowman (Ibrahim 78), Gyokeres (Jesus 78), Tzolis (Martinielli 78). Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o

The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

The German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Checking in for the Emirates Cup 🛬 pic.twitter.com/mQ1eAESKHY

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#1982. Rangers star savours maiden Scotland call-up after candid admission over international hopes

James Penrice has described his first Scotland call-up as an “incredibly proud” moment, admitting that representing his country was not an achievement he had envisaged during the early years of his career.

The Rangers defender was left stunned after learning of his inclusion in Sebastien Pocognoli’s latest squad for the upcoming Nations League double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland only minutes before heading out for training.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The unexpected confirmation that left him struggling to comprehend the personal significance of the milestone, with the versatile 27-year-old rewarded for a string of consistent performances since arriving at Ibrox on a season-long loan from Greek side AEK Athens.

Returning to Scottish football in the summer, the former Partick Thistle, Livingston and Hearts star has been an integral part of Rangers progress under Derek McInnes, making 14 appearances and scoring on his debut against St Mirren. He also provided a crucial assist in last Saturday’s Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Aberdeen.

And Penrice was quick to acknowledge the contribution of his teammates, recognising the dressing room influence in helping him reach a position where international selection became a distinct possibility.

“I found out five minutes before I came out [for training] and just went ‘oh my god unreal’,” Penrice told Rangers TV. “Incredibly proud. I have waited a wee while, but I knew coming back to Scotland, coming to Rangers, it would help my cause. So it's credit to the boys in there as well. They've helped me incredibly and I'm just buzzing.”

Penrice revealed that, earlier in his career, he had not considered representing Scotland a realistic prospect. His selection is an endorsement of the progress made since joining Rangers, where he has established himself as a first-team regular.

He confessed: “It's a weird feeling because I don't ever think going through the early part of my career that I would ever be called up. But it's happened now so I'm just delighted.

“It's an incredibly proud moment for me and my family. They will be buzzing, my phone will probably be going off, it's nuts. I'll have hundreds of missed calls now from my mum asking why I never told her! But I'm just buzzing.”

Penrice will now look ahead to the prospect of making his national team debut when Scotland host League B1 bottom side North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday, 13 November before travelling to St Gallen to face group leaders Switzerland three days later.

#1981. Kaka discusses Hall of Fame induction, tonight’s derby and the Milan project

AC Milan legend Ricky Kaka will be inducted into the Rossoneri’s Hall of Fame ahead of tonight’s derby, which he believes is anyone’s game.

As confirmed in the last few days, after inducting the likes of Marco van Basten, Filippo Inzaghi, Andriy Shevchenko and more, it’s now time for Kaka. The Brazilian is one of the greatest players to have even worn the red and black shirt, scoring 104 goals and assisting another 81 in  307 games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The ceremony will take place before tonight’s derby clash between AC Milan and Inter, which is a very important game for the Rossoneri. A loss would leave them 10 points behind the top, so hopefully Kaka’s presence and celebration can act as fuel for the team.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport, Kaka shared his thoughts on the Hall of Fame, his memories of the derby and what will be needed from Milan tonight. He also commented on the Rossoneri’s project as a whole, stating that time is needed.

“I’m getting ready. My family will be there. My wife, daughters, my brother, and many friends. I also wanted to thank the fans who voted. I can imagine the atmosphere. It’ll be exciting.”

What do you remember about your first derby?

“A header from a cross by Rino Gattuso. It was also my first goal for AC Milan. Fantastic. The city experiences this match in a special way; among my memories, I’d logically put the Champions League derby in the quarterfinals. The comeback from 3-2 was also fantastic.”

You mentioned Gattuso, who as a coach, after changing many clubs, is doing well with Lazio…

“Being a coach is a tough job. Rino is doing really well now. He has a very special character, he’s someone who always wants to win, and I’m happy he’s able to express himself to the fullest. He’s a great friend, I always cheer for my friends and I’m very happy.”

“Let’s say no, for now. The pressure of the coaching job isn’t for me. But we can talk about it again in a couple of years.”

Speaking of friends, what do you think of the Paolo Maldini and Leonardo affair with the national team?

“I’m amazed at how little time passed before their resignations. It’s difficult to judge from afar, but I think it would have been a good thing for Italian football to have such competent people at the helm. I hope Italy regains its place soon.

“There are so many things to manage, from youth development onwards. I often meet with former players who live in Italy and ask questions. Italy at the World Cup is a good thing for football as a whole.

“Plus, my connection to Italy is incredibly strong; I try to return at least once a year, and more if I can. In recent years, we’ve visited the art cities, Florence, Venice, but also the lakes, Capri, and the sea. And Sardinia is wonderful.”

Let’s get back to football. Were you surprised by Milan’s collapse last season?

“I think all the fans expected us to qualify for the Champions League. Was it a physical or mental decline? Maybe a bit of everything. When confidence starts to wane, everything changes. Now, however, we must aim to return to the best of Europe. The Champions League is special.”

“It’s under construction. For seven years, it was Leao’s Milan, a great player on whom a lot of trust was placed. Now it’s different. The team is a collective with new faces and two masters: Modric remains the brains, then there’s Rabiot. And Ramos is a goalscorer.

“It will take some time to put it together. The important thing is to always aim high, even in the Europa League.”

What kind of relationship did you have with the Inter fans?

“A relationship of great respect. Inter helped me grow a lot because I’ve always looked at competition as something that helps me grow, so I saw the matches against Inter or Juventus as important matches, and I had to prepare well because the team was very strong, the opponents were very strong.

“But with the Brazilians of my time, Maicon, Julio, and the others, there was friendship. And also with the Argentines: many others were and remain friends, like Materazzi.”

How do you see Inter on this evening, which will be special for you?

“They are still doing well after last season. They’re a team to beat, but we Milan fans can do it already in this derby. Chivu as a coach was a nice surprise; Inter didn’t play well at the start, but then they corrected their position. But I wouldn’t say the Scudetto is a one-man showdown like you might think in Italy.

“I see the game as open and the road to the title even more so. The season is long, but Milan must aim to be consistent. So far they’ve done better in the league than in Europe, there will be moments of decline in the other teams and we’ll have to take advantage of them.”

“Not great at the World Cup, but it takes a bit of time. The national team is different from a club where you’re there every day evaluating players. Carlo was only able to work with the group for a year.

“For the next World Cup, it will be five years of preparation, five years with these guys, learning the culture of the country, knowing a little about what it’s like to play in the World Cup with Brazil. So I have a lot of confidence.”

You won the Ballon d’Or in 2007 and no one had any reason to argue. This time they gave it to Harry Kane, and Lamine Yamal doesn’t seem to have taken it too well. Your opinion?

“The right choice. Harry Kane has done very well, he was a key player with Bayern Munich and won a lot. Mbappé didn’t win much with Real Madrid, Lamine had success with Barça but wasn’t as decisive as expected. Their time will come, but I think the choice based on their performance this season is acceptable.”

Let’s get back to the derby. Who are the key players?

“Modric and Rabiot are masters, they manage and set the pace. Pulisic enchants me with his intelligence in the game, Goncalo is a goalscorer. As for Inter, what can I say? They are a consistent, solid team and have many dangerous players.”

Do you have any favourite places in Milan?

“I like walking downtown, I like Brera, I love the hidden corners. Drinking coffee, talking to people.”

#1979. 'We're not in Disneyland!': Mikel Arteta fires warning at Arsenal wonderboy Max Dowman, 16, after red card - and says it's not his first offence... as he admits Fleetwood loss left him 'p***ed off'

Published: 10:24 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 15:26 EDT, 30 October 2026

Mikel Arteta has told 16-year-old Max Dowman 'we are not in Disneyland' as he insists his age does not give him a free pass following his red card against Fleetwood.

Dowman was sent off in the 86th minute of Arsenal's shock Carabao Cup defeat by Fleetwood on Tuesday after kicking out in retaliation to a challenge by Harrison Neal.

It was the second time he has been sent off this this month, having also seen red while representing England's Under-19s.

After the club's appeal was rejected by the FA, Dowman will now miss Arsenal's Premier League matches against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle.

As the teenager left the field, manager Mikel Arteta gave him a scathing look and uttered a few words to the attacker, understood to be: 'Get to the changing room, Max.'

And on Friday he suggested Dowman should have kept his cool under provocation.

Arsenal star Max Dowman (second from right) looks shocked after the referee shows him a red card at Fleetwood Town

Manager Mikel Arteta has words with the distraught youngster as he leaves the field

Arteta said: ‘I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction. But you have to understand the context, the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

‘You want to always have the best reaction, the beautiful one. But do you want to see the reaction of his team-mates when they have to play with the 10 men, you want to see that? What do you expect?

‘I don't know. Or the England (Under 16) ones, they are his age, 16, the same. What is their reaction?

‘Whether it’s right or wrong, that's the reaction. And the reaction when I don't win, you know what is? I’m p***** off big time.

‘We have to be ready for that, this is the environment and this is the reality. Otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League at this level.

‘We look after him so much that you cannot imagine, and at the same time we are going to be demanding that anybody continues to earn the right to play. Otherwise what are the rest of the boys going to tell me? It needs to be fair, that's all.’

He further explained that his touchline reaction was borne out of frustration having told Dowman to not react to such a scenario before the game.

‘I thought we discussed that before the game,’ the Spaniard said. ‘It was related to what could happen. Not only the red, but the 10 seconds before, the way he (Dowman) comes to receive the ball, what kind of ball that is, and after that if he gets tackled, what happens next. Exactly that.’

Arteta revealed he had spoken with Dowman about the incident. 'I had a talk with him yesterday,' he said. 'No issue at all. I've done it, so I try to prevent that.

'That's why I'm so protective of these things, and especially with young players, because we have made those mistakes. And you know how much you can get punished and how much it can change what happens next.'

On the FA’s decision to reject the Gunners’ red card appeal, he said: ‘Very disappointed, to be fair. Especially with the reckless tackles that he received, and then his reaction is minimal in relation to the action.

‘(We’re) disappointed that it's not been overturned after looking at the action back.

‘We have put every argument on the table to make a case for it. Not only the action, but when you look back at it in slow motion, the previous action and Max's action, it's clear that obviously we have a very different opinion.

‘And on top of that, I think you have to read the context of the player, the age.’

The severity of the challenge is also an issue for Arteta. ‘It could have been really bad, yeah,’ he said. ‘And we are lucky today that he hasn't had a broken foot. That's clear.’

#1978. Scotland lay out Scott McTominay plans as Sebastien Pocognoli awaits first sight of talisman

Scotland manager Sebastien Pocognoli intends to try to make “a good connection” with Scott McTominay after naming the Napoli midfielder in his squad for the first time.

Pocognoli is relieved the midfielder, who underwent a small heart procedure earlier this season, has returned to the fold.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Belgian is looking forward to meeting McTominay in the flesh. It’s already tempting to suggest that Pocognoli is pinning his hopes on the player following an underwhelming start to his time as manager.

The Belgian succeeded Steve Clarke in August. Scotland have since won just one of their first four Nations League games and are now sitting third in Group B1, behind Switzerland and Slovenia.

They require a minimum of four points against North Macedonia at Hampden next Friday and then away to Switzerland three days later to have any chance of finishing second and featuring in the play-offs.

The latter game is two days before the first anniversary of Scotland’s titanic 4-2 win over Denmark that secured a place at this summer’s World Cup. McTominay got that famous night underway with an overhead kick after just three minutes.

He has already scored twice for Napoli since returning to the side last month. Pocognoli has only spoken to McTominay online so far and is looking forward to sitting down with him in person as he looks to establish a connection with Scotland’s most valuable player.

He stressed that it is up to him as manager to find a way to ensure the other players give McTominay the chance to excel rather than simply waiting for the Italy-based star to spark the team. It will be interesting to see who he replaces. John McGinn, Lewis Ferguson and Billy Gilmour were the middle three in the last outing against Slovenia, which Scotland lost 2-1. Ryan Christie played just behind Oli McBurnie in attack.

“He (McTominay) will bring experience, quality, an expectation of goals, a presence in the box - and he’ll bring leadership as part of the captain’s group,” said Pocognoli.

“He has a strong voice. He’s a different character to the others, everyone is different. But it’s up to me to make sure the game plan for him and the players allows him to shine. And it’s not just on him to make the team shine, if you know what I mean? That’s the challenge.”

“I just want to know him a little bit more, from the personal aspect,” he added. “We all know his quality. I think he can fit into the way we want to play.

“So I’m just excited to see him on the pitch, to see if he can bring something extra in the way we want to play.

“Also, to see how he fits into the group with my own eyes. I want to make a real contact with him because before it has only been on the phone or by video call. I’m looking forward to meeting him.”

Pocognoli, who has also brought striker Che Adams back into the squad after injury, stressed that McTominay remains committed to the Scotland cause. The 29-year-old was heavily criticised in the summer following a perceived poor showing in the World Cup, although this was before the problem with his heart came to light.

“He was really disappointed to miss the first camp and was already talking about the next camp,” said Pocognoli, recalling his first conversations with the player.

“At that point we weren’t sure because we had to see his rehabilitation. But he was excited to try his best to reach the November camp and he’s still excited now, which is good.”

#1977. Sebastien Pocognoli's Scotland report card has stark message as Euro 2028 qualification warning issued

Just a few days after the last international window concluded with a deeply disappointing 2-1 defeat to Slovenia, Sebastien Pocognoli was back at Hampden.

Nothing too surprising about that, really. After all, he is the Scotland manager. He is, though, based in Belgium and he admitted he needed some time back in his homeland with his family to "refuel" after a challenging and sometimes fraught opening period in charge.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

But he was back in Scotland soon enough to attend a review of his first fixtures in charge, which saw his team take just four Nations League points from a possible 12 against Slovenia (twice), North Macedonia and Switzerland. Although it would have been good to be a fly on the wall on Hampden’s sixth floor as Pocognoli endured this assessment exercise, it’s easy to imagine the gist of the early report card: Must do better.

Pocognoli himself recognises this. “We need to improve,” he said on Monday at the national stadium after naming his second squad. “The first camp was to get to know each other.

“I saw things in training and in the games we produced some very good moments. We created a lot of chances, maybe more than in previous years against those types of opponents. But the next step is to score more goals and clean up the mistakes we made because we conceded goals from nothing. We must try to be consistent in the way we want to play.

“We need to improve but then every country who started with a new coach in September would say the same. Many players in the first camp took it as a new experience with a new style of play and system. That needs a little bit of time but it doesn’t mean we can’t now ask for more and reach the level we want.”

Pocognoli will be handed more time whatever happens in the next two games against North Macedonia and Switzerland. Perhaps the most important date left this year is 6 December, when the draw for Euro 2028 takes place in Belfast. Despite a potentially damaging assumption that Scotland have already qualified as one of the hosts, there’s still work to be done. “We are not qualified,” stressed the Belgian. “We need to qualify. The best way is to qualify from our group.”

He mentioned the need to “stimulate” a winning habit as quickly as possible so that when and if qualification is secured, reaching the knockout stage at a major finals – the final frontier as far as Scotland are concerned – is easier to achieve.

This will go down well with the Hampden top brass. While those first four games will have been robustly scrutinised, it’s only fair Pocognoli’s bosses apply some context to their findings beyond the fact that the heavy defeat against Switzerland was defined by an early red card for Jack Hendry. Pocognoli has barely had time to get his loafers under the desk.

He was also badly served by circumstances. On top of the absent Scott McTominay, recovering following a minor heart procedure, Kieran Tierney and Che Adams were unavailable due to injury. Pocognoli has called up all three for the upcoming games, in the process adding 30 goals to a squad that looked severely short in this department last time out.

Then there was the understandable pomp and ceremony involved in Andy Robertson reaching 100 caps. It meant an early invite back for Steve Clarke, who will have found it excruciating to be perceived as peering over Pocognoli’s shoulder as Scotland were outplayed on their own turf by Slovenia. It was an awkward night, off the pitch as well as on it.

Clarke is actually back in Glasgow next week as a guest of honour at the Street Soccer gala dinner. It will be surprising if he decides to attend Scotland’s home match against North Macedonia two days later. He knows Pocognoli needs space and time to continue trying to put his own mark on the role.

“It was a tough camp,” Pocognoli acknowledged, with reference to those first post-Clarke games. “It was an intense camp. I really liked it. But in terms of intensity…..four games, and I needed to get to know everybody – like 50, 60 new faces. Plus all you (journalists) - 70! It was intense.

“I needed to rest a little bit and refuel after the camp. After one week I was already back here for the review of the camp with the staff and the board and now I am here all this week to prepare for the next camp.”

The Belgian needs to familiarise himself with one more new face: on-loan Rangers player James Penrice, who has been recruited to replace the injured Josh Doig. The squad looks infinitely stronger than last time around thanks chiefly to the inclusion of McTominay and also Adams, still reckoned by many observers – this writer included - to be Scotland’s best striker. The Torino forward's presence takes some of the pressure off Oli McBurnie, who is still struggling to score his first Scotland goal but has struck in his last two appearances for Hull City.

Surprisingly, Aaron Hickey has not started for Brentford since before the last international window. On the upside, Ben Gannon-Doak has seen more action than he is used to in a club context - just as Pocognoli predicted when speaking prior to the last Slovenia game.

The manager was addressing the likely negative impact another period of limited playing time for his club would have on the youngster, who started two of Scotland’s four games in the last window. Pocognoli ventured that, because of Bournemouth’s European commitments, Gannon-Doak will be required to play a more meaningful part as the season progresses, and so it has proved.

The 20-year-old winger was even man of the match in the recent 3-0 Europa League win over AC Milan. Many pointed to this result as underlining football’s new world order. Scotland, meanwhile, have dropped one place to 43 in the international rankings since they last played. They need to start going back up the way without delay.

Are emotions ramping up ahead of the game?

“Tonight was a really amazing event. We had legends of AC Milan who know how to win, and that means so much to me, that they came back and bought into what we do. We are bringing this passion and love of winning back.

#1974. Ian Hart: Neutrals want Brighton and Hove Albion to beat Arsenal and Manchester City to the Premier League title

I wasn’t at the Etihad on Saturday, although if the grandchildren ever ask me where I was on the day of this landmark win, I can tell them I watched every exciting, and at times nail-biting, 90 or so minutes at Muddy’s Irish Bar in the basement of the Orchard Hotel, Singapore!

And it was while I enjoyed Albion’s landmark win that another facet of this perhaps never-to-be-forgotten season hit me. Watching football abroad can sometimes be an experience in itself. More often than not you watch it in the company of football fans who follow other teams, and Saturday was no exception.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

With league leaders Arsenal almost becoming ‘The Unwatchables’ and their nearest challengers Manchester City effectively sitting on domestic football’s ‘death row’, it’s Brighton in third place who are attracting the attention of many neutrals in the EPL.

While we, as an Albion fanbase, have to clearly temper our expectations, I sat with a Villa and Forest fan in Muddy’s – both not only want Brighton to win the league, but hope with City knocked out of the equation with their eventual punishment and an Arsenal dip in form, the Seagulls can emulate Leicester City and actually lift the title.

Late night Guinness Goggles? Almost certainly, but with the top two attracting almost nationwide disdain among many football fans, and the apparent popularity of the Albion among the wider football community, it’s clearly going to be an ongoing trait.

I did see the Villa fan at the airport a day later, and although now stone cold sober he reiterated his belief in the Albion and their potential ambitions.

But not for the first time, nor for the last, for me it’s all about managing expectation. Cliche alert, but every game truly is a cup final – and this week is no different with a Conference fixture in Madrid against Getafe on Thursday before the Amex visit of another EPL surprise package Brentford on Sunday.

Back to back victories would enhance Albion’s progress in both competitions, yet on the flip side negative results in either would hamper the aforementioned progress and aid the harbingers of doom with their ‘Thursday-Sunday’ theories.

Joni Mitchell famously sang ‘You don’t know what you’ve got ’til it’s gone’ and so for the Albion faithful let’s just enjoy the ride. There will obviously be blips but Fabian seems to be consistently getting a tune we are all currently enjoying in the main with his squad.

And with Kaoru Mitoma back in the first team mix very soon, that will be like a mid-season marquee signing.

Never forget there’s always someone worse off, be it in life or in football. This could yet prove to be a groundbreaking season for the Seagulls, with a long-awaited major trophy, or even, daring to dream, Champions League qualification.

But with events at the other end of the table, we could end up losing our much coveted ‘M23 Derby’ as Crystal Palace seem destined for a long hard winter with the distinct possibility of relegation next May.

And given the competitive nature of the Championship that may mean us missing out on the much anticipated fixture for at least a couple of years.

#1973. O'Neill hits out at critics as Celtic boss issues surprising response to McGregor's midweek comments

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 15:03 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 15:30 EDT, 30 October 2026

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill has claimed some of the club’s critics are only seeking to cause division within the camp.

On the back of a 2-2 draw with Dundee United earlier this week, Celtic skipper Callum McGregor claimed they are playing like a basketball team who lack control in matches.

McGregor also appeared to question the fact that Celtic started the match effectively with three strikers across the frontline in Kasper Hogh, Camilo Duran and Callum Osmand.

‘It’s not really having a nailed-on profile for each of the positions,’ said McGregor. ‘The players behave like a winger, or they behave like a striker.

‘You can get away with it for a few games but if it’s a striker playing as a winger, you are going to get that behaviour a lot of the time.

‘You’ve got enough quality so you can score goals and get away with it. But we have to try to get the team functioning the way it should.

O'Neill is satisfied with Celtic's start to the season despite criticism over performances

‘Then that will alleviate all the other problems that we are encountering, where it becomes a bit like basketball, you lose control and spend the next 15 minutes trying to get possession back.’

At half-time in the game against United at Parkhead, O’Neill took Hogh off and reverted to a more traditional system with Jota and Haissem Hassan coming on as wingers to replace the misfiring Dane and Osmand.

Celtic eventually fought back to claim a point, but McGregor’s comments became the subject of much scrutiny.

It is not the first time a senior player has spoken out this season, with Cameron Carter-Vickers claiming that Celtic’s style of play was ‘random’ after the Old Firm defeats to Rangers.

O’Neill insists he actually agrees with McGregor’s comments — but has vowed to find a solution at the top end of the pitch.

The veteran boss also appeared to snipe back at some of the critics who have claimed that there is unrest among the squad.

‘I’ve said this to you before, I totally agree that Osmand is actually really a centre-forward,’ said O’Neill when asked about McGregor’s verdict.

‘I’ve said it at the press conference, that he is essentially a centre-forward who probably would play off somebody strong alongside him.

‘I'm not so sure that he could lead the line on his own. And that Duran is really a centre-forward.

‘So the players are getting to know each other. It’s really as simple as that. So I’m in total agreement with Callum. We’ll sort it out.

The manager admits that the likes of Camilo Duran are currently being played out of position

‘We seem to be doing okay domestically, trying to sort it out.

‘There’s a few players that haven’t had a chance. [Jordan] Lotomba hasn’t had a chance yet to play. There’ll be moments, absolutely.

‘Young [Joel] Van Den Berg has trained today. So over the course of the next number of weeks, between now and Christmas, I think everybody will be on the field of play.

‘And then it’s a matter of establishing right positions as much as possible.

‘Players have played out of position before. I don’t know whether it was a big issue when young Osmand came on in the Benfica game and set us alight.

‘I come in here [to the press conference] every single week and I’m most of the time pretty buoyed by things.

‘Don’t try and throw a lot of divides in. At the end of the day, we’re doing fine.

‘A lot of lads here didn’t even do pre-season with us. A number of players came in quite late on, so it will take time for us.

‘So we need to hang in there, and at this minute I think we’re hanging in.’

With Rangers playing Aberdeen in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup, Celtic travel to Falkirk tomorrow knowing that a victory would send them seven points clear of their Old Firm rivals.

O'Neill added: ‘I think we’ve done fine, we’re leading the league with a four-point gap at this minute, which is nothing at all at this stage of the season.

‘We fought back and retrieved those kind of leads on a couple of occasions last season.

‘We’ll try and get a result or two in European football which would be nice, but domestically we’ve been fine.

‘Falkirk had a bit of a stodgy start, but they are flying now, so we know it’ll be a difficult game for us.’

#1972. Bridges left with work to do after Maldon defeat

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Three Bridges suffered another damaging defeat on Saturday afternoon, going down 3–1 away to Maldon & Tiptree in the Isthmian Premier League, further widening the gap between themselves and safety in the relegation zone.

After an even opening, Maldon & Tiptree gradually began to take control of proceedings, finding plenty of joy down their right-hand side in particular.

The hosts took the lead in the 19th minute when Olukolu's cross found Akanbi at the back post. Having beaten Ferreira far too easily, Olukolu delivered an inviting ball into the box, which Akanbi converted with an acrobatic overhead kick to put the hosts ahead.

Noel Leighton almost provided an immediate response for Three Bridges, but his effort was saved by the Maldon & Tiptree goalkeeper. That proved to be one of the few positive moments for the visitors in a first half that quickly became increasingly one-sided.

Maldon & Tiptree continued to threaten, creating numerous opportunities and forcing Sam Roberts into an outstanding save to prevent the deficit from increasing.

However, the goalkeeper could only delay the inevitable. In the 38th minute, the hosts doubled their advantage after Bridges' defence once again failed to deal with a cross into the penalty area. Bennett was allowed far too much room to get his effort away, firing an unstoppable finish into the top corner to make it 2–0.

Things went from bad to worse in first-half stoppage time when a low cross into the box caught the Bridges defence sleeping once again. Ferreira was caught completely unaware, allowing Olukolu to apply the finishing touch and make it 3–0.

It was a poor first-half display from Three Bridges, who had been second best in almost every department and went into the break with the game effectively beyond their reach.

With the hosts taking their foot off the gas after the restart, Bridges began to grow into the game and showed some signs of life. A flicker of hope arrived in the 56th minute when Leighton took a quick free-kick and found Charlie Bennett inside the penalty area, with the forward making no mistake from close range to reduce the deficit to 3–1.

However, any hopes of a comeback were completely extinguished ten minutes later when Ferreira brought down Olukolu in what the referee deemed to be a dangerous position. The defender was shown a straight red card in the 66th minute, bringing a miserable afternoon to an end. From a Three Bridges perspective, it appeared a particularly harsh decision.

There was little of note for the remainder of the contest until the 90th minute, when Leighton received a second yellow card for dissent. To be fair, the dismissal had been coming for some time, with the captain spending much of the previous 15 minutes arguing with the officials and seemingly talking himself into an early shower.

The match eventually finished 3–1, with Maldon & Tiptree deserved winners on the day.

For Three Bridges, however, the result leaves plenty to think about. More concerning than the defeat itself was the manner of the performance, particularly the lack of urgency shown during the opening 45 minutes.

There is still a long way to go, with plenty of games left to play, but performances like this will do little to convince anyone that Bridges have what it takes to turn their season around.

Three Bridges starting XI: Roberts, Irving, Neathey, Malone, Ferreira, Spicer, Adeiynka, Bennett, Velvick, Richards, Leighton (C).

Three Bridges return to Jubilee Field next Saturday, 7 November, when they host Brentwood in the Isthmian Premier League. Kick-off is at 15:00.
